issues.title: How reliable are LLMs at mapping malware/threat behavior to MITRE ATT&CK techniques (TTP mapping)?
open_questions: REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 31 -- the original form ('Does the CTI-ATE F1 ceiling of 0.64 generalize to the newer/larger models evaluated in CyberSOCEval (src-0005, 2025-era)?') was UNANSWERABLE AS POSED and must not be reinstated: cycle 26 established that src-0005 REPORTS NO ATT&CK METRIC AT ALL, so it can never be the comparand. WHAT IS GENUINELY OPEN: no evaluation in this base measures ATT&CK technique extraction on 2026-era frontier models. The two post-2024 measurements that exist are src-0007's (Mar 2026) on GPT-4o and o3-mini, and both land far BELOW src-0002's 0.6388 rather than above it (0.2787/0.2270 and 0.3480/0.1759 precision/recall) -- so there is no evidence of the ceiling rising with model generation, and some evidence against, but the two numbers are not commensurable and cycle 31 established that they are produced under two RADICALLY DIFFERENT and now-known-to-differ scoring rules (see candidate 3). The question a future cycle should actually ask is: does any published evaluation score a 2026-era frontier model on ATT&CK technique extraction under a STATED correctness rule? === CYCLE-45 UPDATE (T2): PARTIALLY ADVANCED BY src-0021, AND IT CARRIES A TRAP THAT WOULD REPRODUCE ctr-0001's DEFECT IF WALKED INTO. === THE ADVANCE, on both limbs of the question as posed. FRONTIER MODELS: src-0021 (TTPrint) evaluates, verbatim, 'GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Open-source models include Qwen 3 235B and DeepSeek v3.2' -- the first 2026-era frontier backbones in this base to be scored on ATT&CK technique extraction. STATED RULE: it states its metric AGGREGATION verbatim -- 'We evaluate at the document level by aggregating predictions across the full report and comparing the resulting technique set to the ground truth. Final scores are macro-averages over all documents: F1bar = 1/|D| sum_{d in D} F1_d' -- and its LABEL GRANULARITY verbatim, from the prompt, 'Output only ATT&CK technique IDs in parent-technique format: TXXXX, no child technique like TXXXX.XXX'. BUT THE ITEM-LEVEL TP/FP/FN ALGEBRA IS NOT PRINTED: a targeted fetch for the set-intersection formula reported that the paper only references macro-averaged F1 computed per document without showing the underlying precision/recall calculation. So the correctness rule is RECOVERABLE ONLY AS AN INFERENCE from two stated facts (a per-document set comparison over parent-level IDs), NOT as a quoted rule, and this question's literal demand for a STATED correctness rule is therefore ADVANCED BUT NOT SATISFIED. THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS PARAGRAPH EXISTS: src-0021's headline 76.48% and 87.39% macro-F1 ARE SCORES FOR THE TTPrint SCAFFOLD, NOT BARE-LLM SCORES. TTPrint is a multi-stage system -- divergent decomposition into atomic behaviours, a deterministic span-localization stage, then a convergent verification stage retaining 'only candidates supported by both the localized evidence and the authoritative MITRE definition'. SETTING 76.48 OR 87.39 AGAINST src-0002's 0.6388 OR src-0007's 0.2787 REPRODUCES EXACTLY THE SYSTEM-VERSUS-MODEL CONFOUND THAT ctr-0001 WAS OPENED ABOUT for src-0003's LANCE. NO T3 AND NO T4 MAY MAKE THAT COMPARISON. What a model-level comparand requires is the paper's PER-BACKBONE BARE BASELINES, and THOSE WERE NOT CAPTURED AT CYCLE 43 -- capturing that multi-backbone table is the single highest-value unfinished fetch on this source (carry-forward [80]). TWO FURTHER LIMITS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH ANY USE: TTPrint-Bench is an AUTHOR-BUILT BENCHMARK TOPPED BY ITS OWN AUTHORS' SYSTEM and TRAM-Clean is those same authors' cleaning of someone else's benchmark, so the 'outperforming the leading baseline by 63.5%' figure inherits that; and the source is an UNREVIEWED v1 PREPRINT (Comments 'Preprint', no journal reference). NOTE FINALLY THAT src-0020 DOES NOT ADVANCE THIS QUESTION AT ALL: its seven models are open-source only (DeepSeek-V2.5, GPT-OSS 120B and 20B, Llama 3.1 Instruct 70B and 8B, Gemma 3 27B and 12B), and its best micro-F1 of 0.22 MUST NOT be read as evidence about 2026-era frontier capability. === CYCLE-46 UPDATE (T3): THE TRAP IS NOW DISARMED AND THE FIRST LIMB IS ANSWERED. THE QUESTION IS NO LONGER 'IS THERE A FRONTIER BARE-MODEL NUMBER' -- THERE IS. === Cycle 46 captured src-0021's Table 1 and Table 2 whole (carry-forward [80], DISCHARGED; see this issue's candidate 4 and src-0021 key_claims[3]). WHAT THAT SETTLED. src-0021's Table 1 contains TWO BARE, DIRECTLY-PROMPTED GPT-4o ROWS, labelled as such by the paper verbatim -- 'For LLM-based approaches, we include two direct prompting baselines: One-Shot, which classifies each sentence with one in-context example, and CoT, which adds explicit chain-of-thought reasoning to the same prompt.' -- scoring, on TTPrint-Bench, 62.99/52.80/44.23 and 69.90/50.70/58.02 precision/recall/F1, and on TRAM-Clean 9.56/10.51/9.66 and 12.54/14.59/12.99. THESE ARE THIS BASE'S FIRST FRONTIER-MODEL, PARENT-GRANULARITY, STATED-AGGREGATION, BARE-MODEL ATT&CK EXTRACTION NUMBERS. The scaffold/bare confound that this paragraph was written to warn about is therefore no longer a reason to withhold the source from this question: the bare rows and the scaffold rows are BOTH available and are clearly separated, and cycle 46's candidate 4 uses only the bare ones for model-level claims. THE PROHIBITION ON THE 76.48/87.39 FIGURES STANDS UNCHANGED -- those are still scaffold scores and still must not be set against src-0002's 0.6388 or src-0007's 0.2787. WHAT REMAINS OPEN, AND IT IS NOW TWO NARROWER THINGS RATHER THAN ONE BROAD ONE. (a) THE LITERAL 'STATED CORRECTNESS RULE' DEMAND IS STILL NOT SATISFIED. src-0021 states its aggregation and its label granularity verbatim but DOES NOT PRINT THE ITEM-LEVEL TP/FP/FN ALGEBRA, so the rule remains an INFERENCE from two stated facts (a per-document set comparison over parent-level IDs) rather than a quoted rule. Per rule (v) that absence still rests on targeted fetches of one URL form and is NOT a confirmed absence; a cheap untried route is the paper's appendix or any released artefact, neither of which has been looked for. (b) THE CROSS-GENERATION QUESTION -- does the ceiling RISE with model generation -- IS STILL UNANSWERABLE, AND NOW FOR A REASON THAT IS PROVEN RATHER THAN SUSPECTED. Comparing bare CoT GPT-4o's 58.02 to src-0002's 0.6388 or src-0007's 0.2787 IS STILL NOT LICENSED, because those three differ on unit of scoring, on label granularity and on aggregation regardless of the scaffold issue being fixed -- see open_questions[5] and candidate 5. So this base now HAS a frontier bare-model number and STILL CANNOT place it on the same axis as its predecessors. A ONE-SOURCE CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL: all of this rests on a SINGLE unreviewed v1 preprint whose benchmark is author-built and whose baseline implementations are the authors' own, so the bare rows are a competitor implementation by an interested party and no second team has reproduced them.

STILL OPEN, TWENTIETH CYCLE MERELY LISTED, AND NOW SHARPENED RATHER THAN DISCHARGED. Is there a human-analyst baseline for ATT&CK technique extraction to contextualize whether these scores are close to human or far below it? NOBODY MAY TREAT src-0018's 41-minutes-per-report figure as discharging this: that is a THROUGHPUT baseline, not an accuracy baseline. Cycle 31 sharpens the question rather than answering it: now that the src-0007/src-0017 scorer's rule is known to be EXACT technique-ID set matching with no partial credit and no parent/sub-technique credit, a useful human baseline would have to be scored under the SAME rule -- and an exact-ID rule is one under which two competent human analysts would themselves disagree substantially, since ATT&CK sub-technique assignment is a known-contested annotation task. So the absence of a human baseline is not merely a gap in this base; it is the reason the absolute magnitudes (0.22-0.35, 0.6388) cannot currently be read as evidence about how hard the task is for anyone. NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE SUPPLIES ONE. === CYCLE-45 UPDATE (T2): ADVANCED, NOT DISCHARGED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT. === The sentence immediately above -- 'NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE SUPPLIES ONE' -- STILL STANDS, because it is about an ACCURACY baseline. What changed at cycle 43 is that the base acquired, for the first time in twenty-three cycles of this question being merely listed, QUANTITATIVE INTER-ANNOTATOR AGREEMENT for parent-level ATT&CK technique labelling, from TWO INDEPENDENT TEAMS. src-0020, verbatim: 'Following the six-phase process, we reached a mean inter-annotator agreement of kappa=0.68 across 114 techniques (Landis and Koch: substantial agreement [25]), with 65 techniques (57.0%) exceeding the kappa>=0.7 quality threshold.' -- a MEAN over 114 per-technique Cohen's kappa values, reported with NO confidence interval, and with 43% of techniques falling BELOW a kappa>=0.7 bar. src-0021, verbatim: 'Each report carries sentence-level annotations produced under double-annotation with adjudication by 3 qualified annotators, achieving Cohen's kappa=0.76' on TTPrint-Bench, plus kappa=0.74 for 'the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases' on TRAM-Clean. TWO TEAMS, TWO CORPORA, ONE BAND: 0.68-0.76 [THIS FRAMING IS RETRACTED AT CYCLE 55 -- SEE THE CYCLE-55 REPAIR BLOCK AT THE END OF THIS QUESTION, WHICH GOVERNS: THE THREE VALUES ARE THREE DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS AND DO NOT FORM A BAND. THE WORDING IS LEFT STANDING ONLY SO THE FINDING REMAINS AUDITABLE AGAINST THE TEXT IT IMPEACHES], 'substantial' on Landis and Koch but well short of the near-perfect agreement an exact-ID scoring rule implicitly presumes. WHAT THIS DOES SETTLE: cycle 31 wrote into this very question that 'ATT&CK sub-technique assignment is a known-contested annotation task' AS A BARE ASSERTION WITH NO SOURCE BEHIND IT. That assertion now has quantitative support -- and the support is in one respect STRONGER than the assertion required, because it was measured on PARENT-level labels, i.e. on the EASIER labelling problem, and trained humans still disagree materially there. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, AND NO CYCLE MAY BLUR IT: AN AGREEMENT STATISTIC IS NOT AN ACCURACY BASELINE. Kappa says two trained annotators disagree with each other; it does not say how well a human scores against a gold standard, so it cannot tell us whether 0.22, 0.2787 or 0.6388 are close to human or far below it -- which is exactly what this question asks. Both papers were checked for a human accuracy or F1 figure at cycle 43 and BOTH ARE ABSENT. THE STANDING PROHIBITION IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW JOINED BY A SECOND: nobody may treat src-0018's 41-minutes-per-report THROUGHPUT figure as discharging this, and nobody may treat src-0020's or src-0021's KAPPA as discharging it either. WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE IT: a published figure for human-analyst accuracy against a gold standard on ATT&CK technique extraction, ideally scored under a stated rule so that it is commensurable with the machine scores it is meant to contextualise. That remains a T1 collection target and no scheduled task currently reaches it. === CYCLE-46 POINTER (T3), ADDED WITHOUT REWRITING ANYTHING ABOVE, AND A SUCCESSOR SHOULD FINISH THE REPAIR. ctr-0015 WAS OPENED AGAINST THE 'TWO TEAMS, TWO CORPORA, ONE BAND: 0.68-0.76' FRAMING WRITTEN ABOVE THIS LINE. Cycle 46's G2 found that this base stores src-0021's TRAM-Clean agreement sentence TRUNCATED: the source reads 'For TRAM-Clean, we report the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases (i.e., cases that reached the adjudication stage).' and the parenthetical was dropped when the quotation was stored. That parenthetical establishes that kappa=0.74 is computed over an ADJUDICATION-SELECTED HARD SUBSET, not over all annotations. THE THREE VALUES ARE THEREFORE THREE DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS: src-0020's 0.68 is a MEAN OVER 114 PER-TECHNIQUE kappas; src-0021's 0.76 is a whole-corpus kappa over all TTPrint-Bench sentence annotations; src-0021's 0.74 is a pairwise kappa over a contested subset. THEIR NEAR-EQUALITY IS NOT EVIDENCE OF CONVERGENCE, because they are not estimating the same quantity, and the words 'ONE BAND' and 'ONE CONCLUSION' above OVERSTATE. THE ORIGINAL WORDING IS DELIBERATELY LEFT STANDING so the finding remains auditable against the text it impeaches; ctr-0015 step (iii) asks a successor to rewrite it once it has been read. WHAT IS NOT DISTURBED: every numeral is exact, and the qualitative point -- that trained annotators on PARENT-level ATT&CK labelling agree substantially but far short of what an exact-ID scoring rule presumes -- SURVIVES ON EACH VALUE INDEPENDENTLY, most strongly on src-0020's, which is the only one measured over an unrestricted item set and the only one reporting its tail (43% of techniques below kappa>=0.7) [THE 'UNRESTRICTED ITEM SET' HALF OF THIS SENTENCE IS WITHDRAWN. ctr-0016, OPENED AT CYCLE 47, ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE THAT src-0020's 114 PER-TECHNIQUE KAPPAS ARE EACH ESTIMATED FROM A RANDOM 10% SAMPLE OF 195 SENTENCES AND ARE COMPUTED AT PHASE (ii) OF SIX, BEFORE RELABELLING AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION. ALL THREE VALUES ARE RESTRICTED OR AGGREGATED. SEE THE CYCLE-55 REPAIR BLOCK BELOW]. THE STANDING PROHIBITION IS REINFORCED RATHER THAN WEAKENED: an agreement statistic is not an accuracy baseline, and cycle 46 found NO human-accuracy figure while reading src-0021 whole. THIS QUESTION IS STILL OPEN AND STILL UNREACHED BY ANY SCHEDULED TASK. === CYCLE-55 REPAIR BLOCK (T3). THIS DISCHARGES ctr-0015 STEP (iii) AND ctr-0016 STEP (iii), WHICH DEMANDED THE SAME SINGLE EDIT AND HAD STOOD UNDONE FOR NINE AND EIGHT CYCLES RESPECTIVELY. NOTHING ABOVE IS DELETED; THE IMPEACHED WORDING IS MARKED IN PLACE AND THIS BLOCK GOVERNS WHEREVER THEY CONFLICT. === WHAT REPLACES 'TWO TEAMS, TWO CORPORA, ONE BAND: 0.68-0.76' AND 'TWO INDEPENDENT TEAMS, TWO CORPORA, ONE CONCLUSION': THE THREE VALUES ARE THREE DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS AND DO NOT FORM A BAND. (1) src-0020's kappa=0.68 is a MEAN OVER 114 PER-TECHNIQUE Cohen's kappa values, reported with NO confidence interval, with 43% of techniques below the kappa>=0.7 threshold -- and per ctr-0016 each of those 114 values is estimated from a RANDOM 10% SAMPLE OF 195 SENTENCES and is computed at PHASE (ii) OF SIX, BEFORE relabelling and dispute resolution. (2) src-0021's kappa=0.76 is a SINGLE WHOLE-CORPUS kappa over all sentence-level annotations of TTPrint-Bench. (3) src-0021's kappa=0.74 is a PAIRWISE kappa restricted to an ADJUDICATION-SELECTED CONTESTED SUBSET of TRAM-Clean -- the defining parenthetical '(i.e., cases that reached the adjudication stage)' having been dropped when this base first stored the sentence (ctr-0015). A mean of per-class kappas from a 10% sample, a whole-corpus kappa, and a hard-subset pairwise kappa are three different quantities. THEIR NEAR-EQUALITY IS NOT EVIDENCE OF CONVERGENCE AND MUST NEVER BE CITED AS MUTUAL CORROBORATION; the phrases 'one band' and 'one conclusion' are withdrawn and must not be reused anywhere in this base. WHAT SURVIVES THE REPAIR, STATED NARROWLY SO THIS BLOCK IS NOT OVER-READ IN EITHER DIRECTION: every numeral is exact and every quotation except the one truncation re-verified PRESENT at cycles 46 and 47; and the QUALITATIVE point -- that trained annotators on PARENT-level ATT&CK labelling agree substantially but far short of the near-perfect agreement an exact-ID scoring rule implicitly presumes -- SURVIVES ON EACH VALUE INDEPENDENTLY, though it can no longer be said to rest 'most strongly' on any one of the three. IT IS NOW CARRIED BEST BY A DIFFERENT NUMBER ENTIRELY, recovered by ctr-0016 and measured over the WHOLE 2,076-sentence corpus rather than over any sample: 981 of 2,076 sentences (47.3%, a cycle-47 derivation from two printed numbers, the printed numbers being exact) required relabelling as low-agreement, kappa<0.7. THAT figure is the cleanest evidence this base holds for ATT&CK annotation being a contested task, and successors should cite it in preference to the 0.68 mean. THE STANDING PROHIBITION IS UNCHANGED AND UNWEAKENED BY THIS REPAIR: AN AGREEMENT STATISTIC IS NOT AN ACCURACY BASELINE. None of 0.68, 0.76, 0.74 or the 47.3% relabelling rate discharges this question, which asks for HUMAN ACCURACY AGAINST A GOLD STANDARD, ideally under a stated scoring rule so as to be commensurable with the machine scores it is meant to contextualise. NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE SUPPLIES ONE. That remains a T1 collection target and no scheduled task currently reaches it.

This directly matches src-0001's finding that fine-tuning can actively degrade CTI sub-tasks rather than 'partially improve' them. STILL OPEN AS LITERALLY POSED: src-0007's fine-tuning is general task fine-tuning, not fine-tuning specifically on ATT&CK-technique-extraction data, so whether a targeted ATT&CK fine-tune would behave differently is untested by any source in this base. CYCLE 31 ADDS ONE CONSTRAINT ON HOW ANY FUTURE ANSWER MAY BE READ: the released scorer admits a predicted technique ID on the sole condition that the ID appears in its mapping file, and DISCARDS the model's own description of the technique before scoring (candidate 3), so a fine-tune that improved the QUALITY of technique descriptions while leaving ID selection unchanged would register as exactly zero improvement on this metric.

NOTE ALSO, from the executing code and bearing on how any answer must be read: article_ttps_set is built with the filter 'if " - " in ttp', so any ground-truth entry NOT written in the form 'ID - Name' is silently excluded from the ground truth altogether and can generate neither a true positive nor a false negative -- so the format question is not merely about granularity, it also determines the effective size of the recall denominator. === CYCLE-55 UPDATE (T3, VIA THE G2 ON src-0017): (a) IS NOW ANSWERED FOR THE WORKED EXAMPLE AND ONLY FOR THE WORKED EXAMPLE, AND A THIRD FACT ABOUT THIS ARTEFACT WAS FOUND THAT NO PRIOR CYCLE KNEW. === Cycle 55 took the first of the two cheap routes cycle 32 named and neither cycle tried. The GitHub trees API (api.github.com/repos/xschen-beb/CyberThreat-Eval/git/trees/main?recursive=true) returned truncated:false and lists stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/example/ as holding example_ground_truth.json at 3,406 bytes, example_predicted.json at 1,191 bytes and simple_test.py at 7,953 bytes. example_ground_truth.json is small enough to fetch WHOLE and was reproduced in full. IT CONTAINS TWO ARTICLES AND SEVEN GROUND-TRUTH ttps ENTRIES, EVERY ONE PARENT-LEVEL AND EVERY ONE IN THE 'ID - Name' FORM THE SCORER'S FILTER REQUIRES: for the first article, 'T1204 - User Execution', 'T1189 - Drive-by Compromise', 'T1036 - Masquerading'; for the second, 'T1204 - User Execution', 'T1036 - Masquerading', 'T1070 - Indicator Removal', 'T1219 - Remote Access Software'. NOT ONE contains a dot, so not one is a sub-technique ID. WHAT THIS LICENSES: the ground-truth FORMAT is 'ID - Name', so the ' - ' membership filter in article_ttps_set does not silently drop entries of this shape, and the recall-denominator worry recorded above does not bite on data written this way. WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE: any claim whatever about data/100-days-articles.json, which is 1,441,832 bytes, still truncates, and is the file the paper's numbers would actually have been computed over. Seven entries from a two-article worked EXAMPLE are an illustration of the format, not a sample of the corpus, and no cycle may promote them into one. SO (a) IS ANSWERED FOR THE EXAMPLE AND REMAINS OPEN FOR THE CORPUS. The direction it points: IF the corpus follows the example, a model emitting sub-technique IDs is double-penalised on every one of them, which is exactly the scenario candidate 3 describes -- now shown to be the granularity actually used in the artefact's own worked case rather than merely admissible under the mapping. NEW AT CYCLE 45 (T2), AND IT IS THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT NOW GOVERNS THIS WHOLE ISSUE. THE FOUR ATT&CK MEASUREMENTS IN THIS BASE ARE MUTUALLY NON-COMMENSURABLE, AND ACQUIRING TWO MORE SOURCES AT CYCLE 43 DID NOT PRODUCE TWO MORE COMPARABLE NUMBERS. Laid out so no cycle has to re-derive it: (1) src-0002 CTI-ATE, 0.6388 for ChatGPT-4 -- document/instance level over 60 malware instances and 397 unique techniques, metric AMBIGUOUS between Micro-F1 (body text, one occurrence) and Macro-F1 (Table 1 header, one occurrence), item-level correctness rule UNSTATED and now known to be UNRECOVERABLE from paper and code alike (see open_questions[3]). (2) src-0007 / src-0017, 0.2787 precision / 0.2270 recall for GPT-4o -- EXACT SUB-TECHNIQUE-ID set intersection with NO partial credit and NO parent/sub-technique credit, read off executing code at cycle 31, and with a ground-truth filter ('if " - " in ttp') that silently drops malformed entries from the recall denominator. (3) src-0020, best micro-F1 0.22 -- SENTENCE-level, PARENT-level (211 techniques, sub-techniques explicitly omitted), MICRO-averaged over technique instances, OPEN-SOURCE models only, ONE corpus (The DFIR Report). (4) src-0021, 76.48% and 87.39% macro-F1 -- DOCUMENT-level, PARENT-level, MACRO-AVERAGED OVER DOCUMENTS, and a SCAFFOLD score rather than a bare-model score. FOUR AXES OF DIFFERENCE ARE IN PLAY AT ONCE -- unit of scoring (sentence vs document vs instance), label granularity (parent vs sub-technique), aggregation (micro vs macro-over-documents vs unknown), and system-vs-model -- and NO TWO OF THE FOUR AGREE ON ALL FOUR. THE SHARPEST INSTANCE, WHICH IS A METRIC-IDENTITY TRAP OF EXACTLY THE SHAPE ctr-0013 STANDS AS A WARNING ABOUT: src-0021's 'macro-F1' is a macro over DOCUMENTS, stated verbatim as 'F1bar = 1/|D| sum_{d in D} F1_d', whereas src-0002's Table 1 header 'Macro-F1' would on any conventional reading be a macro over TECHNIQUES. THESE ARE DIFFERENT STATISTICS SHARING A NAME, and the shared name is the only thing they share. SIMILARLY, src-0020 and src-0021 are BOTH parent-level, which is the single most tempting pairing in this base, and they are STILL NOT COMPARABLE: sentence-level micro over open-source bare models against document-level macro-over-documents over a frontier-backed scaffold. TWO PARENT-LEVEL SOURCES IS NOT TWO COMPARABLE MEASUREMENTS. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN HERE, stated as a question rather than a warning: is there any pair of published ATT&CK-extraction numbers in or reachable by this base that share unit, granularity, aggregation AND system-vs-model status, such that a genuine cross-source comparison could be made at all? If the answer is no, then this issue's honest resolution is a statement ABOUT THE MEASUREMENT LITERATURE -- that ATT&CK extraction reliability is reported in mutually unconvertible units and therefore has no established cross-study magnitude -- rather than a number. A T3 or T4 should treat that as a live candidate resolution in its own right and not as a failure to find one. === CYCLE-46 UPDATE (T3): THE QUESTION AS POSED IS ANSWERED -- NO -- AND THE INVITATION IN THE SENTENCE ABOVE HAS BEEN TAKEN UP. === The question asked whether any pair of published ATT&CK-extraction numbers IN OR REACHABLE BY THIS BASE share unit, granularity, aggregation AND system-vs-model status. FOR THE FOUR MEASUREMENTS IN THIS BASE THE ANSWER IS NO, and cycle 46 wrote it up as candidate 5 with evidence src-0002, src-0007, src-0020 and src-0021, promoted to 'supported' on the ground that a negative existential over four sources is settled by direct inspection of those four sources' own stated methods rather than by an absence-of-evidence argument. CYCLE 43 IS THE EMPIRICAL TEST OF THAT CANDIDATE AND IT PASSED: two new sources arrived and produced ZERO new comparable pairs. ONE GENUINE QUALIFICATION FOUND THE SAME CYCLE AND RECORDED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED, BECAUSE IT CUTS AGAINST THE CANDIDATE. src-0021's Table 1 IS an internally commensurable set of four systems -- TTPDrill 2.19/7.16, One-Shot GPT-4o 9.66/44.23, CoT GPT-4o 12.99/58.02 and TTPrint 76.48/87.39 F1 on TRAM-Clean/TTPrint-Bench -- all scored under one rule on two corpora, and Table 2 adds six backbones under a fixed scaffold. SO COMMENSURABLE COMPARISON IS PLAINLY ACHIEVABLE WITHIN A STUDY; what fails is CROSS-STUDY synthesis. Candidate 5 is scoped to the cross-study claim only, and that scoping is the difference between a defensible finding and an overreach. WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS OPEN HERE, NARROWED FROM THE ORIGINAL: (a) the question said 'or REACHABLE BY this base', and cycle 46 tested only the four sources IN it -- whether an uncollected paper reports ATT&CK extraction under a frame matching one already held is a T1 collection question that has never been asked, and the specific high-value target would be any study that RE-SCORES prior systems under one common metric; (b) whether src-0002's Table 1 'Macro-F1' really is a macro over TECHNIQUES is still an inference from convention, not a stated fact, and cycle 45 proved it is unrecoverable from the paper and from CTIBench's released code, so this axis of the non-commensurability argument rests on a conventional reading rather than on the source -- WHICH WEAKENS THAT ONE LIMB AND MUST BE SAID PLAINLY, though three other axes (unit, granularity, system-vs-model) separate src-0002 from src-0021 regardless; (c) the latent policy question, carried as [97] and NOT decidable by any cycle: whether a non-commensurability finding may count as RESOLVING an issue for scoring purposes, or whether the 0-5 scale presumes a positive answer and would score an honest negative result as a failure. A T4 CONFRONTS (c) DIRECTLY THE MOMENT IT SCORES CANDIDATE 5.

WHAT WAS REMOVED AND WHY. (1) The quantified cross-task comparison, '0.6388 ... far below the ~71-72% accuracy the same models reach on knowledge-recall tasks'. src-0002's own metric paragraph forbids that subtraction: verbatim, 'We use accuracy to evaluate the CTI-MCQ and CTT-RCM tasks, as both tasks are equivalent to multi-class classification', against an F1 over a MULTI-LABEL space of 397 technique IDs. A multi-class accuracy with a non-trivial chance baseline and a multi-label F1 with a near-zero chance baseline are not differenceable quantities. The comparison was OURS and never the paper's: exact-string checks returned 'task difficulty' ABSENT and 'most challenging' ABSENT, and a third fetch asked for every sentence comparing performance BETWEEN tasks returned ABSENT. (2) The second sentence, which rested on src-0005 for the claim that the gap has not closed with newer models. Cycle 26 established that src-0005 REPORTS NO ATT&CK METRIC AT ALL, so it cannot support an ATT&CK claim in either direction. src-0005 IS ACCORDINGLY REMOVED FROM THIS CANDIDATE'S EVIDENCE LIST. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS, STATED QUALITATIVELY. On CTIBench's CTI-ATE task -- extracting MITRE ATT&CK techniques from threat text and mapping them to technique IDs -- the best-performing model of the five evaluated (ChatGPT-4) reaches 0.6388, and no evaluated model exceeds that. The paper's own characterisation of the task is 'ChatGPT-4 significantly outperforms other models on the CTI-ATE task, underscoring the complexity of the task', which is a CROSS-MODEL observation and is the only textual anchor the paper offers. TWO METROLOGICAL LIMITS ARE NOW PART OF THE CLAIM RATHER THAN FOOTNOTES TO IT. (A) THE METRIC IDENTITY OF 0.6388 IS AMBIGUOUS BY THE PAPER'S OWN TEXT. Section 4.2 body text says 'We adopt the Micro-F1 score as the evaluation metric for the CTI-ATE task', while Table 1's column header reads 'CTI-ATE (Macro-F1)'. Micro-F1 and Macro-F1 are different quantities and diverge substantially over a 397-label multi-label space with a long tail. Both strings are PRESENT and verbatim in two independent fetches of arxiv.org/html/2406.07599v3. This is a defect IN THE SOURCE, not in this state, and it is unresolvable from the paper. (B) THE PAPER NEVER STATES HOW A PREDICTED TECHNIQUE COUNTS AS CORRECT -- exact technique ID, parent technique, sub-technique, or partial credit -- ABSENT in two fetches. So this leg reports a number whose metric is ambiguous and whose correctness rule is unstated, and cycle 31 could not repair either from the paper (see open_question 4). WHAT MUST NOT BE SAID, AND THIS IS THE STANDING PROHIBITION ctr-0006 EXISTS TO ENFORCE: that CTI-ATE is measurably harder than any other CTIBench task by a stated margin. Beyond the non-commensurability above, the ordering does not even hold naively in the direction the old text implied -- Table 1's CTI-TAA Correct column reads 52 for the same model, BELOW 63.88, so 'ATT&CK mapping is the worst task' is false on the paper's own printed numbers as well as unsupported by its text. FETCHING NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE CHECK: use arxiv.org/html/2406.07599v3 or the latest render. ARXIV v2 HAS NO CTI-ATE TASK AT ALL, so a v2 fetch returns spurious ABSENTs. ADDED cycle 16 by T2, discharging carry-forward [2] which was cited in cycles 10 and 13 rationales but never attached to the graph. A third independent source now measures ATT&CK technique mapping and it lands FAR BELOW CTIBench's already-low ceiling. src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026), on expert-annotated material drawn from a real company's daily CTI workflow, reports MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (fine-tuned GPT-4o) and 0.1771/0.1414 (fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini) -- against src-0002's CTI-ATE best-model F1 ceiling of 0.6388. THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION WITH src-0002 and no G3 entry was opened: different benchmark, different corpus, and a different metric decomposition (precision and recall separately, no F1), and real production material proving harder than a curated benchmark is the expected direction rather than a conflicting one. What src-0007 adds is twofold. (a) INDEPENDENCE: its authors are unaffiliated with CTIBench's and with PRISM/LANCE's, so the hardness of ATT&CK mapping is no longer resting on one team's benchmark design. (b) A WITHIN-TABLE CONTROL that cross-benchmark synthesis cannot supply: the identical models, on the identical corpus, through the identical harness, reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, so the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. Provenance note: every figure quoted here was re-verified verbatim against the source by cycle 15's G2, exact to four decimal places, with no discrepancy. === CYCLE-31 ADDENDUM, APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED: CLAIM (b) IS NOW WITHDRAWN AND CLAIM (a) IS NARROWED. === Cycle 29's assessment held that this candidate's two distinctive contributions were both damaged, and cycle 31 read the missing scorer and can now say exactly how. (b) THE WITHIN-TABLE CONTROL DOES NOT SURVIVE AND MUST NOT BE CITED AGAIN. The argument was that because the identical models on the identical corpus through the identical harness reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. That inference silently assumed the two numbers were produced by comparable scoring. THEY ARE NOT, AND THE TWO RULES ARE NOW BOTH KNOWN FROM EXECUTING CODE IN THE SAME ARTEFACT. The IoC side (ctr-0004, cycle 27) is ONE-DIRECTIONAL SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT: any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set), so a prediction scores a true positive merely by being a substring of a ground-truth entry. The ATT&CK side (cycle 31, candidate 3) is EXACT TECHNIQUE-ID SET INTERSECTION with no partial credit of any kind. These are not two settings of one dial; they are different KINDS of matching, and the substring rule is the more permissive of the two on the axis that matters here. A comparison between a leniently scored number and a strictly scored number cannot license a conclusion about corpus or harness quality, which is precisely what claim (b) asserted. THE CONTROL IS WITHDRAWN. (a) INDEPENDENCE STANDS BUT DELIVERS LESS THAN CYCLE 16 CREDITED. src-0007's authors are genuinely unaffiliated with CTIBench's, so the finding that ATT&CK mapping scores low no longer rests on one team's benchmark design. But after ctr-0006 and cycle 31, the two legs are scored under rules that are (src-0007) known and strict, and (src-0002) unstated and metrically ambiguous. What the two independent sources jointly establish is therefore the DIRECTION of the finding -- ATT&CK technique mapping scores low on every measurement anyone has published -- and NOT any quantitative relationship between the two figures, which this candidate already disclaimed and which must stay disclaimed. WHAT IS UNCHANGED AND MUST NOT BE STRIPPED: all nine of src-0007's figures remain exact and remain the best-verified numbers in this base, and the fine-tuning result (0.2787/0.2270 for GPT-4o falling to 0.2387/0.1846 fine-tuned, and 0.1771/0.1414 for fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini) is untouched by anything above, since it is a WITHIN-COLUMN comparison scored by one rule against itself and is exactly the comparison the scorer supports best.

ADDED CYCLE 31. THE ATT&CK/TTP SCORING RULE BEHIND src-0007's TTP NUMBERS IS NOW KNOWN, READ OFF EXECUTING CODE, AND IT IS SUBSTANTIALLY STRICTER THAN ANY RULE PREVIOUSLY ASSUMED IN THIS BASE -- AND ITS OWN DOCUMENTATION DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT RULE FROM THE ONE IT RUNS. This is the fetch ctr-0006 step (iii), ctr-0001's remaining path and carry-forward [34] had all been asking for since cycle 24. The file is stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py in the src-0017 artefact, retrieved WHOLE via raw.githubusercontent.com and read for which lines EXECUTE, per the ctr-0004 trap in which the IoC evaluator's documented rule turned out to live inside dead triple-quoted string literals. THE EXECUTING RULE, quoted verbatim from the live code. Ground truth per article: article_ttps_set = {ttp.split(' - ')[0].strip() for ttp in raw_ttps if ' - ' in ttp}. Predictions are a dict keyed by technique ID; each key is looked up in a mapping loaded from data/TTP_Mapping.csv, and the scoring set is validated_ttps_set = set(validated_ttps_final.keys()). Metrics: tp = len(article_ttps_set.intersection(validated_ttps_set)); fp = len(validated_ttps_set - article_ttps_set) + missing_in_mapping_count; fn = len(article_ttps_set - validated_ttps_set); then micro-averaged as overall_precision = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fp) and overall_recall = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fn). SO THE RULE IS EXACT STRING EQUALITY OF TECHNIQUE IDS, VIA SET INTERSECTION. There is no substring matching, no parent-technique credit, no sub-technique credit and no partial credit anywhere in the executing path. CONSEQUENCE THAT IS DIRECTLY ASSERTABLE, because TTP_Mapping.csv verifiably contains sub-technique IDs (T1548.001, T1548.002, T1548.003 and T1548.004 were quoted verbatim from it this cycle): if the ground truth says T1548 and a model predicts T1548.002, that prediction is admitted by the mapping check, fails the intersection, and is counted as a FALSE POSITIVE while T1548 is simultaneously counted as a FALSE NEGATIVE. One arguably-correct answer at the wrong granularity is penalised TWICE. SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS ctr-0004 BUT A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. The scorer's own docstring says, verbatim, 'If a TTP's description does not match the expected mapping, issue a warning and do NOT add this TTP to the final validated TTPs. (Such TTPs will be treated as false positives.)', and the directory README says the same in its own words -- 'Filtering: Only TTPs with matching descriptions are included' and, for a worked mismatch example, 'Result: Rejected (counted as false positive)'. THE CODE DOES THE OPPOSITE. On a description mismatch the live else-branch prints a warning and then executes corrected_details = ttp_mapping[ttp_id] followed by validated_ttps_final[ttp_id] = corrected_details -- it OVERWRITES the model's description with the canonical one and KEEPS the entry. There is no dead string literal here; the live code simply contradicts the docstring sitting above it in the same function. THE OPERATIVE CONSEQUENCE: the description check is INERT for scoring. A predicted technique ID counts on the sole condition that the ID appears in the mapping file, whatever the model wrote about it. So the scorer measures ID SELECTION ONLY, and any claim that it also measures whether the model correctly characterised the technique is false. THIRD FINDING, LENIENCY IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, RECORDED SO THE BIAS IS NOT ASSUMED TO RUN ONE WAY: a per-article json5 parse failure executes 'continue' and the whole surrounding block is wrapped in a bare 'except Exception', so an article whose model output is malformed is DROPPED ENTIRELY -- contributing no false negatives for its ground truth and no false positives. Malformed output is not penalised; it is excluded from the micro-average. This is the one respect in which the rule is generous, and it cuts against the strictness above rather than reinforcing it. STATUS AND SCOPE, STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE THE TEMPTATION TO OVERREACH HERE IS LARGE. This candidate is supported as a claim about WHAT THE RELEASED SCORER DOES. It is NOT established that src-0007's Table 4 TTP figures were produced by this code: neither the paper nor the artefact says so, and the link is an inference from src-0017 being src-0007's release (see open_question 5). src-0017 is NOT INDEPENDENT of src-0007 -- same authors, same artefact -- so this pair can never serve as the two independent sources a strong claim requires; the claim is a direct reading of one artefact and needs no second source, but it also cannot borrow independence it does not have. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE ISSUE RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA: one of this issue's two comparands now has a stated, verified correctness rule and the other still has none. That is an improvement in the state of the evidence and simultaneously a demonstration that the two numbers were never comparable. === CYCLE-32 ADDENDUM, APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED. THIS CANDIDATE WAS RE-VERIFIED BY AN INDEPENDENT RE-FETCH AND IT PASSES; ONE FINDING IS ADDED THAT STRENGTHENS IT. === Cycle 32's G2 chose this candidate as its subject precisely because it was the newest, most load-bearing and least replicated conclusion in the graph -- a single fetch, made at cycle 31, on the strength of which ctr-0006 was CLOSED. stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py was re-fetched whole from raw.githubusercontent.com and reproduced verbatim a second time, with ten exact-string checks run against the strings stored above. ALL TEN RETURNED PRESENT AND EXACT: the article_ttps_set comprehension, the validated_ttps_set assignment, the tp/fp/fn lines, the two overall_ ratio lines, the docstring sentence 'do NOT add this TTP to the final validated TTPs', corrected_details = ttp_mapping[ttp_id], validated_ttps_final[ttp_id] = corrected_details, json5 and except Exception. THE CRITICAL STRUCTURAL POINT WAS RE-CONFIRMED SPECIFICALLY AND SEPARATELY: the description-mismatch else-branch was reproduced with its indentation and the fetch was asked to state whether it is live executable code or sits inside a triple-quoted string, comment or docstring; the answer was that it is LIVE. So the docstring-versus-code contradiction is replicated, and this is not a second instance of the ctr-0004 dead-literal artefact. NOTHING IN THIS CANDIDATE IS RETRACTED OR NARROWED. THE ONE ADDITION, AND IT SHARPENS THE STRICTNESS FINDING RATHER THAN QUALIFYING IT. Cycle 32 read the head of data/TTP_Mapping.csv verbatim under an explicit instruction to make no claim about the whole file (it is 1,083,078 bytes and truncates -- see this issue's open_question 5 and cycle 31's own retraction). The header row is verbatim ',TechniqueID,name,longdescription,is sub-technique,sub-technique of,description,tactics', which on a 0-based naive comma split puts TechniqueID at field 1 and name at field 2, CONFIRMING that load_ttp_mapping's fields[1]/fields[2] do select the intended columns. BUT FIELD 5 IS 'sub-technique of', AND IT CARRIES THE PARENT ID. Verified verbatim on real data rows: T1548 appears with is sub-technique FALSE and an empty parent field, while T1548.001, T1548.002, T1548.003, T1548.004 and T1548.005 each appear with is sub-technique TRUE and 'sub-technique of' = T1548. load_ttp_mapping reads ONLY fields[1] and fields[2] and DISCARDS field 5. CONSEQUENCE: the parent-child relation needed to award parent-level credit for a sub-technique prediction is PRESENT IN THE SCORER'S OWN MAPPING FILE AND THROWN AWAY BY THE LOADER. The correct statement of this candidate's central finding is therefore not merely that the scorer implements no partial credit, but that it discards the data that would let it -- and that both legs of the double-penalty scenario asserted above are demonstrably reachable, since a parent ID and its sub-technique IDs are simultaneously admissible keys in the same mapping. TWO SMALLER POINTS, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT MISTAKEN FOR DEFECTS LATER. (1) The naive parser's spurious keys, noted at cycle 31, are SCORING-INERT and here is the reason, which cycle 31 left unstated: continuation lines of quoted long descriptions do get parsed as candidate rows, but their fields[1] values are prose fragments that cannot equal a technique ID, and even in the improbable case that one did, the only thing it could corrupt is a mapped NAME -- and a name mismatch keeps the entry regardless, per this candidate's second finding. The pollution therefore cannot change any tp, fp or fn. (2) The header line itself satisfies the parser's conditions and enters the mapping as ttp_mapping['TechniqueID'] = 'name'; likewise inert. NO CONTRADICTION ENTRY WAS OPENED BY CYCLE 32 AND NONE WAS WARRANTED: this is a clean replication plus a strengthening addition, which is the outcome the G2 mechanism is supposed to be able to produce and had produced only twice in twelve source-checks before now.

ADDED CYCLE 46 (T3). THE FIRST CONTROLLED BARE-MODEL-VERSUS-SCAFFOLD COMPARISON IN THIS BASE, AND IT SHOWS THE SCAFFOLD CONTRIBUTES MORE THAN THE BACKBONE DOES. THIS DISCHARGES CARRY-FORWARD [80]. Everything below comes from ONE paper (src-0021, TTPrint) so that unit of scoring, label granularity, metric aggregation and corpus are HELD CONSTANT -- which is precisely what no cross-source comparison in this issue has ever been able to do. All cells were obtained by a discovery fetch of arxiv.org/html/2605.25836v1 and then RE-CONFIRMED by a separate exact-string ask, per methodological rule (xvii). THE MEASUREMENT FRAME, CONSTANT THROUGHOUT: document-level scoring, parent-level technique IDs only (prompt, verbatim: 'Output only ATT&CK technique IDs in parent-technique format: TXXXX, no child technique like TXXXX.XXX'), and macro-averaged over documents (verbatim: 'Final scores are macro-averages over all documents'). FINDING 1, AND IT IS THE ONE THIS ISSUE HAS WANTED SINCE CYCLE 26: THERE IS NOW A BARE FRONTIER-MODEL ATT&CK EXTRACTION NUMBER WITH A STATED GRANULARITY AND A STATED AGGREGATION. src-0021's Table 1 carries two DIRECTLY-PROMPTED, UNSCAFFOLDED GPT-4o rows, and the paper labels them as such verbatim: 'For LLM-based approaches, we include two direct prompting baselines: One-Shot, which classifies each sentence with one in-context example, and CoT, which adds explicit chain-of-thought reasoning to the same prompt.' On TTPrint-Bench, One-Shot GPT-4o scores 62.99 precision / 52.80 recall / 44.23 F1 and CoT GPT-4o scores 69.90 / 50.70 / 58.02. On TRAM-Clean the same two score 9.56 / 10.51 / 9.66 and 12.54 / 14.59 / 12.99. A second verbatim anchor prints one of these rows in prose: 'One-Shot GPT-4o achieves 52.80% recall and 62.99% precision (F1 44.23%), reflecting incomplete behavior extraction and surface similarity mismatch respectively.' FINDING 2, THE SCAFFOLD DELTA, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. With the backbone held at GPT-4o, the progression on TTPrint-Bench is bare One-Shot 44.23 -> bare CoT 58.02 -> full TTPrint 87.39, and on TRAM-Clean 9.66 -> 12.99 -> 76.48. THIS IS DIRECT QUANTITATIVE EVIDENCE THAT THE SYSTEM-VERSUS-MODEL CONFOUND ctr-0001 WAS OPENED ABOUT IS REAL AND LARGE, and it is the first time this base has been able to put a number on it rather than merely warn about it: on TRAM-Clean the scaffold moves the same model from 12.99 to 76.48, so ROUGHLY FIVE SIXTHS OF THAT HEADLINE FIGURE IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE PIPELINE AND NOT TO THE LANGUAGE MODEL. FINDING 3, BACKBONE SENSITIVITY UNDER A FIXED SCAFFOLD. Table 2 runs the full pipeline on six backbones with, verbatim, 'All pipeline hyperparameters are held constant across backbones to isolate the effect of the underlying model': GPT-4o 82.15/95.50/87.39; GPT-4o-mini 61.31/57.49/58.01; Claude Sonnet 4.6 65.09/80.12/71.07; Gemini 2.5 Flash 46.62/94.41/61.62; Qwen 3 235B 57.81/80.91/66.59; DeepSeek v3.2 67.05/77.94/71.04. So under a fixed scaffold the backbone spread is 58.01 to 87.39. TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS ISSUE. (A) THE 'DOES THE CEILING RISE WITH MODEL GENERATION' QUESTION NOW HAS A PARTIAL, PROPERLY-SCOPED ANSWER: a 2026-era frontier model prompted DIRECTLY reaches 44.23-58.02 macro-F1 at parent granularity on a document-level benchmark -- materially above src-0007's 0.2787-class figures and BELOW OR NEAR src-0002's 0.6388, but NONE of those three comparisons is licensed, because all three differ on at least one of the four axes in open_questions[5]. WHAT IS LICENSED IS ONLY THE WITHIN-PAPER READING. (B) THE STRONGEST CROSS-CUTTING CLAIM THIS BASE CAN NOW MAKE ABOUT ATT&CK MAPPING IS THAT PIPELINE DESIGN DOMINATES MODEL CHOICE ON THIS TASK -- 12.99 to 76.48 from scaffolding one fixed model, against 58.01 to 87.39 from swapping backbones under a fixed scaffold. LIMITS THAT BIND AND MUST TRAVEL WITH ANY REUSE: this is a SINGLE unreviewed v1 preprint (re-confirmed at cycle 46 as still v1, Comments 'Preprint', no journal reference), TTPrint-Bench is AUTHOR-BUILT AND TOPPED BY ITS OWN AUTHORS' SYSTEM and TRAM-Clean is those same authors' cleaning of someone else's benchmark, so the bare-baseline rows are the authors' OWN implementation of their competitors and a weak baseline implementation would flatter the delta in Findings 2 and 3 -- NO SECOND TEAM HAS REPRODUCED THESE BASELINE NUMBERS and until one does, Finding 2's magnitude is single-team evidence. It is also worth recording that the paper's item-level TP/FP/FN algebra is still not printed, so the correctness rule remains an inference from two stated facts. FINALLY, A READING TRAP IN THE ABSTRACT, NOW SETTLED: 'outperforming the leading baseline by 63.5% and 29.4%' is an ABSOLUTE PERCENTAGE-POINT DIFFERENCE and the 'leading baseline' is CoT GPT-4o. The body prints it verbatim: 'CoT GPT-4o at 58.02%) and 76.48% on TRAM-Clean (+63.49 over CoT GPT-4o at 12.99%).' Cycle 46's arithmetic check, LABELLED DERIVED per rule (xii): 76.48 minus 12.99 = 63.49 and 87.39 minus 58.02 = 29.37. Read as a RELATIVE improvement the first would be about +489%, so the misreading is large.

ADDED CYCLE 46 (T3), ANSWERING THE QUESTION open_questions[5] POSES AND TAKING UP ITS OWN INSTRUCTION THAT A NON-COMMENSURABILITY FINDING SHOULD BE TREATED AS A LIVE CANDIDATE RESOLUTION RATHER THAN AS A FAILURE TO FIND ONE. THE PROPOSED RESOLUTION, STATED FLATLY: ATT&CK TECHNIQUE-EXTRACTION RELIABILITY IS REPORTED IN MUTUALLY UNCONVERTIBLE UNITS, AND THIS ISSUE THEREFORE HAS NO ESTABLISHED CROSS-STUDY MAGNITUDE -- only a direction, and a set of within-study magnitudes that cannot be pooled. THE ARGUMENT, FROM THE FOUR MEASUREMENTS IN THIS BASE. (1) src-0002 CTI-ATE, 0.6388 for ChatGPT-4: instance-level over 60 malware instances and 397 techniques; metric AMBIGUOUS between Micro-F1 (body text, exactly one occurrence) and Macro-F1 (Table 1 header, exactly one occurrence); item-level correctness rule UNSTATED and, since cycle 45, known to be UNRECOVERABLE from the paper AND from the released code of two mirrors. (2) src-0007 via the src-0017 artefact, 0.2787 precision / 0.2270 recall for GPT-4o: EXACT SUB-TECHNIQUE-ID set intersection, no partial credit, no parent credit, read off executing code, with a ground-truth filter that silently drops malformed entries from the recall denominator. (3) src-0020, best micro-F1 0.22: SENTENCE-level, PARENT-level over 211 techniques, MICRO-averaged over technique instances, OPEN-SOURCE models only, one corpus. (4) src-0021, 87.39 macro-F1: DOCUMENT-level, PARENT-level, MACRO-AVERAGED OVER DOCUMENTS, and a SCAFFOLD score. FOUR AXES VARY AT ONCE -- unit of scoring, label granularity, aggregation, and system-versus-model -- AND NO TWO OF THE FOUR AGREE ON ALL FOUR. THE SHARPEST CASE IS A METRIC-IDENTITY TRAP OF THE ctr-0013 SHAPE: src-0021's 'macro-F1' is a macro over DOCUMENTS, stated verbatim as 'Final scores are macro-averages over all documents', whereas src-0002's Table 1 header 'Macro-F1' would on any conventional reading be a macro over TECHNIQUES. Different statistics sharing a name. Even the most tempting pairing fails: src-0020 and src-0021 are BOTH parent-level and are STILL not comparable, being sentence-level micro over bare open-source models versus document-level macro-over-documents over a frontier-backed scaffold. WHY CYCLE 46 PROMOTES THIS TO 'supported' RATHER THAN LEAVING IT 'proposed'. The claim is NEGATIVE and EXISTENTIAL -- that no commensurable pair exists among these four -- and it is established by direct inspection of the four sources' own stated methods, each of which is separately cited and verbatim-quoted in this base. It does not depend on any absence-of-evidence argument about the wider literature, and it is deliberately NOT stated as a claim about the literature as a whole: what is supported is that THE FOUR MEASUREMENTS IN THIS BASE ARE PAIRWISE NON-COMMENSURABLE, which is checkable and checked. Four independent sources back it, exceeding the two-source bar for a strong claim. WHAT THIS RESOLUTION DOES NOT SAY, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE VALUE OF IT. It does NOT say the task is unmeasured, and it does NOT license agnosticism about the finding this issue has carried since cycle 16. THE DIRECTION IS ROBUST AND IS ESTABLISHED BY THE VERY MULTIPLICITY THAT BLOCKS THE MAGNITUDE: four teams with no author overlap, using four different scoring frames on four different corpora, ALL find ATT&CK technique extraction to be the weakest CTI sub-task they measure, and three of the four put bare-model performance below 0.65 on their own scale. Non-commensurability defeats the average, not the sign. NOR does it say the numbers are wrong; each is presumptively correct WITHIN its own frame. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE A T4 SHOULD PRICE: this issue cannot be resolved by collecting more numbers, because each new paper has so far arrived with its own frame -- cycle 43 added TWO sources and produced ZERO new comparable pairs, which is the empirical test of this candidate and it passed. What WOULD move it is a single study scoring multiple systems under one stated rule, or a published re-scoring of prior work under a common metric. CYCLE 46 NOTES ONE PARTIAL COUNTERWEIGHT DISCOVERED THE SAME CYCLE AND RECORDS IT HERE RATHER THAN SUPPRESSING IT: src-0021's Table 1 DOES contain an internally commensurable set -- TTPDrill, One-Shot GPT-4o, CoT GPT-4o and TTPrint scored under one rule on two corpora -- so commensurable comparison is achievable WITHIN a study. The non-commensurability is a property of CROSS-STUDY synthesis in this literature, not of the measurement task itself, and this candidate is scoped to the cross-study claim only. THIS CANDIDATE IS ALSO A LATENT POLICY QUESTION FOR A HUMAN, carried as [97]: whether a finding of this shape may count as RESOLVING an issue for scoring purposes, or whether the scoring scale presumes a positive answer and would score an honest non-commensurability finding as a failure. Cycle 46 has no standing to decide that.

issues.title: How reliable is LLM-assisted extraction of mechanical indicators of compromise (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes) from threat reports?
open_questions: STILL OPEN, BUT SHARPENED (cycle 9): no direct replication or critique of LANCE/PRISM exists -- cycle 6 searched for one and cycle 9 searched again over a wider net (see logs/cycle-009.md for exact queries), and 2603.09452 and 2605.06910 do not cite arXiv 2506.11325 at all. What now exists instead is an independent measurement of a DIFFERENT system on a DIFFERENT corpus (src-0007, vanilla LLM IoC extraction, precision 0.82-0.88) sitting ~10-15 points below LANCE's 97.6% F1. The live question is no longer 'has anyone replicated LANCE' (no) but 'is the gap between 97.6% and 0.82-0.88 explained by LANCE's regex pre-filter + human-validation loop, by corpus difficulty, or by the metric difference (F1 vs precision-only)?' Answering it needs a head-to-head: run LANCE on CyberThreat-Eval's IoC set, or run a vanilla LLM on PRISM. CYCLE-21 UPDATE -- ONE OF THE THREE BRANCHES IS NOW CLOSED, THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT. The METRIC branch is effectively eliminated (see the fourth candidate_resolution): cycle 18 computed that reconciling the two sources by the F1-vs-precision difference alone would require IoC recall of 0.09-0.15, and cycle 21 recovered src-0007's own Section 4.3 verdict that IoC extraction is 'relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary' -- a characterisation no author would write over a recall of 0.09-0.15. The SYSTEM branch is strengthened but still unmeasured, and the CORPUS branch is exactly where cycle 9 left it: nothing in the base compares PRISM's 50 public threat reports against src-0007's unnamed company's internal workflow for difficulty, and no cycle has attempted it. STILL NO HEAD-TO-HEAD EXISTS. Cycle 21 searched the artefact release rather than the literature, so the head-to-head search itself was not re-run this cycle -- but note carry-forward [6]: forward-citation sweeps have failed on two different arXiv ids and that is unavailable infrastructure, not an unsearched direction.

Does the result generalize beyond the 4 indicator types tested (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes) to e.g. registry keys, mutexes, YARA/Sigma rules? Cycle 9 note: src-0007 does NOT extend the coverage -- its ground truth is described as 'file hashes, IP addresses, or domain names'. Two independent benchmarks now both confine themselves to the same small family of network/file indicators, which suggests the field has not measured the harder indicator types at all rather than that they were measured and found comparable. CYCLE-21 UPDATE, AND THE COVERAGE IS NARROWER THAN RECORDED, NOT EQUAL. A verbatim pull of src-0007's annotation sentence gives 'concrete, structured artifacts--such as file hashes, IP addresses, or domain names'. URLs are NOT named. So src-0007 covers THREE indicator types against src-0003's four, and the two benchmarks' indicator families are not even coextensive with each other, let alone extended beyond the network/file family. The direction of the cycle-9 note is confirmed and its scope tightened: registry keys, mutexes and YARA/Sigma rules remain entirely unmeasured by any source in this base.

How much of LANCE's gain over IoC Searcher/AlienVault OTX/VirusTotal comes from the LLM component specifically vs. the regex pre-filtering and human-validation loop around it? Cycle 9 gives the first indirect evidence: src-0007's Table 4 is explicitly headed 'Vanilla LLMs' and a bare LLM there reaches only 0.82-0.85 precision on expert-annotated real-world data, which is consistent with (though it does not prove) the LLM component alone not being what delivers high-90s performance. Confounded by corpus and metric differences. CYCLE-21 UPDATE: THE METRIC CONFOUND IS NOW LIFTED FROM THIS QUESTION, THE CORPUS CONFOUND IS NOT, AND THE 'Vanilla LLMs' HEADING TURNS OUT TO BE WEAKER TEXTUAL EVIDENCE THAN NINE CYCLES OF NOTES HAVE ASSUMED. A whole-table pull confirms the caption verbatim as 'Performance Metrics for Vanilla LLMs by Task Category, Task, Metric, and Model' -- but two of the table's four columns are GPT-4o (FT) and GPT-4o-mini (FT), i.e. fine-tuned. 'Vanilla' therefore cannot mean 'not fine-tuned' in this paper's usage, and the only reading consistent with the columns is 'the LLM used directly, without an agentic or tool-scaffolded pipeline'. THE PAPER NEVER DEFINES THE TERM. That reading is an inference from column headers, not a quotation, and the whole system-confound argument rests on it. It should be labelled as an inference everywhere it is used. Note this cuts BOTH ways: it is still the best available textual evidence that src-0007 measures an unscaffolded system, and it is weaker evidence than 'explicitly headed' implies.

LARGELY ANSWERED AT CYCLE 21, RESIDUE STATED PRECISELY. Original (cycle 9): src-0007 reports precision only for IoC extraction, with no recall or F1 and no stated reason -- can recall/F1 be recovered from the released benchmark? ANSWERED, THREE PARTS. (a) NO, the number is not recoverable from the release: src-0017 shows stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/ holds data, eval, example and README.md, and the only prediction file anywhere is example/prediction/manual_ioc_predictions.json, a manual worked example. The paper's four model outputs are not published, so recall could only be obtained by re-running GPT-4o, o3-mini and the two fine-tunes. (b) BUT THE OMISSION IS NOW EXPLAINED AS A CHOICE, NOT A LIMIT: the released evaluator eval_ioc.py computes recall in the same function as precision and prints it on the very next line, with no code path that yields one without the other, and the sub-README treats recall as a first-class benchmark metric. src-0007 published the first line of that output and withheld the second. (c) The paper is NOT silent about recall either -- Section 4.3 reads 'In the TI drafting stage, the extraction of IoCs is relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary.' It still states no reason for the omission. RESIDUE, GENUINELY STILL OPEN: the numeric value; and whether the ground truth is EXHAUSTIVE per article, which src-0017's README never states -- recall against a non-exhaustive ground truth would not be comparable to recall against PRISM regardless. The README's displayed 'Overall Recall: 0.6667' is illustrative quick-start output against the manual example file and is NOT a measurement; no cycle may cite it. Unexplored: the HuggingFace mirror (huggingface.co/datasets/xse/CyberThreat-Eval) was not fetched and is where model outputs would live if they are released at all.

NEW (cycle 9): src-0008 shows LLM recovery of plaintext indicators from code is ~100% but collapses to ~0-1% under XOR/AES-256 concealment. Report-based extraction has never been evaluated under an adversarial threat model at all -- if report authors or adversaries defang/encode indicators (a routine practice in published reporting), does extraction accuracy degrade similarly? No source measures this. CYCLE-21: UNTOUCHED. This cycle did not reach this question and nothing found bears on it. It remains the issue's only wholly unaddressed question and is now the strongest candidate for a future T1's collection target, since no source in the base measures it and none is known to exist. CYCLE-35 RELABEL, ctr-0007 steps (ii) and (iii), APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED -- the text above stands but its two src-0008 figures are mis-labelled. The '~100%' and the '~0-1%' quoted above are FIGURE-DERIVED AND NOT TEXT-VERIFIED: src-0008's per-phase P0-P12 breakdown exists ONLY inside Figure 2 (caption 'LLM detection outcomes across all obfuscation phases (P0-P12)'), confirmed by two fetches instructed to write CANNOT READ rather than infer. What the body text supports verbatim is qualitative only: 'near-complete failure', 'encrypted IoCs become effectively opaque', 'once the code is encrypted, detection of IoCs remains essentially zero for all models'. A METRIC AMBIGUITY also travels with any src-0008 percentage: the paper defines detection rate twice, incompatibly -- body 'Detection rate, i.e., the proportion of samples in which the model correctly identifies the presence of an IoC' against Table 6's caption 'DR reflects the detection rate, i.e., ratio of YES an answers' -- so whether '~100%' means correctly-identified or answered-YES is UNDETERMINED BY THE PAPER. AND THE '~100%' IS NOT TRUE OF ALL FIVE MODELS: it holds for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, while Cohere degrades progressively under purely syntactic obfuscation (1%/2%/5% misses at P1-P3, then 65% misses plus 35% Don't Know at P4). NONE OF THIS WEAKENS THE QUESTION ITSELF, which is about report-based extraction under an adversarial threat model and remains WHOLLY UNADDRESSED IN ITS TWENTY-SIXTH CYCLE. CYCLE-52 QUALIFICATION OF THE CYCLE-35 RELABEL, ctr-0019 STEP (ii), APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED. The relabel's sentence 'AND THE ~100% IS NOT TRUE OF ALL FIVE MODELS' IS CORRECT AT P1-P4 AND IS WRONG AT P0. The Results paragraph's FIRST sentence, missed by cycles 29 and 35 and recovered by cycle 51's G2, reads verbatim: 'all evaluated LLMs achieve 100% detection when the IoC appears in plain text'. At the unobfuscated baseline P0 the paper puts ALL FIVE evaluated models, Cohere included, at 100%; Cohere's degradation starts at P1. So the four-versus-one split belongs to P1-P4 only. The paper states no P0-specific per-model figure for Cohere other than that collective sentence (asked directly at cycle 51, answered ABSENT). NOTE THE DIRECTION OF THIS QUALIFICATION AS IT BEARS ON THIS QUESTION: the P0 sentence makes the plaintext-recovery baseline UNIFORM across models, which SHARPENS rather than blunts the adversarial question -- if every model reads a plaintext indicator perfectly and the divergence appears only once a transformation is applied, then the interesting quantity really is the degradation curve under transformation, which for NARRATIVE REPORTS (defanging, encoding, homoglyphs, screenshots) nobody has measured. THE QUESTION ITSELF IS STILL WHOLLY UNADDRESSED, now in its TWENTY-SEVENTH CYCLE, and cycle 52 did not attempt it: no source in this base measures it, so it is a T1 collection target and a T3 cannot discharge it.

NEW (cycle 21), and it undercuts the comparability of the 0.8240 precision figure itself rather than only the missing recall. src-0017's evaluator matches predicted IoCs to ground truth with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions -- its own comments read 'For prediction, if pred.lower() in ground truth or ground truth in pred' alongside 'Exact match'. A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality, so src-0007's precision is not a strict-match figure and may not be commensurable with src-0003's F1 even once a recall number exists. The full test() function body was not transcribed, so the exact conditions under which each rule fires are unknown. Resolving this needs the remainder of eval_ioc.py read, and ideally src-0003's own matching rule read alongside it -- a cheap, well-specified, high-value next step that requires no new search.

[6] NEW (cycle 35). THIS SUPERSEDES open_questions[5] ABOVE, WHICH IS LEFT IN PLACE PER THE APPEND-ONLY SPIRIT BUT IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. This discharges step (i) of ctr-0004, open since cycle 27. open_questions[5] says src-0017's evaluator matches 'with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions'. IT DOES NOT. The EXECUTING code in stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/eval/eval_ioc.py is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, verbatim: 'true_positives = sum(any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set) for pred in pred_list)', with 'false_positives = len(pred_list) - true_positives' and 'false_negatives = sum(not any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for pred in pred_list) for gt in gt_set)'. The two-directional variant and the exact-match variant are EACH ENCLOSED IN A TRIPLE-QUOTED STRING LITERAL and never execute; the comment lines cycle 21 quoted are the headers standing above those dead blocks. THE SOURCE STATES THE SAME RULE IN ITS OWN PROSE -- IoC sub-README, verbatim: 'A prediction is considered a True Positive (TP) if pred.lower() in gt.lower() for any ground truth IOC from the same source'. Code and documentation agree with each other and against what this issue said. THE CONSEQUENCE IS AN ASYMMETRIC BIAS, NOT A ONE-WAY ONE. The rule is LENIENT toward short or fragmentary predictions, since any prediction that is a substring of a longer ground-truth entry scores TP. It is STRICT against verbose predictions, since a prediction containing the ground-truth IoC plus surrounding text scores a FALSE POSITIVE -- and that is the characteristic failure mode of a free-form LLM extractor, i.e. exactly the case the dead two-directional block would have scored TP. A verbose-but-correct prediction is moreover penalised TWICE, as a false positive AND as a false negative, because the ground-truth entry it contains is simultaneously left unmatched by the false_negatives line above. So the limitation recorded at src-0017.md, that 'A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality', is HALF RIGHT and must never be repeated unqualified: relative to strict equality this matcher INFLATES on one axis and DEFLATES on the other, and THE NET SIGN IS UNKNOWN because it is the difference of two unmeasured quantities. PARTIAL MITIGATION, recorded so the deflation is not over-read: both sides pass through the same normalisation chain (transcribed verbatim in ctr-0004), which strips defanging -- hxxp to http, bracket removal -- and truncates at the first ' - ' separator, so the commonest verbose-prediction artefacts in CTI text are normalised away BEFORE matching. What survives the chain as verbose FP is free prose around the indicator, and a URL-with-path predicted against a bare-domain ground truth. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN: the net sign and magnitude of the bias. It cannot be recovered without the per-model prediction files, which are now confirmed ABSENT from both release mirrors -- see open_questions[7].

[7] NEW (cycle 35), AND IT CLOSES THE CHEAPEST REMAINING ROUTE ON ctr-0001 RATHER THAN OPENING ONE. huggingface.co/datasets/xse/CyberThreat-Eval was named as the cheapest unexplored step in ctr-0001's cycle-21 update and in open_questions[3], and had never been fetched by any cycle. IT WAS FETCHED THIS CYCLE, THREE URL FORMS, AND THE PER-MODEL IoC PREDICTIONS ARE NOT THERE. The HuggingFace tree API (huggingface.co/api/datasets/xse/CyberThreat-Eval/tree/main?recursive=true) returns a COMPLETE 52-file listing WITH BYTE SIZES, so this is an authoritative absence and not a truncated render. The only prediction artefact anywhere under the IoC task is stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/example/prediction/manual_ioc_predictions.json at 1,298 bytes -- the manual worked example already known from the GitHub mirror, far too small to be four models' output over 1,310 IoCs. The only other model-named file in the whole repository is stage3_ti_drafting/score_evaluation/example/test_output/gpt-4o.json at 8,571 bytes, which belongs to the threat-actor/root-cause SCORING task and is likewise an example. THE MIRROR IS THE SAME REPOSITORY, NOT A SUPERSET: stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/data/TTP_Mapping.csv is 1,083,078 bytes, byte-for-byte the size cycle 31 recorded from GitHub. CONSEQUENCE: src-0007's unreported IoC recall is NOT obtainable from any released artefact, and the only remaining route is re-running GPT-4o, o3-mini and the two fine-tunes, which is outside this loop's means. ctr-0001's METRIC confound therefore stays 'eliminated by argument' and can no longer be 'settled by number' from the release. SECOND QUESTION ASKED AND ANSWERED IN THE NEGATIVE: whether the ground truth is stated to be EXHAUSTIVE per article. ABSENT, confirmed at two URL forms (the rendered dataset card and the raw README at /resolve/main/README.md), consistent with the IoC sub-README read whole at cycle 27. So even if a recall number existed it would be recall against a ground truth of unstated completeness, which is not comparable with PRISM's regardless -- this residue of open_questions[3] is now CONFIRMED OPEN AT SOURCE rather than merely suspected, and it is a permanent limit on the comparison, not a fetch away from closing.

[8] NEW (cycle 52), AND IT IS THE FIRST OPEN QUESTION IN THIS ISSUE ABOUT THE src-0003 SIDE OF THE COMPARISON RATHER THAN THE src-0007 SIDE. Cycle 52 CLOSED two things about src-0003 and OPENED one. CLOSED (i): the strings '76%' and '72%' -- the IoC Searcher+whitelist and AlienVault OTX baseline F1 values carried at status SUPPORTED in candidate_resolutions[0] -- are ABSENT from src-0003's body text at BOTH arxiv.org/html/2506.11325v1 and v2, on renderings that were asked directly whether they could see Section 5.1.1 (both YES) and whether they were truncated (v1 NO, v2 only mid-References). They are FIGURE-6-DERIVED and may never be cited as reported values. CLOSED (ii): the 86% IS text-stated, verbatim 'VirusTotal with threshold 1 performs reasonably well, achieving an average F1 score of 86%, with consistent scores across indicator types', so cycle 22's blanket figure-only ruling was half wrong and ctr-0014 is discharged. STILL OPEN AND NOW FORMALLY TRACKED AS ctr-0020: WHAT QUANTITY, AND OVER WHICH ANALYSTS, IS src-0003's 43% MEASURED? The paper states it three ways -- 'a 43% drop in the average and median time the analysts spent on a report' (the only one attached to a measurement), 'a 43% reduction in parsing time compared to manual-only workflows', and 'reduces analysts work factor by 43% compared to manual annotation, as demonstrated in our evaluation with six analysts' -- while the state calls it 'junior analysts manual annotation time', a fourth wording that appears nowhere in the paper and narrows a population the source leaves broad (five junior analysts PLUS one senior). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is cheap: fetch the HITL evaluation section end to end and see whether the timing measurement is restricted to the five juniors. This is the ONLY analyst-productivity number in this base and it sits inside a SUPPORTED candidate, so the scope of its population is load-bearing. A SECOND, SMALLER RESIDUE: src-0003 is an UNREVIEWED PREPRINT WITH NO VENUE (no 'Comments:' and no 'Journal reference:' line on arxiv.org/abs/2506.11325), which no cycle knew for forty-two cycles and which bears on how much weight the 97.6% -- the highest number in this base and one side of ctr-0001 -- should carry against src-0007, whose TMLR acceptance is recorded on its arXiv abstract page but STILL not entered in this base after fifteen cycles of being flagged.

candidate_resolutions.summary: For narrow, mechanical IoC extraction (as opposed to open-ended CTI reasoning), a hybrid regex+LLM+human-validation pipeline (LANCE) reached 97.6% F1 against the manually-validated PRISM benchmark, substantially outperforming legacy tools (IoC Searcher+whitelist 76%, AlienVault OTX 72%, VirusTotal@threshold=1 86%) and also improving downstream analyst speed (43% less annotation time) and downstream model training data quality (+6% F1). This is a single-study result from the benchmark's own authors, not yet independently replicated. [FOUR INLINE QUALIFICATIONS APPENDED AT CYCLE 52, T3. THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS RETAINED UNALTERED SO THE CORRECTION IS AUDITABLE; DO NOT CITE IT WITHOUT THESE. (a) TWO OF THE THREE BASELINE FIGURES ARE FIGURE-DERIVED, NOT REPORTED VALUES. Cycle 52 settled ctr-0014 step (iii), which cycle 43 left undecided: the strings '76%' and '72%' are ABSENT from the paper's body text at BOTH arxiv.org/html/2506.11325v1 and arxiv.org/html/2506.11325v2, on renderings that were asked directly whether they could see Section 5.1.1 (both YES) and whether they were truncated (v1: NO; v2: only mid-References at [32]). Those two values exist only inside Figure 6 and MUST be cited as FIGURE-DERIVED AND NOT TEXT-VERIFIED. The ordering 86 > 76 > 72 is separately supported by the prose and is untouched. (b) THE 86% IS TEXT-STATED AND IS THE ONE BASELINE THAT SURVIVES AS A REPORTED VALUE, verbatim in Section 5.1.1: 'VirusTotal with threshold 1 performs reasonably well, achieving an average F1 score of 86%, with consistent scores across indicator types.' (c) '43% LESS ANNOTATION TIME' MATCHES NONE OF THE PAPER'S THREE WORDINGS AND OVER-ATTRIBUTES THE POPULATION -- see ctr-0020, opened this cycle. The measurement-bearing sentence is 'From the results of those measurements, we see a 43% drop in the average and median time the analysts spent on a report'; the paper also says 'a 43% reduction in parsing time compared to manual-only workflows' and, in the abstract, 'reduces analysts work factor by 43% compared to manual annotation, as demonstrated in our evaluation with six analysts'. Parsing time, work factor and time-spent-on-a-report are not stated by the paper to be the same quantity, and the evaluation population is five junior analysts PLUS one senior, not junior analysts alone. Cite sentence (1) or cite none. (d) PROVENANCE, first recorded in this base at cycle 52 from cycle 43's check: src-0003 is an UNREVIEWED PREPRINT WITH NO VENUE -- arxiv.org/abs/2506.11325 carries no 'Comments:' and no 'Journal reference:' line. Since this candidate's 97.6% is the highest number in this base and one side of ctr-0001, that matters to how much weight it carries. NOTE also key_claims[4] of src-0003 in index.json: the 97.6% is a CLASSIFICATION score over a regex-extracted candidate set, not free-form extraction.]

ADDED cycle 9. A second, fully independent measurement of LLM IoC extraction from real-world CTI material now exists: CyberThreat-Eval (src-0007; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026), an expert-annotated benchmark built from a production CTI workflow covering 1310 IoCs, reports vanilla-LLM extraction precision of 0.8240 (GPT-4o), 0.8503 (o3-mini), 0.8846 (fine-tuned GPT-4o) and 0.6944 (fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini). Read narrowly, this establishes that a bare LLM prompted to extract indicators from real analyst-workflow material errs on roughly 1 in 6 of the indicators it emits -- materially short of the near-solved impression left by src-0003's 97.6% F1, and short of even the 86% VirusTotal@threshold=1 baseline src-0003 reports. It does NOT refute src-0003, because it measures a different system (no regex pre-filter, no human validation loop), on a different corpus, with a different metric (precision only; no recall or F1 given). See contradiction ctr-0001, opened this cycle rather than resolved either way.

ADDED cycle 9, deliberately weak status. Candidate synthesis: the reliability of mechanical IoC extraction is set mainly by the scaffolding around the model (regex pre-filtering, whitelisting, human validation) rather than by the LLM itself, which is why src-0003's scaffolded pipeline reports 97.6% F1 while src-0007's 'Vanilla LLMs' reach 0.82-0.88 precision and src-0008 finds an unscaffolded LLM recovers plaintext indicators ~100% of the time but is defeated entirely by encryption it has no tooling for. [SENTENCE CORRECTED AT CYCLE 35, ctr-0007 step (i) -- THE PRECEDING CLAUSE ABOUT src-0008 IS FALSE AND IS RETAINED ONLY SO THE CORRECTION IS AUDITABLE; DO NOT CITE IT. src-0008 evaluates FIVE models, not one and not four, and ENCRYPTION IS NOT THE BOUNDARY FOR ALL OF THEM. Body text verbatim: 'ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok achieve 100% across all four phases without reporting uncertainties' -- and immediately after it -- 'Cohere, however, shows progressive degradation: 1% missed detections in P1, 2% in P2, 5% in P3, and in P4, 65% misses plus 35% explicit Don't Know responses'. Phases P1-P4 contain NO CRYPTOGRAPHY: Table 3 defines them verbatim as '1. Base64 encoding', '2. Identifier obfuscation', '3. Dead code injection', '4. Structural obfuscation'. So one of five models loses roughly two thirds of its detections under PURELY SYNTACTIC transformation that leaves the indicator in plain text. THE CORRECT STATEMENT IS: four of src-0008's five models recover plaintext indicators at 100% through four levels of syntactic obfuscation and then fail near-completely once the indicator is encrypted, while the fifth degrades progressively under syntactic obfuscation alone. TWO CITATION CONSTRAINTS TRAVEL WITH ANY src-0008 PERCENTAGE USED HERE, per ctr-0007 steps (ii) and (iii). (a) FIGURE-DERIVED: the per-phase P0-P12 breakdown exists ONLY inside Figure 2, confirmed by two fetches instructed to write CANNOT READ rather than infer, so the '~0-1%' and '~95%+ misses' figures are FIGURE-DERIVED AND NOT TEXT-VERIFIED; what the body text supports verbatim is qualitative only ('near-complete failure', 'encrypted IoCs become effectively opaque'). (b) METRIC AMBIGUITY: the paper defines its own detection rate twice, incompatibly -- body 'Detection rate, i.e., the proportion of samples in which the model correctly identifies the presence of an IoC' against Table 6's caption 'DR reflects the detection rate, i.e., ratio of YES an answers' -- and a ratio of YES answers does not require correctness, so whether '100% detection' means correctly-identified or answered-YES is UNDETERMINED BY THE PAPER.] This is a plausible reading of three sources that were never designed to be compared, and no source tests it directly -- it is recorded as proposed so a later cycle can attack it, NOT as a finding. CYCLE-21 ATTACKED IT AND IT SURVIVES, BUT IT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 'proposed'. What changed: the competing explanation for the same evidence -- that the src-0003/src-0007 gap is a metric artefact -- is now effectively eliminated (see the fourth candidate_resolution), which removes the main rival reading and leaves scaffolding as the live explanation. What did NOT change: no source tests this claim directly, no head-to-head exists, the corpus confound is completely unaddressed, and the 'Vanilla LLMs' heading that anchors the claim turns out to be an inference rather than a definition (see open_questions). Eliminating one rival explanation is not the same as demonstrating a causal claim about scaffolding, and promoting on that basis would be exactly the over-reach this candidate was created to resist. It stays 'proposed'. CYCLE-35 DECISION ON ctr-0007's OPEN QUESTION, WHICH CYCLE 29 EXPLICITLY DECLINED TO ANSWER. The question put was: does large model-side variance under PURELY SYNTACTIC noise SUPPORT the scaffolding hypothesis (regex pre-filtering and whitelisting are indifferent to dead-code injection and control-flow flattening, so scaffolding is what buys robustness) or UNDERCUT it (the variance is model-side, i.e. the model is exactly what varies)? I DECIDE THAT IT CUTS BOTH WAYS, AND THE CANDIDATE STAYS 'proposed' -- but that is a decision with content, not a refusal to decide, because the two readings turn out to be about DIFFERENT PROPOSITIONS and both can be true at once. (1) THE UNDERCUTTING READING IS THE STRONGER OF THE TWO ON THIS EVIDENCE. Five models, one corpus, one task, NO scaffolding on any arm, and a spread running from 100% to roughly 35% at P4. If the model were not what sets reliability, that spread could not exist. Model identity is therefore a large variance component under unscaffolded conditions, which is a direct qualification of a hypothesis whose whole content is that reliability is set 'mainly by the scaffolding around the model rather than by the LLM itself'. (2) THE SUPPORTING READING IS REAL BUT IS A COUNTERFACTUAL, NOT A MEASUREMENT. It is true that a regex extractor would be indifferent to dead-code injection and structural obfuscation, since those transformations leave the indicator in plain text; so scaffolding WOULD plausibly have erased Cohere's degradation.
