But src-0008 RUNS NO SCAFFOLDED ARM, so this is an inference about an experiment nobody performed, and it must not be entered as evidence. (3) THE DECISIVE POINT, AND IT IS WHY NEITHER READING PROMOTES OR DEMOTES THE CANDIDATE: src-0008 CANNOT ADJUDICATE THIS HYPOTHESIS AT ALL. Its task is recovering a planted indicator from JavaScript SOURCE CODE under adversarial transformation; this candidate is about extracting indicators from NARRATIVE THREAT REPORTS. The scope limit was already recorded at src-0008 key_claims[2] and this cycle enforces it. src-0008's role in this candidate is accordingly DEMOTED from evidence-for-the-boundary to ILLUSTRATION ONLY, and a weak one, further weakened by the metric ambiguity and the image-locked per-phase figures noted above. src-0008 IS RETAINED in the evidence list because removing it would erase the trail, NOT because it supports the claim. NET EFFECT ON THE CANDIDATE'S STANDING: the hypothesis now rests on the src-0003-versus-src-0007 contrast alone, i.e. on two sources that were never designed to be compared, with the corpus confound untouched and the 'Vanilla LLMs' anchor known to be an inference. That is WEAKER than the position cycle 21 left it in, since cycle 21's ground for keeping it alive was that eliminating the metric rival left scaffolding as the live explanation, and this cycle adds a second live explanation -- MODEL IDENTITY -- that no cycle had put on the board. A future cycle should treat 'model choice sets the floor, scaffolding sets the ceiling' as the compatible third reading and test it, rather than treating scaffolding and model as rivals. CYCLE-52 QUALIFICATION OF THE CYCLE-35 CORRECTION ABOVE, ctr-0019 STEP (ii). THE CYCLE-35 CORRECTION IS RETAINED UNALTERED AND IS NOT WITHDRAWN, BUT ITS SPAN IS WRONG AT ONE PHASE. Its 'CORRECT STATEMENT' sentence says four of five models recover plaintext indicators at 100% through four levels of syntactic obfuscation while the fifth degrades. THAT HOLDS AT P1-P4 AND DOES NOT HOLD AT P0. The Results paragraph's FIRST sentence, which no cycle recorded until cycle 51's G2, reads verbatim: 'all evaluated LLMs achieve 100% detection when the IoC appears in plain text'. At the unobfuscated baseline the paper puts ALL FIVE models, Cohere included, at 100%; Cohere's degradation begins at P1. Cycles 29 and 35 quoted the THIRD and FOURTH sentences of that paragraph and missed the FIRST. The paper states NO P0-specific per-model figure for Cohere other than that collective sentence (asked directly at cycle 51, answered ABSENT). AND ctr-0019 STEP (iii), RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THIS IS WHERE ctr-0007 IS RELIED ON: ctr-0007's verdict sentence -- that 'the stored claim's generalisation to current LLMs is contradicted by the paper it cites' -- LOCATED THE DEFECT IN THE WRONG WORDS. On the narrowest reading of src-0008.md key claim 1's headline sentence, the paper asserts that generalisation in its own words, for all five models, at P0. The actual defect is the CONFLATION OF P0 WITH P1-P4 under one four-model span. THIS DOES NOT REINSTATE src-0008.md KEY CLAIM 1; it relocates the error, and the relocation must travel wherever ctr-0007 is cited. SUBSTANTIVE EFFECT ON THE CYCLE-35 DECISION ABOVE: IT STRENGTHENS IT. Cycle 35's undercutting argument -- that a 100%-to-~35% spread across five unscaffolded arms on one corpus proves model identity is a large variance component -- was missing a baseline control. The omitted P0 sentence supplies it: because all five models sit at 100% at P0, the whole P1-P4 divergence is attributable to the transformation interacting with model identity rather than to any difference in baseline extraction capability. THE CANDIDATE'S STATUS IS UNCHANGED at 'proposed' and src-0008 remains ILLUSTRATION ONLY under cycle 35's scope ruling, since src-0008's task is JavaScript SOURCE CODE and this candidate concerns NARRATIVE THREAT REPORTS. The two citation constraints (a) and (b) above are likewise unchanged: the P0 sentence is TEXT-verified, but the metric ambiguity still means '100% detection' may mean correctly-identified or answered-YES, undetermined by the paper. ALSO APPENDED AT CYCLE 52, bearing on the src-0003 side of this candidate's contrast: two of src-0003's three baseline figures (76%, 72%) are now CONFIRMED absent from the body text at both v1 and v2 and are FIGURE-DERIVED, the 86% is text-stated, and src-0003 is an UNREVIEWED PREPRINT WITH NO VENUE -- see candidate_resolutions[0] and ctr-0014, discharged this cycle.

ADDED cycle 21, and this is the cycle's substantive result. THE METRIC CONFOUND CANNOT ACCOUNT FOR THE src-0003 / src-0007 GAP, so ctr-0001 does not dissolve into an artefact of comparing an F1 with a precision. Two independent lines converge. (1) ARITHMETIC (cycle 18): for src-0007's unreported IoC recall to drag an F1 down far enough to reconcile 97.6% with a precision of 0.82-0.88, recall would have to fall in the range 0.09-0.15. (2) THE AUTHORS' OWN VERDICT (cycle 21, newly recovered from Section 4.3 of arXiv 2603.09452v1, verbatim): 'In the TI drafting stage, the extraction of IoCs is relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary.' A team describing their own system's IoC extraction as 'relatively robust' with recall merely needing 'improvements' is not describing recall of 0.09-0.15 -- particularly when the same paper flatly calls the TTP task, at recall 0.1414-0.2270, 'a substantial challenge'. The paper's own contrast between the two tasks puts IoC recall well above the reconciling range. SUPPORTING CONTEXT from src-0017: the omission is not a measurement limitation but a reporting decision -- the released evaluator computes recall in the same function as precision and prints it on the next line. INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY: both textual legs come from the same author team, and src-0017 is the same team's artefact, so this rests on ONE independent measurement plus arithmetic over src-0003's published figure, not on two independent measurements. It is an ELIMINATIVE claim -- it rules a confound out; it does not establish what the gap IS. The SYSTEM and CORPUS confounds both remain live, and ctr-0001 accordingly stays OPEN. [CYCLE-35 ADDENDUM, EXECUTING ctr-0004 STEP (ii). THE HEADLINE ELIMINATIVE CLAIM SURVIVES AND IS NOW ON STRICTLY BETTER GROUND, BUT LEG (1) AS STATED ABOVE IS MIS-SCOPED AND IS RESTATED HERE; see ctr-0010, opened this cycle. NOTHING ABOVE IS DELETED.] (A) WHAT THE 0.09-0.15 FIGURE ACTUALLY IS. Leg (1) above says the range is what 'reconciling 97.6% with a precision of 0.82-0.88' would require. IT IS NOT. logs/cycle-018.md prints the derivation as a four-row table headed 'Solving 2PR/(P+R) for the unreported IoC recall at which each model's IoC F1 falls to its own derived TTP F1', with columns model / IoC precision / derived TTP F1 / crossover recall / actual TTP recall: GPT-4o 0.8240 / 0.2502 / 0.1475 / 0.2270; o3-mini 0.8503 / 0.2337 / 0.1354 / 0.1759; GPT-4o (FT) 0.8846 / 0.2082 / 0.1180 / 0.1846; GPT-4o-mini (FT) 0.6944 / 0.1572 / 0.0887 / 0.1414. So 0.09-0.15 is a WITHIN-src-0007 quantity -- the IoC recall at which src-0007's IoC task would score no better than src-0007's OWN TTP task -- and src-0003's 97.6% ENTERS IT NOWHERE. Cycle 18's own carry-forward [7] restated it as a src-0003 reconciliation and every downstream use in this graph and in scores.json inherited that restatement. The ARGUMENT cycle 18 built on it is untouched and remains good: every crossover sits BELOW that model's own TTP recall by a factor of 1.3-1.6, so IoC recall would have to be worse than TTP recall on a task the same authors call 'relatively robust' while calling TTP 'a substantial challenge'. (B) DOES THE ONE-DIRECTIONAL ASYMMETRY CHANGE THAT ARITHMETIC? NO, AND THE INSENSITIVITY IS DERIVED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The matcher enters only through P. Solving 2PR/(P+R) = F for R gives R = FP/(2P-F), whence dR/dP = -F squared / (2P-F) squared. For GPT-4o (F = 0.2502, P = 0.8240) that is -0.0626/1.9538 = -0.0320. A correction to P of a full 0.13 in either direction therefore moves the crossover recall by about 0.004. Worked at the extreme: if the matcher were deflating GPT-4o's precision all the way from 0.8240 to 0.9531, the crossover moves from 0.1475 to 0.1440. THE 0.09-0.15 RANGE IS ROBUST TO THE MATCHER ASYMMETRY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. (One second-order effect is noted and is neutral: the same one-directional rule deflates measured RECALL as well as measured precision, since a verbose-but-correct prediction is scored FP and FN together -- but the crossover threshold, the authors' Section 4.3 characterisation and eval_ioc.py's printed output are all in the SAME matcher-measured units, so the comparison is internally consistent.) (C) THE src-0003 RECONCILIATION, DONE PROPERLY FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND IT NEEDS NO RECALL VALUE AT ALL. F1 = 2PR/(P+R) is increasing in R, so for any system F1 <= 2P/(P+1). Setting 2P/(P+1) >= 0.976 gives 1.024P >= 0.976, i.e. P >= 0.9531. LANCE's published 97.6% F1 therefore ENTAILS a precision of at least 0.9531. That is a PRECISION, and src-0007's 0.8240-0.8846 are PRECISIONS, so the two sources can be compared like with like and the F1-versus-precision mismatch that defines ctr-0001's METRIC confound simply does not arise. THE METRIC CONFOUND IS ELIMINATED DEDUCTIVELY, not by a plausibility argument, and no value of src-0007's missing recall can revive it. MARGIN, AS REQUIRED: 0.9531 - 0.8846 = 0.069 against src-0007's BEST model, and 0.9531 - 0.8240 = 0.129 against vanilla GPT-4o. (D) WHAT THE ASYMMETRY DOES INSTEAD -- IT CREATES A FOURTH CONFOUND RATHER THAN REVIVING THE SECOND. Call it MATCHER. For it to close the 0.069 gap, src-0007's one-directional rule would have to be NET-DEFLATING its precision by 6.9 points, i.e. at least 6.9% of the fine-tuned model's emitted IoCs would have to be verbose-but-correct predictions scored FP. That is not absurd -- it is the characteristic free-form-LLM failure mode -- but three things stop it being asserted: the rule is simultaneously LENIENT toward fragmentary predictions so the net is a difference of two unmeasured quantities of unknown sign; the shared normalisation chain already strips defanging and truncates at ' - ', closing the commonest deflation channel before matching; and src-0003 NEVER STATES ITS OWN MATCHING RULE (src-0003.md line 141), so LANCE's entailed 0.9531 may itself be leniently scored and the correction could run either way on BOTH sides. (E) VERDICT ON THIS CANDIDATE'S STATUS. It stays 'supported' and it is NOT over-claimed in its headline: the METRIC confound cannot account for the gap, and after (C) that is a stronger result than when it was written. What is defective is its stated leg (1), which attributes to the 0.09-0.15 range a scope that range does not have; ctr-0010 records that rather than the edit being made silently. ctr-0001 STAYS OPEN, now against THREE live confounds -- SYSTEM (unmeasured), CORPUS (untouched) and MATCHER (new, and not settleable from any released artefact, per open_questions[7]).

issues.title: Beyond raw accuracy, are LLM-generated CTI outputs consistent across repeated queries and well-calibrated in stated confidence?
open_questions: ANSWERED AT CYCLE 25 IN THE NEGATIVE, AND RESTATED AS WHAT REMAINS. src-0001's Table 6 was pulled whole for the first time at cycle 25 (caption verbatim: 'ECE and BS with gpt4o for information generation and extraction'). It is gpt4o-ONLY and complete at NINE rows -- extraction campaign/APT/CVE/attack vector, generation goals/labels/country/CVE/attack vector -- across all three paradigms; the base had stored only five of those rows. The paper reports NO ECE or Brier figure for gemini-1.5-pro-latest or mistral-large-2 ANYWHERE, so the gpt4o-specificity question cannot be settled from this source at all. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: whether the fine-tuning-can-worsen-calibration pattern is gpt4o-specific now requires a NEW measurement of proper-scoring calibration on a CTI task for a non-gpt4o model, and no such measurement exists in this base or was found by cycle 25's searches.

STILL FULLY OPEN, AND CYCLE 25 WIDENED RATHER THAN NARROWED IT. None of src-0001's 3 tested models (gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, mistral-large-2) overlaps src-0002's (GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo, Gemini-1.5, LLAMA3-70B/8B) or src-0005's lists -- would the consistency/calibration findings replicate on the specific models shown to struggle with ATT&CK mapping and attribution in those benchmarks? src-0018, added this cycle, does NOT answer it either: its five models (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus 4.5) overlap NO list in this base. So the base now has CTI-task consistency evidence on two disjoint model sets a generation apart, and zero per-model replication on any single model.

Does the multi-dimensional reliability framing (accuracy + consistency + calibration) proposed in src-0001 apply equally across the other CTI sub-tasks measured in src-0002/src-0005 (MCQ, RCM, ATE, TAA, malware analysis), or was it only measured in src-0001's own information-extraction/-generation evaluation setting?

NARROWED AT CYCLE 25, STILL OPEN. Fine-tuning and few-shot were both shown to sometimes worsen accuracy and calibration (gpt4o APT-extraction P/R 0.87->0.68 after fine-tuning; CVE-generation ECE 0.15->0.91, both re-verified exact this cycle) -- is this degradation specific to small fine-tuning dataset size / overfitting, or a general risk for CTI fine-tuning regardless of data volume? WHAT CYCLE 25 ESTABLISHED: the paper NOWHERE attributes the degradation to dataset size or overfitting (checked explicitly), so it offers no answer, and the only sentence bearing on the fine-tuning set size came back ELIDED from the fetch ('We randomly select 70% of the dataset...70% to the few-shot examples section and fine-tuning') and is therefore NOT verbatim-captured. Two concrete next steps: re-pull that split sentence verbatim, and note that the fine-tuning pool is bounded above by 350 reports either way, which makes small-data overfitting a live but unconfirmed explanation. === CYCLE 39: THE NAMED UNDONE STEP IS DISCHARGED, THE BOUND CYCLE 25 RECORDED WAS WRONG, AND THE UNDERLYING QUESTION NARROWS BUT STAYS OPEN. The split passage is now captured WHOLE AND UNELIDED, identical from two URL forms (arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and the unversioned render, which is v4), verbatim: 'Dataset division. We randomly select 70% of the dataset, thus mimicking the splitting which is typical of ML and DL model validations. In ML and DL, the splitting would have been in training, validation, and testing respectively in portions of 70%, 20%, and 10%. Since we do not train from scratch our model we assign 70% to the few-shot examples section and fine-tuning and 30% for the testing. We employ this division to avoid overfitting both for fine-tuning and for few-shot learning, if the few-shot examples are gathered directly from the dataset on which testing is conducted.' CORRECTION TO CYCLE 25: the fine-tuning pool is NOT bounded above by 350 reports. It is bounded by 70% of 350 = 245 reports (AGENT-DERIVED; the paper prints only '# of reports: 350' and the percentages), and that 245 is SHARED with the few-shot example pool, so fine-tuning alone used at most 245 and possibly far fewer. Test set is 30% = 105 reports (AGENT-DERIVED). THE EXACT NUMBER OF REPORTS USED FOR FINE-TUNING IS ABSENT, confirmed against two URL forms. SO IS THE ENTIRE FINE-TUNING SETUP: no hyperparameters, no epoch count, no learning rate, no endpoint, no fine-tuning-set size appear anywhere in the paper, confirmed ABSENT by two fetches on two URL forms, each permitted to answer ABSENT. This is a real reporting limitation of src-0001 and had never been recorded. CYCLE 25's 'the paper NOWHERE attributes the degradation to dataset size or overfitting' is CONFIRMED, but it must be scoped more precisely than cycle 25 scoped it: the word 'overfitting' DOES occur in the paper, twice, and both occurrences are about the SPLIT DESIGN rather than about the observed degradation -- the sentence above, and 'To control for prompt overfitting ... we evaluate the LLMs on the part of the dataset from which we do not gather any few-shot examples'. The paper invokes overfitting only as something its design controls FOR, never as an explanation of what it measured, and that control is asserted rather than measured. WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS OPEN: whether the post-fine-tuning calibration collapse is a small-data or overfitting artefact CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM src-0001 AT ALL, because the paper reports neither the fine-tuning set size nor any fine-tuning configuration. A 245-report ceiling is small in absolute terms for fine-tuning, so a small-data explanation is AVAILABLE but remains UNTESTED AND UNASSERTED. Answering this now requires a source that fine-tunes on CTI at more than one data volume and reports calibration at each; no such source is in this base.

NEW AT CYCLE 25, AND THE CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE ITEM ON THIS LIST. Every quantitative artefact in src-0018 is an IMAGE and none of its numbers is recoverable by this agent's fetch tooling: the table 'LLM decision consistency' (five models x {is_compromised, attack_stage} x {% of IOCs with P_o < 1, D-bar_o}), the chart 'Abstention error rates' (FDR/FNR per model), and the charts 'Selective IOC extraction performance' and 'Value assignment performance'. Two fetches instructed to answer 'IMAGE - CANNOT READ' rather than infer both did so. Until those cells are read, src-0018 supports DIRECTION only and supplies no magnitude to compare against src-0001's CI widths of 0.02 (extraction) and 0.06 (generation). Is there another route -- a companion paper, a conference talk, a PDF version, or alt-text? Cycle 25 searched for an arXiv companion by Milenkoski and Cirstea and found none.

NEW AT CYCLE 25. Does ANY source measure proper-scoring confidence calibration (ECE, Brier, reliability diagrams) on a CTI task other than src-0001? Cycle 25 ran three targeted searches and found none. Two leads were positively KILLED rather than left dangling: CTIArena (arXiv 2510.11974, Cheng/Liu/Li/Song/Gao, Virginia Tech and UC Berkeley; 9 CTI tasks, 10 models) was fetched and measures NEITHER repeat-query consistency NOR calibration/abstention, so it is not a candidate for this issue and should not be re-proposed for it; and no arXiv companion exists for src-0018. The calibration half of this issue therefore remains SINGLE-SOURCE on CTI (src-0001 alone) even though the consistency half is now two-source. === CYCLE 39 SPENT NO SEARCH BUDGET ON THIS AND IT IS UNCHANGED. Cycle 39's four fetches all went to the ctr-0003 resolution and the G2, which was the right call given ctr-0003 had been open fourteen cycles, but it means this question has now gone fourteen cycles without a new search. IT REMAINS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM ON THIS LIST for the reason cycle 36 gave and cycles 37 and 39 endorse: a second CTI-task ECE/Brier source is the single measurement that would let a T4 move this issue off 2, because the level-3 bar requires the PRIMARY candidate -- the one answering BOTH conjuncts of the title -- to have two independent sources, and that candidate rests on src-0001 alone. Do NOT re-propose CTIArena (arXiv 2510.11974); cycle 25 killed it at source. CYCLE 39 ADDS A REASON THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT DID BEFORE: the calibration leg is not merely single-source, it is single-source, single-model (gpt4o only) and now, per the new open_question below, INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT BETWEEN ITS TWO METRICS. A second source would be doing more work than simple corroboration.

NEW AT CYCLE 39, RAISED BY THE ctr-0003 RESOLUTION AND NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THIS BASE. src-0001's Table 6 reports ECE and Brier Score side by side and the paper defines them identically, verbatim: 'The ECE and BS, are two measures of calibration that quantify the deviation from perfect calibration.' BUT THE TWO METRICS ORDER THE TWO TASK FAMILIES DIFFERENTLY. On family means derived by cycle 39 from the printed cells (all AGENT-DERIVED, not printed), generation is worse than extraction on ECE at all three paradigms (0.278 vs 0.205 zero-shot, 0.320 vs 0.2425 few-shot, 0.538 vs 0.295 fine-tuned) but on Brier the gap is nil at zero-shot (0.304 vs 0.2975) and REVERSED at few-shot (0.294 vs 0.3225). A single row disagrees outright: extraction attack vector is the best-calibrated extraction cell on zero-shot ECE (0.13) and the worst on zero-shot BS (0.46). THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHICH METRIC SHOULD GOVERN A CALIBRATION CLAIM ON CTI, AND WHY. The paper does not distinguish them, offers no reliability diagram, and never comments on the divergence; this base has no source that discusses ECE-versus-Brier behaviour at all. An answer needs either a methodological source on proper scoring rules versus binned calibration error, or a CTI source reporting both metrics with a stated preference. UNTIL THEN, NO CYCLE MAY STATE AN EXTRACTION-VERSUS-GENERATION CALIBRATION GRADIENT WITHOUT NAMING THE METRIC IT HOLDS ON, and the only paradigm at which it holds on BOTH metrics is fine-tuning. This bears directly on extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis and task-dependent-reliability-framing, both of which use src-0001's extraction-versus-generation split as a calibration data point; a T3 targeting either must read this before citing it. NOTE THAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH THE CONSISTENCY HALF, where the CI widths of 0.02 against 0.06 are a single measurement with no competing metric.

NEW AT CYCLE 39, PROVENANCE, AND CHEAP FOR THE NEXT CYCLE THAT TOUCHES src-0001. Cycle 25 upgraded src-0001 from 'unreviewed preprint' to 'PEER-REVIEWED AND PUBLISHED at ARES 2025' on the strength of a citation block on the arXiv /html render giving 'In International Conference on Availability, Reliability and Security (pp. 343-364). Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland' and a conference DOI of 10.1007/978-3-032-00627-1_17. Cycle 39 fetched arxiv.org/abs/2503.23175 and found that arXiv's OWN METADATA FIELDS DO NOT CARRY IT: the Comments line is ABSENT, the Journal reference line is ABSENT, and the only DOI listed is the arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2503.23175. Contrast src-0007, whose /abs page does carry both 'Comments: Accepted at TMLR' and a Journal reference. THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION -- an /html citation block can legitimately carry a venue the /abs metadata omits, and the four listed versions all predate nothing that would explain it -- BUT IT MEANS THE PEER-REVIEW STATUS OF THIS BASE'S MOST LOAD-BEARING SOURCE RESTS ON A SINGLE UNCORROBORATED ARTEFACT. One fetch of https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-00627-1_17 would settle it. Cycle 39 did not spend that fetch and flags it as the cheapest outstanding provenance item in the base.

candidate_resolutions.summary: Reliability for CTI cannot be reduced to accuracy alone: on a 350-real-report evaluation, tested LLMs were both inconsistent across repeated/paraphrased queries and overconfident relative to their actual correctness, and this did not resolve with few-shot learning or fine-tuning (only partial improvement across all three paradigms tested). Exact per-model numeric scores are not yet captured in our knowledge base and are needed before this can be scored as strongly (vs. qualitatively) supported. === SCOPING NOTE ADDED AT CYCLE 39 WHILE RESOLVING ctr-0003. ctr-0003 named 'candidate_resolutions 1 and 2' as carriers of the disputed extraction-versus-generation calibration gradient. On inspection THIS candidate carries no gradient claim at all: its only calibration word is 'overconfident', which is the paper's own abstract term ('We show how LLMs cannot guarantee sufficient performance on real-size reports while also being inconsistent and overconfident.', re-verified verbatim from arxiv.org/abs/2503.23175 at cycle 39) and is not a between-task comparison. THIS CANDIDATE IS THEREFORE UNCHANGED BY ctr-0003 and no rewrite was needed here; the retirement was applied to the next candidate only, which is the one that actually states the gradient. Recorded so that no later cycle reads ctr-0003 and concludes this candidate was overlooked.

Full-text retrieval (cycle 3) confirms and sharpens the above with concrete numbers. The 3 tested models were gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, and mistral-large-2. Consistency (10-re-prompt bootstrapped confidence intervals) was tight for mechanical information-extraction (max CI width 0.02) but notably wider for open-ended information-generation (max CI width 0.06). Calibration (ECE/Brier, gpt4o) was substantially worse for generation than extraction sub-tasks, and critically, fine-tuning and few-shot prompting often WORSENED both accuracy and calibration rather than uniformly 'partially improving' them -- e.g. gpt4o APT-extraction precision/recall fell from 0.87 (zero-shot) to 0.68 (fine-tuned), and CVE-generation ECE rose from 0.15 to 0.91 after fine-tuning. This refines the cycle-2 resolution: the unreliability is not just persistent across paradigms -- more training examples or fine-tuning can actively degrade both accuracy and calibration on some CTI sub-tasks. === REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 39 TO RESOLVE ctr-0003. THE 'SUBSTANTIALLY WORSE FOR GENERATION THAN EXTRACTION' CALIBRATION FRAMING IN THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS HEREBY RETIRED AS UNSUPPORTED. Everything else in this candidate stands and every number in it is re-verified exact; only the calibration GRADIENT is withdrawn. WHY IT IS RETIRED: it does not hold row-wise at zero-shot -- generation goals 0.13, CVE 0.15 and country 0.19 all beat extraction campaign 0.25 and CVE 0.28 -- and its own worked example, CVE generation at 0.15, is better calibrated than its extraction counterpart at 0.28. THE REPLACEMENT IS NARROWER THAN THE RESTATEMENT ctr-0003 PROPOSED, BECAUSE CYCLE 39 FOUND THE GRADIENT IS METRIC-DEPENDENT. Per methodological rule (xii) cycle 39 re-derived every family mean from Table 6's printed cells itself rather than inheriting ctr-0003's figures. ctr-0003's FOUR ECE MEANS REPRODUCE EXACTLY: zero-shot extraction 0.205 (0.25+0.16+0.28+0.13 = 0.82, /4) against generation 0.278 (0.13+0.45+0.19+0.15+0.47 = 1.39, /5); fine-tuned extraction 0.295 (1.18/4) against generation 0.538 (2.69/5). The two few-shot ECE means, never derived by any prior cycle: extraction 0.2425 (0.97/4), generation 0.320 (1.60/5). So ON ECE the generation mean does exceed the extraction mean at all three paradigms. BUT TABLE 6 PRINTS BRIER SCORE BESIDE ECE, the paper defines BOTH as calibration measures ('The ECE and BS, are two measures of calibration that quantify the deviation from perfect calibration'), AND ON BRIER THE GRADIENT DOES NOT SURVIVE: zero-shot extraction 0.2975 (1.19/4) against generation 0.304 (1.52/5), a gap of 0.0065 and effectively nil; few-shot extraction 0.3225 (1.29/4) against generation 0.294 (1.47/5), WHICH IS REVERSED, extraction being the worse-calibrated family; fine-tuned extraction 0.375 (1.50/4) against generation 0.562 (2.81/5). ALL TWELVE MEANS ARE AGENT-DERIVED AND ARE NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER; they are labelled derived here and must be labelled derived wherever else they are used. THE SUPPORTED STATEMENT IS THEREFORE: on src-0001's Table 6 the extraction-versus-generation calibration gradient is NOT a robust property of the data. It holds on ECE at every paradigm, vanishes on Brier at zero-shot, REVERSES on Brier at few-shot, and is large and metric-agnostic ONLY after fine-tuning, where it is driven almost entirely by two generation rows (CVE ECE 0.91 / BS 0.98 and attack vector ECE 0.87 / BS 1.00). One row shows the two metrics disagreeing outright: extraction attack vector is the BEST-calibrated extraction cell on zero-shot ECE (0.13) and the WORST on zero-shot BS (0.46). WHAT SURVIVES UNDAMAGED AND SHOULD BE CARRIED FORWARD INSTEAD: fine-tuning does not reliably improve calibration and sometimes destroys it -- ECE worsened on 7 of 9 rows and BS on the same 7. THE CONSISTENCY HALF OF THIS CANDIDATE IS UNTOUCHED: the CI widths of 0.02 (extraction) against 0.06 (generation) are a different measurement, re-verified, and stand. VERSION CHECK, NEW AT CYCLE 39: Table 6 was re-pulled WHOLE from arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and all 54 cells are IDENTICAL to the cycle-25 pull from the unversioned render, which resolves to v4 (four versions exist: v1 29 Mar 2025, v2 16 Jul 2025, v3 4 Nov 2025, v4 12 Nov 2025, all 1,203 KB). The arithmetic above is therefore not version-dependent. ctr-0003 RESOLVED AT CYCLE 39.

ADDED cycle 15 by a T1 collect, status PROPOSED and deliberately not promoted -- READ THE SCOPE LIMIT BEFORE USING IT. This issue sat at score 2 from cycle 3 to cycle 15 for one reason: both candidate_resolutions above cite src-0001 and nothing else, and single-source support is a 2 by rubric. Four independent sources now measure the consistency/calibration/abstention axes on SECURITY tasks, none by src-0001's team, none on CTI material. (1) CALIBRATION: src-0013 (Siddiq/Rahman/Santos, ICSME 2026) is the first non-src-0001 source in this base reporting ECE and Brier on a security task -- GPT-4o-mini ECE 0.456-0.481, Qwen3-Coder-Next 0.408-0.421, Gemini-2.0-Flash 0.247-0.263 -- and independently reproduces src-0001's most counter-intuitive result, that an intervention meant to help can worsen calibration: moving from a controlled benchmark to a realistic repository-level setting raised ECE for every model (GPT-4o-mini 0.411->0.697, Gemini 0.161->0.721) and architectural gating helped on the controlled benchmark while degrading the realistic one. (2) INSTABILITY UNDER REPEATED IDENTICAL QUERY, src-0001's own method: src-0016 (Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0) ran each task five times with code, prompt and harness held constant and found 134/158 reference-matched findings recurred in all five runs while 80/161 unmatched findings appeared in only one of five -- a grounded-stable / volunteered-unstable split that parallels src-0001's extraction-vs-generation CI-width divide (0.02 vs 0.06). (3) PROMPT SENSITIVITY AND ABSTENTION: src-0014 (PromptAudit) fixes dataset/decoding/parsing and varies only prompting strategy, finding cross-strategy F1 ranges from 0.398 (Gemma) down to 0.103 (Mistral) and that self-consistency collapses coverage to 24.04-60.85%. (4) UNDER-REFUSAL: src-0015 (OpenSec) finds frontier IR agents over-trigger (GPT-5.2 100% containment at 82.5% FP) and locates the defect precisely -- 'the calibration gap is not in detection but in restraint' -- the same shape as src-0007's triage asymmetry. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO. It DOES establish that consistency failure, overconfidence and under-refusal are not artefacts of one team, one paper, one model family or one evaluation harness, and it supplies the base's first abstention data. It DOES NOT replicate src-0001 on CTI: every one of the four measures a security-adjacent task (secure code generation, CVE-code vulnerability detection, JavaScript SAST review, simulated incident response), NOT IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or threat-report drafting. So open_question (ii) -- would the findings replicate on src-0002's and src-0005's model lists on CTI tasks -- REMAINS FULLY OPEN, and none of the four tests a model from src-0001's, src-0002's or src-0005's lists. A T4 scoring this issue must decide explicitly whether cross-domain corroboration on the same failure mode counts toward multi-source support or whether the domain gap holds it at 2; that judgement has not been made and this entry does not make it.

SCOPE RULING, made by T2 at cycle 16 and recorded here so that no future cycle re-litigates it. THE QUESTION cycle 15's T1 raised and correctly refused to answer: it added four independent sources (src-0013, src-0014, src-0015, src-0016) measuring consistency, calibration and abstention on SECURITY tasks, and asked whether cross-domain corroboration of the same failure mode counts toward multi-source support for this issue, or whether the domain gap holds it at single-source. THE RULING IS THAT THE DOMAIN GAP HOLDS. This issue's scope stays anchored to CTI, and the two candidate_resolutions above -- the only ones making a claim about CTI material -- remain single-source (src-0001) for scoring purposes. REASONING, three grounds. (a) Every one of the four measures a security-ADJACENT task -- secure code generation, CVE-code vulnerability detection, JavaScript SAST review, simulated incident response -- and none measures IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or threat-report drafting, which are the tasks this topic is scoped to. (b) Not one tests a model from src-0001's, src-0002's or src-0005's lists; the model overlap is empty, so open_questions (i) and (ii) are untouched by them and must NOT be marked answered. (c) This base's own precedent for admitting a security-adjacent source is src-0008 (JavaScript obfuscation), which was admitted WITH an explicit scope gap and was never treated as a replication of the CTI work; ruling the other way here would retroactively change what that precedent meant. WHAT IS NEVERTHELESS ESTABLISHED, and it is not nothing: the MECHANISM -- output instability under identical or perturbed input, systematic overconfidence, and under-refusal -- is robust across four unrelated teams, four methods, four corpora and roughly fifteen models, so it is not an artefact of one paper, one team or one model family; and two of src-0001's most fragile-looking sub-findings are independently echoed by different mechanisms (an intervention intended to help WORSENING calibration: src-0013's repository-level ECE rising 0.411 to 0.697 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.161 to 0.721 for Gemini-2.0-Flash, and src-0014's adaptive-CoT reducing recall for every model, e.g. Gemma 0.420 to 0.057; and GROUNDED-OUTPUT-STABLE versus VOLUNTEERED-OUTPUT-UNSTABLE: src-0016's 134 of 158 reference-matched findings recurring in all five identical repetitions against 80 of 161 unmatched findings appearing in only one of five, paralleling src-0001's extraction-vs-generation CI widths of 0.02 vs 0.06). That is a claim about SECURITY-TASK LLM RELIABILITY GENERALLY. It is held here as context for the CTI claim, not as support for it. CONSEQUENCE FOR A T4: score this issue on its CTI candidates. A T4 may overrule this scope ruling, but if it does it must say so explicitly and give its reason -- what it must not do is silently count the four as multi-source support for a CTI claim. NO SCORE IS SET HERE; scoring is T4's work and this entry deliberately does not perform it. TWO THINGS REMAIN UNCHANGED AND SHOULD NOT BE FORGOTTEN: this base still has no non-src-0001 source measuring consistency AND calibration together, and per carry-forward [20] src-0013's and src-0014's numbers are single-pass fetches whose results tables have never been pulled whole, with src-0013 additionally carrying an unreconciled internal discrepancy (False Trust for GPT-4o-mini given as 33.9% in one section and as rising from 16.9% to 83.2% in another) -- those two figures must not be quoted together until a G2 pulls that table.

ADDED AND PROMOTED TO SUPPORTED BY CYCLE 25's T3. THE CTI-DOMAIN SINGLE-SOURCE BLOCKER IS BROKEN, BUT FOR THE CONSISTENCY HALF ONLY -- read the split below before scoring. THE CLAIM: on CTI material specifically, LLM outputs are NOT stable across repeated identical queries, and this is now measured by two teams with nothing in common. (1) src-0001 (Mezzi, Massacci, Tuma; ARES 2025, peer-reviewed -- see the cycle-25 note appended to that source, the base had wrongly carried it as an unreviewed preprint since cycle 1): 350 real threat-intelligence reports, 3 models, ten re-prompts per input with bootstrapped CIs, max CI width 0.02 for information extraction and 0.06 for information generation. The cycle-25 whole-table pull recovered the protocol sentence verbatim -- 'we re-prompt each LLM ten times on the same input, with temperature=0 and the same seed to guarantee maximum determinism' -- so the measured spread is RESIDUAL NON-DETERMINISM UNDER MAXIMAL DETERMINISM SETTINGS, which strengthens the finding. (2) src-0018 (Milenkoski and Cirstea, SentinelLabs, 9 March 2026): selective IOC/hash/playbook extraction from narrative threat reports, ground truth of 343 atomic IOCs and 1859 labeled contextual-attribute instances, five current-generation models, 'repeated executions of each evaluation experiment' under 'identical conditions', with two purpose-built decision-consistency metrics (share of IOCs receiving two or more different values for one attribute across runs; average mode-based observed disagreement). INDEPENDENCE IS CLEAN: no shared author, academia vs industry lab, different corpora, model sets a full generation apart and disjoint, and src-0018 does not cite src-0001. This clears the cycle-16 scope ruling on its own terms rather than overturning it -- src-0018 is CTI proper (IOC extraction from threat reports), not a security-adjacent task, so no cross-domain generalisation is being asserted. TWO LIMITS A T4 MUST HOLD ONTO. (a) src-0018 SUPPLIES NO NUMBERS: all four of its quantitative artefacts are images this agent cannot read, so the corroboration is of DIRECTION AND EXISTENCE only, and no magnitude may be compared with src-0001's CI widths. (b) THE CALIBRATION HALF IS UNTOUCHED: src-0018 measures ABSTENTION errors (FDR/FNR over an explicit None class), which is a restraint construct and NOT ECE/Brier -- the same non-pooling rule already recorded for src-0015. Proper-scoring calibration on CTI remains src-0001-only, gpt4o-only, nine table rows. SO THE HONEST SCORING POSITION IS SPLIT: consistency-on-CTI is now two-source and qualitative-plus-quantitative; calibration-on-CTI is still one-source. This issue's title asks both. === REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 39 TO RESOLVE ctr-0005, WHICH FOUND LIMIT (a) ABOVE TOO BROAD. Limit (a) as written -- 'src-0018 SUPPLIES NO NUMBERS: all four of its quantitative artefacts are images' -- is WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED, on two counts. FIRST, THE COUNT IS WRONG: the page carries TEN figures, of which six are quantitative, not four; the two no cycle knew existed are 'Prediction and error diversity (GPT-4.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.5)' and 'LLM Performance in Playbook and knowledge graph assembly', plus 'Human vs. LLMs: Time efficiency in report processing'. SECOND, THE PROHIBITION WAS SCOPED TO THE WHOLE PAGE WHEN IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN SCOPED TO THE PERFORMANCE ARTEFACTS. THE CORRECTED SCOPE, AND IT IS THE OPERATIVE RULE FROM CYCLE 39 ONWARD: the FOUR performance artefacts -- the 'LLM decision consistency' table and the 'Abstention error rates', 'Selective IOC extraction performance' and 'Value assignment performance' charts -- are confirmed IMAGE, CANNOT READ, for a THIRD independent time, and quoting, estimating, ranking or comparing THOSE magnitudes REMAINS FORBIDDEN IN FULL; no cycle should re-attempt them by fetch, since three have failed and no OCR route exists in this sandbox. Numbers in the page's BODY TEXT are readable and citable, and the base was needlessly locked out of them -- the same entry already cited two of them (343 atomic IOCs, 1859 labeled contextual-attribute instances), so the blanket ban was internally inconsistent with its own source entry. THIRD AND MOST IMPORTANT FOR THIS CANDIDATE, THE METHODOLOGICAL FACT THE OVER-BROAD HEDGE HAD LOCKED OUT, verbatim from the page: 'the LLM temperature parameter was set to 0 to minimize randomness and reduce non-deterministic behavior'. src-0018's repeat-run decision inconsistency is therefore residual non-determinism measured UNDER a determinism setting, exactly as src-0001's is ('temperature=0 and the same seed to guarantee maximum determinism'). THIS STRENGTHENS THE CANDIDATE RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT: two independent teams, on disjoint model sets a generation apart, on different CTI corpora, both report output instability on CTI extraction tasks AT TEMPERATURE 0. The corroboration is still of DIRECTION AND EXISTENCE only -- no magnitude may be compared with src-0001's CI widths -- but it is now direction-and-existence under a matched and unusually strong experimental control, which is a stronger form of agreement than two uncontrolled observations. RULING ON ctr-0005 STEP (ii), THE 41-MINUTE HUMAN BASELINE: IT DOES NOT BELONG IN THIS ISSUE AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ENTERED HERE. 'whose average was 41 minutes per report' against 'about 3.3 minutes per report' is a THROUGHPUT fact, not a reliability fact, and this issue is about consistency and calibration; admitting it would smuggle a speed measurement into a reliability claim. It is also NOT the human-analyst F1 that ttp-attack-mapping-reliability's open_question has wanted for sixteen cycles, so it discharges nothing there either. It is left recorded in ctr-0005 and in src-0018's own entry, and carried forward for a T1 or T2 to place on a throughput or cost-benefit issue if one is ever opened. THE NON-POOLING RULE IS RESTATED UNCHANGED: src-0018's abstention metrics (FDR/FNR over an explicit None class) are a RESTRAINT construct and must never be pooled with src-0001's or src-0013's ECE/Brier proper-scoring calibration, nor with src-0015's action-threshold calibration, nor with src-0014's selective-prediction coverage. LIMIT (b) STANDS UNCHANGED: proper-scoring calibration on CTI remains src-0001-only and gpt4o-only. ctr-0005 RESOLVED AT CYCLE 39.

ADDED BY CYCLE 25's T3 (G2 by-product, promoted because it is verified directly against the source's own printed table). WHAT src-0001's TABLE 6 ACTUALLY SHOWS, now that it has been pulled whole for the first time in 25 cycles. Caption verbatim: 'ECE and BS with gpt4o for information generation and extraction.' Nine rows, gpt4o only, three paradigms, ECE and BS. Extraction, zero-shot | few-shot | fine-tuning ECE: campaign 0.25 | 0.26 | 0.48; APT 0.16 | 0.17 | 0.25; CVE 0.28 | 0.35 | 0.18; attack vector 0.13 | 0.19 | 0.27. Generation, same order: goals 0.13 | 0.04 | 0.08; labels 0.45 | 0.57 | 0.48; country 0.19 | 0.38 | 0.35; CVE 0.15 | 0.13 | 0.91; attack vector 0.47 | 0.48 | 0.87. THREE CONSEQUENCES. (i) The five cells this base had stored are all EXACT; the base had simply never held the other four rows or the few-shot column. (ii) The generation-is-worse-calibrated-than-extraction framing carried in candidate_resolutions 1 and 2 above and in src-0001's key_claims[4] DOES NOT HOLD ROW-WISE AT ZERO-SHOT -- generation goals 0.13, CVE 0.15 and country 0.19 are all better calibrated than extraction campaign 0.25 and extraction CVE 0.28, and the framing's own worked example (CVE generation 0.15) beats its extraction counterpart (0.28). What holds is a mean gap that is small at zero-shot (generation 0.278 vs extraction 0.205) and large after fine-tuning (0.538 vs 0.295), driven almost entirely by two fine-tuned generation rows. Those four means are DERIVED BY THIS AGENT from the printed cells and are NOT printed in the paper. Contradiction ctr-0003 is opened for this; nothing above has been rewritten. (iii) The strongest surviving version of the fine-tuning finding is not about extraction vs generation at all but about DIRECTION OF CHANGE: relative to zero-shot, fine-tuning WORSENED ECE on 7 of the 9 rows and WORSENED BS on the same 7 (derived by cell-by-cell comparison, not printed), improving only extraction CVE (ECE 0.28->0.18, BS 0.32->0.21) and generation goals (ECE 0.13->0.08, BS 0.14->0.05) -- so 'fine-tuning does not reliably improve calibration and sometimes destroys it' is well supported, whereas 'generation is markedly worse than extraction' is not, at least not before fine-tuning. === AMENDED AT CYCLE 39, RESOLVING ctr-0003. Consequence (ii) above is CORRECT BUT INCOMPLETE, and the omission changes the conclusion. It reports the mean gap on ECE ONLY. Table 6 prints Brier Score in the adjacent column and the paper defines both metrics identically as 'two measures of calibration that quantify the deviation from perfect calibration', so a calibration gradient claim must survive on both. Cycle 39 re-derived all twelve family means from the printed cells (rule (xii); ctr-0003's four ECE means reproduce EXACTLY). ECE: extraction 0.205 / 0.2425 / 0.295 against generation 0.278 / 0.320 / 0.538 for zero-shot / few-shot / fine-tuning -- generation worse at all three. BRIER: extraction 0.2975 / 0.3225 / 0.375 against generation 0.304 / 0.294 / 0.562 -- generation worse by 0.0065 at zero-shot (effectively nil), BETTER than extraction at few-shot (0.294 against 0.3225, a REVERSAL), and worse only after fine-tuning. ALL TWELVE ARE AGENT-DERIVED, NOT PRINTED. SO THE MEAN-GAP FRAMING THAT ctr-0003 OFFERED AS THE DEFENSIBLE RESTATEMENT IS ITSELF METRIC-DEPENDENT AND MUST NOT BE STATED WITHOUT NAMING THE METRIC. The only paradigm at which the gradient holds on both metrics is fine-tuning, and there it rests on two rows (generation CVE 0.91/0.98 and attack vector 0.87/1.00). Consequence (iii) above is unaffected and is the robust finding. ALSO NEW AT CYCLE 39: all 54 cells of Table 6 re-pulled whole from v1 are IDENTICAL to the cycle-25 pull from the current render (v4), so no version effect; and a single row shows the two metrics contradicting each other outright -- extraction attack vector, best-calibrated extraction cell on zero-shot ECE at 0.13 and worst on zero-shot BS at 0.46.

issues.title: How often do LLMs outright misattribute the threat actor, and how well is that error rate measured? [SPLIT AT CYCLE 45: this issue is now the attribution-ERROR-RATE leg only. The id is LEGACY and deliberately unchanged -- see open_questions[3]. The attribution-CONFIDENCE leg moved to attribution-expressed-confidence-unmeasured.]
open_questions: REWRITTEN cycle 28 (T3). THE QUESTION AS PREVIOUSLY POSED IS MALFORMED AND IS RETIRED, NOT DELETED; the old wording asked whether 'the plausible-vs-correct gap' measured on 2024-era models narrows for later models, and ctr-0002 established that that gap is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION -- CTIBench defines Plausible Accuracy as 'the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined', so it contains Correct Accuracy and there is no empirical quantity there to narrow. THE WELL-POSED REPLACEMENT: does CTIBench's own INCORRECT bucket -- the hallucination-inclusive one, defined verbatim as 'when the LLM misattributes the threat actor due to misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation', numerically equal to 100 minus Plausible Accuracy and standing at 14 / 38 / 26 / 20 / 64 percent for GPT-4-turbo / GPT-3.5-turbo / Gemini-1.5 / LLAMA3-70B / LLAMA3-8B (DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM TABLE 1, NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER) -- fall for post-2024 models? STATUS: NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE ANSWERS IT, and cycle 28 confirms the previous cycle's diagnosis rather than improving on it. src-0007's 1-5 'Content: Threat Actor' rubric is the only later-generation threat-actor measurement here and it reports a graded quality score, not a correct / underdetermined-but-related / outright-wrong partition, so it cannot be converted into this quantity at any exchange rate. What is missing is any source that partitions post-2024 attribution outputs into those three buckets, or that reports an outright-misattribution rate for a post-2024 model. This is the highest-value collection target for this issue; the next T1 is cycle 43, so the realistic route is a T3 with search budget.

NOT WORKED AT CYCLE 28 -- HONEST DEFERRAL, recorded so no successor assumes it was checked. THE QUESTION, unchanged: is attribution error correlated with how well-documented a threat actor group is (e.g. major APTs with abundant public reporting vs. obscure/emerging groups)? Cycle 28's budget went to ctr-0002's three-step resolution path and to a G2 on src-0018, and this question was not touched. NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, from inspection of the base rather than from a fetch: no source here publishes a per-report or per-actor breakdown of attribution outcomes -- src-0002's CTI-TAA result is 50 reports reported only as aggregate percentages in Table 1, and src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' rubric is likewise a corpus aggregate -- so the question cannot be answered from stored values and needs new material. The cheapest untried route is CTIBench's own released dataset/evaluation artefact, which would carry per-report ground truth; that is the same route that worked for src-0007 at cycle 21 (src-0017) and no cycle has looked for CTIBench's equivalent.

ANSWERED AT CYCLE 28 (T3), after ten cycles in which it was merely articulated. THE QUESTION WAS: did ENISA's APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' naming-convention hallucination (src-0004) contribute to, or correlate with, the kind of plausible-but-wrong attribution measured quantitatively in src-0002, or is it a distinct hallucination sub-type (citation/naming fabrication vs. attribution judgment)? THE ANSWER IS: DISTINCT SUB-TYPE. THE DECIDING ARGUMENT COMES FROM src-0002'S OWN SCORING RULE, already stored verbatim in this base: 'To further ensure accuracy, we manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use.' CTI-TAA SCORES AN ALIAS AS CORRECT -- its 'correct answer' bucket is defined as 'when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases'. APT29 and Midnight Blizzard are two names for one group, and the ENISA passage names the right group; its error is the claim about WHICH VENDOR USES WHICH NAME, i.e. a false statement about naming provenance, not a false statement about who conducted the activity. Under CTI-TAA's own rule the ENISA sentence would be scored CORRECT. The ENISA defect is therefore INVISIBLE TO THE MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT this issue's quantified leg rests on, and the two cannot be instances of one measured phenomenon. Two corroborating considerations, neither load-bearing: the same ENISA report's other documented defect is 26 of 492 incorrect footnotes, a citation-validity failure of exactly the kind src-0011 (GhostCite) and src-0012 (EY Canada) measure; and src-0004 attaches no accuracy or confidence measurement of any kind to the passage. CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED AGAINST THIS ISSUE'S OWN INTEREST: src-0004's evidential home is institutional-incident-real-world-impact, and it must not be counted as an independent second source for THIS issue's central claim -- which is why the primary candidate below now cites src-0002 alone, where it previously cited src-0002 and src-0004. RESIDUAL, GENUINELY OPEN AND NOT TO BE ASSERTED EITHER WAY: whether the two sub-types share an upstream generative cause (both being ungrounded production of a specific-looking fact) is a mechanism question that no source in this base tests.

NEW AT CYCLE 45 (T2) AND IT IS A RECORD OF A STRUCTURAL CHANGE, NOT A QUESTION. THIS ISSUE HAS BEEN SPLIT. Carry-forward [45] has requested this since cycle 25 and only a T2 has standing to do it. WHAT WAS WRONG: this issue bundled TWO questions with wildly asymmetric evidence. Leg one, the attribution-ERROR-RATE leg -- how often does a model name the wrong actor -- is well evidenced by src-0002 and corroborated in direction by src-0007. Leg two, the attribution-CONFIDENCE leg -- how confidently is the wrong answer asserted, which is what the issue's ORIGINAL TITLE actually asked about ('How large is the gap between plausible-sounding and factually correct LLM threat-actor attribution?') -- HAS NO EVIDENCE AT ALL, as this issue's own second candidate_resolution established at cycle 28. Successive T4s identified leg two as the weaker leg actually governing the bundled score, so the well-evidenced leg was being held down by a leg nothing in this base measures. WHAT WAS DONE: THIS issue is now the ERROR-RATE leg alone and has been RETITLED accordingly. A NEW issue, attribution-expressed-confidence-unmeasured, carries the CONFIDENCE leg. NOTHING WAS DELETED AND NO TEXT WAS MOVED -- all three existing candidate_resolutions and all three prior open_questions stay HERE, because every one of them is error-rate material; the confidence leg's substance is restated FRESH in the new issue rather than cut out of candidate_resolutions[1], which remains here as the audit record of the cycle-28 decision that produced the split. WHY THE ID WAS NOT RENAMED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT: the string 'attribution-confident-wrong-gap' is cited from state/knowledge/index.json, state/knowledge/src-0002.md and state/knowledge/src-0017.md, ALL THREE OF WHICH ARE APPEND-ONLY under scripts/validate_state.py lines 105-107. Renaming the id would strand those three references with no legal repair available. The id is therefore LEGACY: it now names the error-rate leg and no longer describes its own contents. Any future cycle reading that id must read this note. Checked at cycle 45: the knowledge-file reference concerns ctr-0008, which is src-0007 rubric material and belongs to THIS leg, so the retained references remain correct in substance. WHERE THE CONTRADICTIONS LANDED, AND THE SPLIT FORCED THIS CHOICE because a contradiction entry carries exactly ONE issue_id (carry-forward [41]). BOTH STAY HERE, and this is a deliberate decision rather than an accident of not moving them. ctr-0008 (OPEN) is the src-0007 Table 4 metric-definition defect -- Content: Threat Actor 'Attribution' measures SOURCE LINKING while Content: Root Cause 'Attribution' measures ACTOR IDENTIFICATION -- and its own text says in terms that it 'evidences WRONGNESS rather than CONFIDENCE and supplies nothing to this issue's titular confident half'. By its own words it belongs to the error-rate leg. ctr-0002 (RESOLVED cycle 28) is the plausible-versus-correct nesting defect in src-0002, likewise error-rate material. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE G3 CEILING, STATED SO NO T4 MISREADS IT: THIS issue still carries exactly ONE open contradiction (ctr-0008), so its ceiling under lines 144-156 is unchanged at scale_max minus g3_contradiction_demotion = 3. The NEW issue carries NONE, so its ceiling is 5 -- THAT IS A LIFTED CONSTRAINT AND EMPHATICALLY NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR A HIGH SCORE, since the new issue's whole content is that its quantity is unmeasured. WHAT A T4 MUST NOT CONCLUDE FROM THIS SPLIT: that this issue's score should rise merely because the weak leg left. The split makes an honest reassessment POSSIBLE; it does not perform one. Cycle 45 is a T2 and has rescored nothing. The new issue's scores.json entry was created at score 0, the schema's value for 'unexamined', precisely so that no scoring judgement is smuggled in by a task type that has no standing to make one.

candidate_resolutions.summary: REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 28 (T3), executing step (i) of ctr-0002's resolution path. THE 86-VS-52 FRAMING IS RETIRED, NOT REPAIRED. The old text of this candidate said 'every one of the 5 tested models' plausible-sounding attribution rate substantially exceeds its correct attribution rate (e.g. GPT-4-turbo: 86% plausible vs 52% correct; Gemini-1.5: 74% vs 38%)'; CTIBench defines Plausible Accuracy as 'the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined', so it CONTAINS Correct Accuracy and that inequality is true by construction for every model on every dataset. It evidenced nothing and is withdrawn. WHAT REPLACES IT. CTI-TAA partitions each response into three buckets, verbatim: 'correct answer (when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases), plausible answer (when the threat report lacks sufficient details to pinpoint the answer, but the LLM provides a plausible or related threat actor within a similar group), and incorrect answer (when the LLM misattributes the threat actor due to misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation)'. The THIRD bucket is the paper's own hallucination-inclusive misattribution rate and equals 100 minus Plausible Accuracy: GPT-4-turbo 14%, GPT-3.5-turbo 38%, Gemini-1.5 26%, LLAMA3-70B 20%, LLAMA3-8B 64%, over 50 real threat reports, with the authors stating that they 'manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use'. THOSE FIVE VALUES ARE DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM TABLE 1 BY THIS AGENT AND ARE NOT PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER; every cell they are derived from was re-verified EXACT against Table 1 by two independent fetches at cycle 23, and the ChatGPT-4 row was re-confirmed a third time at cycle 28. THE FINDING: outright misattribution of the threat actor is common in 2024-era models, from roughly one report in seven for the best model to nearly two in three for the weakest, on real reports scored with alias tolerance. WHAT THIS CANDIDATE DOES NOT CLAIM, and the distinction is the whole point of this issue: src-0002 measures WRONGNESS, NOT CONFIDENCE. It records no verbalised confidence, no hedging rate, no calibration metric and no reader-facing plausibility judgement, and no sentence in the paper interprets the correct-versus-plausible gap. Its 'plausible' bucket is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor from a similar group -- arguably reasonable behaviour under ambiguity -- and is explicitly NOT its hallucination bucket. The string 'plausible-sounding' does not occur in the paper, though this state presented it in scare quotes for 27 cycles. This candidate is therefore supported as an ATTRIBUTION-ERROR-RATE finding and supplies no support whatever for the 'confident' half of this issue's title. src-0004 has been REMOVED from this candidate's evidence: see open_question[2], answered this cycle, which finds the ENISA error to be a distinct sub-type invisible to CTI-TAA's scoring rule.

ADDED cycle 28 (T3), executing step (ii) of ctr-0002's resolution path and recording the decision in the graph rather than only in a log. THE DECISION: NEITHER READING (a) NOR (b) WHOLE. The honest answer is (a) FOR THE NUMBER AND (b) FOR THE ISSUE AS TITLED, and this candidate exists to state the (b) half, because nothing else in the graph does and a T4 scoring the graph alone would not see it. Reading (a) is right that a 14-64% outright misattribution rate on 50 real reports is a real, citable finding; it is now this issue's primary candidate above. Reading (b) is right that what made src-0002 compelling FOR THIS ISSUE was the SIZE of the 86-versus-52 gap read as plausible-sounding-but-wrong output, and that reading is gone and cannot be recovered. I record explicitly that I did NOT adopt (a) alone despite cycle 26's T4 writing that doing so would return the issue to 3 -- that was an expectation, not an instruction, and the scoring consequence is not a reason to pick a reading. THE SURVEY FINDING, which is the substance of the (b) half: NO SOURCE IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION. src-0002 partitions outputs by correctness only and records no confidence construct of any kind (its metric section defines accuracy for CTI-MCQ/CTI-RCM, MAD for CTI-VSP, F1 for CTI-ATE, and the three-bucket partition for CTI-TAA -- nothing else). src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' block is an LLM-judged 1-5 quality rubric (Relevance / Accuracy / Attribution) whose absolute level is uninterpretable and which grades attribution QUALITY, not how confidently the model asserts it. src-0004 is a single published passage with no measurement attached at all. The nearest confidence measurements anywhere in this base -- src-0001's and src-0013's ECE and Brier scores -- are on different task sets entirely and belong to consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode, which this issue already lists in depends_on. CONSEQUENCE: this issue's titular quantity, the gap between plausible-SOUNDING and factually correct attribution, IS UNMEASURED BY EVERY SOURCE IT CITES. That is a finding about the evidence, not a claim about the world -- it does not show the gap is small or absent, it shows that nobody in this base has measured it, and no cycle may treat attribution error rates as a proxy for it. STRUCTURAL NOTE FOR A FUTURE T2, WHICH IS THE ONLY TASK TYPE WITH STANDING TO ACT ON IT: this issue bundles an attribution-ERROR-RATE question, now well evidenced by src-0002 and corroborated in direction by src-0007, with an attribution-CONFIDENCE question that has no evidence at all. That is the same asymmetry carry-forward [37] describes for consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode, and the natural cut is the same shape. A T3 cannot split an issue and this one does not attempt to. === CYCLE-45 ANNOTATION (T2). THE STRUCTURAL NOTE IMMEDIATELY ABOVE HAS BEEN ACTED ON. THE SPLIT IS DONE; see this issue's open_questions[3]. === THIS CANDIDATE STAYS HERE UNCHANGED, and the reason matters: it is the audit record of the cycle-28 decision -- '(a) FOR THE NUMBER AND (b) FOR THE ISSUE AS TITLED' -- and that decision is what made the primary candidate above say what it says, so removing it would orphan the primary candidate's justification. BUT ITS (b) HALF NO LONGER GOVERNS THIS ISSUE. The SURVEY FINDING it states -- that NO SOURCE IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION -- has been RESTATED FRESH as the primary candidate of the new issue attribution-expressed-confidence-unmeasured, where it is now the whole point rather than a caveat attached to somebody else's number. A T4 SCORING THIS ISSUE MUST THEREFORE NOT DEDUCT FOR THE UNMEASURED CONFIDENCE QUANTITY ANY MORE: that quantity is no longer part of this issue, and double-counting it against both issues is exactly the failure the split was performed to prevent. WHAT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL BINDS HERE: the (a) half in full, including that src-0002 measures WRONGNESS AND NOT CONFIDENCE, that its five incorrect-bucket rates are DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION AND NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER, and that src-0004 is not an independent second source for this leg.

issues.title: How confidently do LLMs assert threat-actor attributions they get wrong -- and is that quantity measured by anything at all?
open_questions: CREATED AT CYCLE 45 (T2) BY SPLITTING attribution-confident-wrong-gap, per carry-forward [45], which had requested the split since cycle 25. READ THAT ISSUE'S open_questions[3] FIRST -- it records the split in full, including why the OTHER issue kept the now-misleading legacy id 'attribution-confident-wrong-gap' (it is cited from three APPEND-ONLY knowledge files and cannot legally be renamed). THIS ISSUE IS THE LEG WITH NO EVIDENCE, AND THAT IS ITS ENTIRE POINT: it exists so that the well-evidenced attribution-ERROR-RATE leg can be scored on its own merits instead of being held down by a question nothing in this base answers, and so that the unanswered question stays VISIBLE instead of being quietly absorbed as a caveat on somebody else's number. A SUCCESSOR MUST NOT TREAT A LOW SCORE HERE AS A FINDING ABOUT THE WORLD. It is a finding about the evidence base.

THE PRIMARY OPEN QUESTION, AND IT IS A COLLECTION QUESTION BEFORE IT IS AN ANALYTIC ONE: does ANY published evaluation measure expressed confidence on threat-actor attribution -- verbalised confidence ('I am 80% sure'), token-level probability, hedging rate, refusal/abstention rate, or a calibration statistic such as ECE or Brier computed ON AN ATTRIBUTION TASK? NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE DOES, as of cycle 45 and as surveyed at cycle 28. [SENTENCE REPAIRED AT CYCLE 49 -- THE TEXT THAT STOOD HERE FROM CYCLE 45 TO CYCLE 48 WAS FALSE.] What stood here was 'THIS IS A T1 TARGET AND NO SCHEDULED TASK CURRENTLY REACHES IT', and it is withdrawn. Cycle 48 first doubted it and cycle 49 re-read prompts/t3_investigate.md at source and confirmed: step 2 reads VERBATIM 'Work through the open questions using the existing knowledge base FIRST. Only web-search for what the knowledge base cannot answer (and if you fetch something substantial, add it properly as a source per T1 rules -- it counts toward the same max_new_sources budget).' A T3 IS EXPLICITLY AUTHORISED TO WEB-SEARCH AND TO ADD SOURCES when the base cannot answer, which is precisely this issue's condition. THIS ISSUE WAS NEVER STARVED; it was simply never scheduled until cycle 49, which did collect against it (src-0023, src-0024) under exactly that clause. The starvation premise behind carry-forward [96] and [55] is withdrawn. No contradiction entry was opened for this because G3's trigger is two SUPPORTED CLAIMS in conflict and an open_questions annotation is not a candidate_resolution -- the precedent is cycle 26 and ctr-0010. Note precisely what would and would not count: a calibration number on a DIFFERENT task set does NOT count (see the next question), and an accuracy or error rate does NOT count at any exchange rate, because a model can be uniformly wrong while being uniformly hedged or uniformly strident and the error rate cannot distinguish those cases.

WHY THE NEAREST-LOOKING EVIDENCE DOES NOT TRANSFER, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-DISCOVERS IT AND SO NOBODY IMPORTS IT ANYWAY. The base DOES contain confidence and calibration measurements -- src-0001's and src-0013's ECE and Brier scores -- but they are computed on ENTIRELY DIFFERENT TASK SETS and belong to consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode, which is listed in this issue's depends_on for exactly that reason. The genuinely open question is whether calibration behaviour measured on those tasks TRANSFERS to attribution, and NOTHING IN THIS BASE TESTS TRANSFER. Until something does, importing an ECE from another task to stand in for attribution confidence would be an operationalisation mismatch of the shape this project has already booked twice. THE THREE SOURCES CLOSEST TO THIS ISSUE ALL FAIL IT FOR STATED REASONS: src-0002 partitions CTI-TAA outputs by CORRECTNESS ONLY (correct / plausible / incorrect) and records no confidence construct of any kind, and its 'plausible' bucket is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor from a similar group -- arguably reasonable behaviour under ambiguity, and NOT a confidence measurement; src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' block is an LLM-judged 1-5 QUALITY rubric whose absolute level is uninterpretable and which, per ctr-0008, measures SOURCE LINKING rather than actor identification in its 'Attribution' row; src-0004 is a single published passage with no measurement attached at all. Also note, from src-0002's own text, that the exact string 'plausible-sounding' DOES NOT OCCUR IN THE PAPER, though this project presented it in scare quotes as a quotation for 27 cycles -- the phrase in this issue's ancestry is OURS, not a source's.

A DESIGN QUESTION THIS ISSUE SHOULD NOT DUCK, because it determines whether the issue is answerable in principle: WHAT WOULD THE RIGHT MEASUREMENT EVEN LOOK LIKE? Attribution is unlike the tasks calibration is normally measured on, because the ground truth is itself contested, aliased and sometimes genuinely underdetermined by the report -- which is precisely why CTIBench needed a 'plausible' bucket and why it scores an ALIAS as correct. A confidence measurement that ignored that would be measuring the wrong thing. So a well-posed target is narrower than 'is the model calibrated': it is whether a model's expressed confidence DISCRIMINATES between reports whose attribution is determined by the evidence and reports whose attribution is not. If no published work measures that, saying so with this reasoning attached is a legitimate resolution of this issue and should be recorded as such rather than treated as a failure to find an answer.

ADDED AT CYCLE 49 (T3, THE FIRST TASK EVER AIMED AT THIS ISSUE). SCOPE OF THE EXTERNAL SEARCH, RECORDED BECAUSE A NEGATIVE FINDING IS WORTH NOTHING UNLESS ITS SCOPE IS STATED. Five web searches were run, in these directions: (1) verbalised-confidence and calibration on threat-actor attribution specifically; (2) abstention/refusal rate plus ECE/Brier on a CTI attribution task; (3) CTIArena and other current CTI benchmarks against confidence/calibration/abstention; (4) 'threat attribution' with overconfidence/hedging/uncertainty; (5) uncertainty quantification and confidence elicitation applied to APT-group identification. WHAT CAME BACK: a large and active general-domain literature on verbalised confidence, calibration and abstention (ConfidenceBench, I-CALM, Abstain-R1, 'Wired for Overconfidence', LLM-as-Judge overconfidence, black-box UQ surveys) and a separate CTI-benchmark literature that measures CORRECTNESS ONLY. THE TWO DO NOT MEET ON AN ATTRIBUTION TASK IN ANYTHING CYCLE 49 FOUND. The single most probative new artefact, src-0023 (arXiv 2510.11974, ACCEPTED TO KDD 2026, with a Threat Actor Profiling task in v1 and an Entity Attribution task category in v2), returned ABSENT on two URL forms serving two different versions for every one of: calibration, Expected Calibration Error, ECE, Brier, confidence, likelihood, abstain, abstention, 'I don't know', 'insufficient evidence', uncertain, logprob, 'how certain'. SEPARATELY AND INDEPENDENTLY, the released CTIBench artefact was checked at source (src-0019, evaluation/evaluation.ipynb): its CTI-TAA scorer compute_taa_accuracy computes correct-and-plausible accuracy from a string-connection helper and NOTHING ELSE, and the strings confidence, calibration, probability, abstain, abstention, unknown, refus, hedge, ECE, Brier and logprob are ALL ABSENT from the entire notebook. So for the benchmark this issue's ancestry was built on, the absence of a confidence construct is now confirmed IN THE EXECUTABLE CODE and not merely in the prose. THIS IS THE SECOND, DIFFERENTLY-SHAPED CONFIRMATION THAT METHODOLOGICAL RULE (v) REQUIRES FOR AN ABSENT VERDICT.

ADDED AT CYCLE 49. WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS OPEN, REPLACING THE BLANKET 'NOBODY HAS LOOKED' THAT PRECEDED IT. (a) THE STRONGEST UNCHECKED LEAD IS INSIDE THIS BASE AND NOBODY HAS PULLED IT: src-0015 (OpenSec) defines its reward with the verbatim clause 'Attribution rewards correct identification (+1 per correct field) and penalizes unknowns (-0.5 each)' -- an explicit PENALTY ON ABSTENTION attached to a component the paper itself calls Attribution. That is the closest construct in this base to an abstention measure on an attribution task. IT IS NOT YET A COUNTEREXAMPLE TO THIS ISSUE'S SURVEY FINDING, for two stated reasons: it is a TRAINING-SIGNAL component rather than a reported measurement, and OpenSec's 'Attribution' is incident-field identification inside synthetic RL episodes, not threat-actor identification from a threat report. BUT NOBODY HAS CHECKED WHETHER OpenSec REPORTS AN UNKNOWN-RATE OR ABSTENTION-RATE ANYWHERE, and if it does, this issue's primary question changes shape. This is a cheap, well-specified next action against a source already in the base. (b) src-0023's Appendix D PROMPT TEMPLATES were unreadable in both fetches, and prompt templates are exactly where an instruction to state a confidence level would live -- under rule (xvi) that absence is NOT established; the ar5iv render or the KDD 2026 proceedings would close it. (c) The MISP taxonomy LEVEL SETS behind src-0024 were not fetched, so this base cannot yet say how many levels admiralty-scale or estimative-language define or what they are. (d) UNCHANGED AND STILL THE DEEPEST GAP: whether calibration behaviour measured on other task sets TRANSFERS to attribution is tested by NOTHING, in this base or in anything cycle 49 found. (e) Note for the record that cycle 49's searches were English-language, and that a benchmark could measure this in an appendix a search engine does not index -- the finding is 'not found by these searches', which is weaker than 'does not exist', and must always be stated that way.

candidate_resolutions.summary: SURVEY FINDING, RESTATED FRESH AT CYCLE 45 (T2) FROM THE (b) HALF OF attribution-confident-wrong-gap's candidate_resolutions[1], WHERE IT WAS ESTABLISHED AT CYCLE 28 AND WHERE IT REMAINS AS THE AUDIT RECORD. It is restated rather than moved so that no text was cut out of the other issue. THE FINDING: NO SOURCE IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION. src-0002 partitions outputs by correctness only -- its metric section defines accuracy for CTI-MCQ and CTI-RCM, MAD for CTI-VSP, F1 for CTI-ATE, and the three-bucket correct/plausible/incorrect partition for CTI-TAA, and nothing else -- so it records no verbalised confidence, no hedging rate, no calibration metric and no reader-facing plausibility judgement, and no sentence in the paper interprets the correct-versus-plausible gap. src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' block is an LLM-judged 1-5 quality rubric that grades attribution QUALITY rather than how confidently the model asserts it, and per ctr-0008 its 'Attribution' row measures SOURCE LINKING rather than actor identification. src-0004 is a single published passage with no measurement attached at all. THE STATUS IS 'supported' AND WHAT IT SUPPORTS IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE EVIDENCE, NOT ABOUT THE WORLD: it does NOT show the confident-but-wrong gap is small, large, or absent. It shows that nobody in this base has measured it, and that NO CYCLE MAY TREAT AN ATTRIBUTION ERROR RATE AS A PROXY FOR IT. The three source ids are cited as the evidence for the SURVEY -- i.e. these are the sources that were read and found not to measure the quantity -- which is the only sense in which a negative finding can carry evidence at all, and it is stated explicitly here so that a T4 does not mistake this for three sources SUPPORTING a positive claim.

CYCLE 49 (T3), THE FIRST TASK EVER AIMED AT THIS ISSUE, EXTENDED THE SURVEY BEYOND THE KNOWLEDGE BASE AND THE ANSWER DID NOT CHANGE: NO PUBLISHED EVALUATION FOUND BY A FIVE-DIRECTION EXTERNAL SEARCH MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION. The previous candidate was a claim about THIS BASE; this one is a claim about what a targeted search of the published literature returns, and it is deliberately kept separate rather than merged, because the two have different scopes and different failure modes. THE POSITIVE CONTENT OF THE NEGATIVE: there are TWO healthy literatures here and they do not intersect on attribution. One measures verbalised confidence, calibration, selective prediction and abstention in general domains and is large and current. The other -- CTIBench (src-0002), CyberThreat-Eval (src-0007), CyberSOCEval (src-0005), and now src-0023, a KDD-2026-accepted benchmark with an explicit Threat Actor Profiling task -- evaluates CTI attribution BY CORRECTNESS ONLY. src-0023 returned ABSENT for calibration, ECE, Brier, confidence, likelihood, abstain, abstention, uncertain, logprob and 'how certain' across two URL forms serving two different versions of the paper. INDEPENDENTLY, the CTIBench artefact's own executable scorer (src-0019) was read at source and computes correct-and-plausible accuracy and nothing else, with every confidence-related string ABSENT from the notebook -- so for the benchmark this issue descends from, the absence is now confirmed in CODE as well as in prose. That is the second, differently-shaped confirmation methodological rule (v) demands. STATUS IS 'supported' AND WHAT IT SUPPORTS IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE LITERATURE, NOT ABOUT MODELS: it does not show that LLMs are, or are not, confidently wrong when attributing. It shows that the quantity is still not being measured, by anyone cycle 49 could find. SCOPE LIMIT STATED HONESTLY: this is 'not found by five English-language searches plus targeted checks of the nearest benchmarks', which is weaker than 'does not exist', and no cycle may upgrade it to the stronger form.

THE DESIGN QUESTION IN open_questions[3] NOW HAS AN ANSWER, AND IT COMES FROM OPERATIONAL HUMAN PRACTICE RATHER THAN FROM ML: THE MEASUREMENT THIS ISSUE ASKS FOR IS ALREADY A STANDARDISED, MACHINE-READABLE CONSTRUCT -- IT HAS SIMPLY NEVER BEEN APPLIED TO AN LLM ATTRIBUTION EVALUATION. open_questions[3] worried that attribution may be unlike the tasks calibration is normally measured on, because attribution ground truth is contested, aliased and sometimes genuinely underdetermined by the report -- which is why CTIBench needed a 'plausible' bucket -- and concluded that the well-posed target is narrower than 'is the model calibrated': it is whether expressed confidence DISCRIMINATES between reports whose attribution is determined by the evidence and reports whose attribution is not. src-0024, the MISP threat-intelligence best-practice on expressing confidence, shows that human CTI practice resolved exactly this by SPLITTING THE JUDGEMENT IN TWO. It names two taxonomies and gives verbatim tag examples 'estimative-language:likelihood-probability="almost-no-chance"' and 'estimative-language:confidence-in-analytic-judgment="moderate"', alongside 'admiralty-scale:source-reliability="a/b/c..."'. LIKELIHOOD-PROBABILITY grades how likely the claim is to be true; CONFIDENCE-IN-ANALYTIC-JUDGMENT grades confidence in the judgement itself, i.e. in the sufficiency of the evidence and reasoning -- and the two are tagged separately and can move independently. THE SECOND AXIS IS PRECISELY THE QUANTITY open_questions[3] DERIVED, UNDER AN OPERATIONAL NAME. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART: the objection that attribution confidence is too ill-posed to measure because the ground truth is contested DOES NOT HOLD. A well-posed evaluation is constructible today -- elicit both axes on an attribution task and test whether confidence-in-analytic-judgment tracks evidential determinacy while likelihood tracks correctness -- and CTIBench's own correct/plausible/incorrect partition, whose 'plausible' bucket is scoped by src-0002's verbatim definition to reports that LACK SUFFICIENT DETAIL to pinpoint the answer, already supplies a determinacy label to test against. THIS IS A DESIGN CLAIM, NOT A MEASUREMENT. src-0024 contains no LLM, no model and no number, and may never be cited as evidence about model behaviour. Per this issue's own standing permission, recording that no published work measures this WITH the reasoning attached is a legitimate resolution rather than a failure to find an answer -- and this candidate is that resolution's constructive half.

issues.title: Is 'AI-generated CTI reliability' a single property, or does it vary sharply by task type (mechanical extraction vs. open-ended reasoning)?
open_questions: SPLIT NOTE (cycle 16, T2, discharging carry-forward [1] after it was carried unactioned for nine consecutive cycles). This issue now covers ONLY the narrow claim: that AI-generated CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being a single uniform property. The SPECIFIC ORDINAL AXIS ('mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation'), together with the cycle-2 proposed cross-source synthesis that carried it and the open question about whether a better explanatory variable exists, was MOVED VERBATIM to the new issue 'extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis'. The reason for the split is that the two claims have very different evidential status and were sharing one issue and one candidate_resolution from cycle 2 to cycle 15, which is exactly why no T4 could score either honestly: the narrow claim has five independent supporting sources (src-0001, src-0002, src-0006, src-0007, and now src-0013 on the calibration axis) while the ordinal axis is actively disputed between src-0006 and src-0007. Do NOT re-merge them.

src-0006's causal-intervention mitigations raised an attribution-adjacent task (Threat Actor Linking) by only +0.055 accuracy, a much smaller gain than LANCE's ~72-86%->97.6% F1 jump on IoC extraction (src-0003) -- but the two are not a controlled comparison (different tasks, metrics, mitigation types: automated retrieval/inference intervention vs. human-in-the-loop regex+LLM pipeline). No source yet tests a LANCE-style human-validated pipeline specifically on ATT&CK mapping or attribution; a search this cycle for such a study (and for RAM/src-2502.02337, an automated non-human-in-the-loop ATT&CK mapper) found none.
