Does human-in-the-loop validation specifically (not just any targeted mitigation) transfer to reasoning-heavy tasks, and if so how much of the IoC-extraction gain would it recover?

Since src-0003's strong result is single-study/in-house, would the task-dependence conclusion survive an independent replication showing a smaller IoC-extraction advantage? A cycle-6 search for independent LANCE/PRISM replication or critique found none published yet.

candidate_resolutions.summary: The core, narrower claim -- that AI-generated CTI reliability is genuinely task-dependent rather than a single uniform property -- is now supported, not just proposed: src-0006 (cycle 6) directly measures reliability across multiple distinct CTI sub-tasks within one consistent study design (rather than only via cross-benchmark synthesis across different teams/models) and finds F1/AUC ranging roughly 0.20-0.90 by specific sub-task, corroborating the cross-study pattern already visible in src-0001/0002/0003/0005. However, the SPECIFIC ordinal axis proposed above (mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation) is not confirmed by this evidence and is likely too coarse: src-0006 found its failure patterns cut across all 4 CTI pipeline stages it defines, including extraction/contextualization-type tasks, rather than concentrating in 'reasoning' stages. So: task-dependence itself = supported; the specific extraction-vs-reasoning explanatory axis = open, and now positively questioned rather than merely unverified.

ADDED cycle 16 by T2 at the split. Two further within-study measurements strengthen the NARROW claim -- that CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property -- and both are of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task. (1) src-0007: on one expert-annotated corpus drawn from a real company's CTI workflow, the same four models reach IoC-extraction precision 0.8240-0.8846 while scoring 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o) and 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini) precision/recall on MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification, and GPT-4o scores 1.140 out of 5 on the threat-actor Attribution rubric against 3.612 out of 5 for root-cause content in the same table -- roughly a 3x spread across sub-tasks with everything else held constant. (2) src-0013 extends task-dependence to a NEW AXIS that no prior source in this base had tested: reliability varies by sub-task not only in accuracy but in CALIBRATION. Within one study, functional calibration is consistently worse than security calibration for every model tested (delta ECE -0.15/-0.16 GPT-4o-mini, -0.26/-0.27 Gemini-2.0-Flash, -0.52/-0.53 Qwen3-Coder-Next). SCOPE LIMIT ON (2), do not strip it: src-0013 measures secure code generation, not CTI, so it corroborates the SHAPE of task-dependence on a security-adjacent task rather than replicating it on CTI material -- see the cycle-16 scope ruling recorded in 'consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode', which declines to treat security-adjacent corroboration as CTI multi-source support. PROVENANCE ASYMMETRY: src-0007's figures were re-verified verbatim by cycle 15's G2 and are exact to four decimal places; src-0013's are single-pass fetches whose results tables have never been pulled whole (carry-forward [20]). This candidate supports TASK-DEPENDENCE ONLY and deliberately takes no position on the ordinal ranking of sub-tasks, which was moved out of this issue to 'extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis' at the cycle-16 split.

issues.title: Is there a valid ordinal difficulty ranking across CTI sub-tasks (mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation), or is the extraction-vs-reasoning binary too coarse to explain where reliability breaks down?
open_questions: CYCLE-18 HEADLINE, and it changes what this issue is asking. The commensurable measurement that the 'WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE THIS' question below demanded ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE and has since cycle 6: src-0006's Table 2 contains nine rows all reported in F1, over ONE corpus and ONE 15-model set (printed column order G5, Go4, CLD, GEM, LL70, MIX, QWN, GRK, FSC, CB0, ZYS, LLY, CBS, SPT, DHT; 8 general-purpose then 7 cybersecurity-specialised), spanning both ends of the proposed ordering. Restricted to those nine rows the yardstick does not change between sub-tasks, which is exactly the property src-0007 lacks. The table was pulled whole and recomputed at cycle 17, then pulled again from a second URL form and recomputed independently at cycle 18 -- cycle 17's state edits were reverted by the validator, so cycle 18 is the first time this finding has landed. THE ORDERING IS NOT REPRODUCED. Mean F1 across all 15 models, Contextualization ('extraction') stage: IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607, stage mean 0.636. Attribution ('reasoning') stage: TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511, stage mean 0.602. Stage gap 0.034 F1 -- about one fifth of the within-Attribution spread (0.511-0.673) and about one eighth of the mean between-model spread on a single task (0.272). The single BEST task in the whole commensurable subset is TTP Extraction at 0.673, an Attribution-stage task, outscoring every Contextualization task including IOC Normalization: the predicted ordering is not merely weak, it is locally inverted at its strongest predicted point. WHAT IS NOW OPEN: (a) does a 0.034 stage gap survive a SECOND commensurable multi-sub-task study; (b) is 0.034 distinguishable from zero at all, given that src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so this issue cannot presently attach an uncertainty to its own headline number; (c) src-0006's stage labels are the paper's own four-stage pipeline taxonomy and 'Contextualization' is a looser construct than 'mechanical extraction', so a future cycle should test whether re-labelling the nine tasks by output-label-space size rather than by pipeline stage produces a cleaner split.

NEW cycle 18, and it is the strongest replacement hypothesis on the table. On the same nine-row commensurable F1 subset of src-0006's Table 2, the mean BETWEEN-MODEL range within a task is 0.272 (Affected Systems 0.464, False Flag Detection 0.393, Attack Infrastructure 0.371, Patch Recommendation 0.276, TTP Extraction 0.273, Infrastructure Reuse 0.226, Malware Family Mapping 0.155, Relation Graph Building 0.155, IOC Normalization 0.132) and the mean BETWEEN-TASK range within a model is 0.263 (from 0.171 for ZYS up to 0.404 for LL70 and 0.403 for LLY). EQUAL TO WITHIN 0.009. That answers the last inherited open_question below in the affirmative and mis-specifies the axis: task identity is not the dominant explanatory variable, model identity is at least its equal. A further and weaker signal points at CORPUS identity: the same nominal sub-task, ATT&CK TTP mapping, scores F1 0.478-0.751 in src-0006 but a derived F1 of 0.157-0.250 in src-0007 -- a shift of roughly 0.4 on ONE task, larger than any between-task gap either paper reports. That comparison is uncontrolled (task definition, model set, publication year and metric decomposition all differ at once) and is recorded as a lead, not a result. STILL OPEN: is there any study that varies task while holding model fixed and varies model while holding task fixed, reporting variance components rather than leaving them to a reader's arithmetic? No source in this base does.

NEW cycle 18, and it is a caveat on this issue's own headline evidence rather than a question about CTI. Four of the nine commensurable F1 rows in src-0006's Table 2 -- IOC Normalization, Malware Family Mapping, Relation Graph Building, Infrastructure Reuse -- are STRICTLY MONOTONE DECREASING across all eight general-purpose model columns in exactly the printed column order, with unusually smooth decrements. For independent measurements the chance of one row matching a fixed eight-column order is 1/8! = about 1 in 40,320. Cycle 17 counted eleven such rows across all twenty-eight rows of the table and re-pulled ten of them from a second URL form with an explicit instruction to answer 'CANNOT READ' rather than reconstruct; they returned identical cell for cell. Cycle 18 pulled the nine F1 rows again and independently reproduced every cell and every derived mean. So the pattern is as-printed in the paper and is NOT a fetch artefact; its cause is unknown and no cycle should guess at one. It matters because src-0006 is cited by three issues. The cycle-18 headline is deliberately robust to it: dropping all four monotone rows leaves Contextualization 0.641 against Attribution 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, TTP Extraction still the highest single task. SEPARATELY, AND NOW CONFIRMED BY TWO CYCLES: src-0006's stored key_claim describes 'Infrastructure Reuse peaks at F1 0.754 for a specialized agent vs. 0.688 for a general model', but the 0.688 column is ZYS, which sits inside the paper's cyber-specialised block; the general-purpose peak on that row is G5 at 0.677. The comparison's direction survives, the label does not. A corrective key_claim was APPENDED to src-0006's entry in state/knowledge/index.json at cycle 18 -- nothing was deleted or rewritten -- and state/knowledge/src-0006.md was left untouched.

ANSWERED IN PART BY CYCLE 18, kept verbatim because its closing question is still live. Its premise 'reliability ranging F1/AUC ~0.20-0.90' is loose and is corrected above: the true F1 span of the nine commensurable rows is 0.286 (False Flag Detection, LLY) to 0.882 (Affected Systems, LL70). Its closing question -- is there a better explanatory variable than a coarse extraction-vs-reasoning binary -- now has a candidate answer, model identity, entered as a proposed candidate_resolution below. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. MOVED HERE VERBATIM from 'task-dependent-reliability-framing' at the cycle-16 split; originally written by cycle 6. The cross-cutting 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation' ordinal axis is not confirmed and is now positively in doubt: src-0006 (cycle 6), the first source to measure multiple distinct CTI sub-tasks within one consistent study, found its 3 failure patterns (spurious correlations, contradictory knowledge, constrained generalization) occur across all 4 pipeline stages it defines, including 'contextualization'-type tasks that would loosely be called extraction, with reliability ranging F1/AUC ~0.20-0.90 by specific sub-task rather than cleanly by extraction-vs-reasoning category. Is there a better explanatory variable (e.g. heterogeneity/volatility/ambiguity of the specific task's input data, or the size/discreteness of its output label space) than a coarse extraction-vs-reasoning binary?

CYCLE-18 NOTE, prepended not substituted. I re-examined this pair with src-0006's Table 2 in hand and STILL DECLINE to open a G3 contradiction, for the cycle-10 reason endorsed by cycle 16 and repeated verbatim below. What cycle 18 adds is that src-0007's ordinal reading, stated below as fact, does not survive src-0007's own table: the third rung depends entirely on an unstated normalisation of a 1-5 rubric -- GPT-4o's 1.140/5 becomes 0.228 under x/5 or 0.035 under (x-1)/4, against a derived TTP F1 of 0.2502, so attribution either ties classification or is seven times worse -- and the middle-to-third rung ORDERING REVERSES BETWEEN TWO MODELS IN THE SAME TABLE, since o3-mini's 2.968/5 is 0.594 or 0.492, both ABOVE its derived TTP F1 of 0.2337. The SUPPORTS half of the tension below is therefore weaker than it reads. That is a reason to doubt src-0007's ordinal reading, not a reason to declare the two sources in conflict. (Provenance note for a future cycle: the rubric values 1.140 and 2.968 come from cycle 15's verbatim whole-table pull of src-0007's Table 4 and were re-checked at cycle 16, but they are NOT recorded in state/knowledge/src-0007.md, which notes those rows only as existing. They are traceable to src-0007 through the cycle-15 log.) ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. THE CENTRAL TENSION, and why NO contradiction entry was opened -- restated in full at the cycle-16 split so that no future cycle re-litigates it from scratch. src-0007's Table 4 SUPPORTS an ordinal reading: on one corpus with one model set, IoC extraction precision is 0.8240-0.8846, ATT&CK TTP identification precision is 0.2787-0.3480, and the threat-actor Attribution rubric score for GPT-4o is 1.140 out of 5 -- mechanical extraction above technique mapping above attribution, which is the ordering the axis predicts. src-0006's Table 5 OPPOSES it: its failure subtypes span all four pipeline stages it defines, e.g. 'Co-mention bias (Type 1.1) -- stages 1234', so the failure MECHANISMS do not respect the ordering. Cycle 10 examined this pair and DECLINED to open a G3 contradiction, reasoning that src-0006 measures where failure mechanisms OCCUR while src-0007 measures where performance LEVELS differ, and that these are compatible rather than conflicting. Cycle 16 re-read both and did NOT overturn that reasoning: a failure mechanism can be present at every pipeline stage while its impact on measured performance is unequal across those stages, and both facts can hold simultaneously. That is precisely why this is an OPEN ISSUE and not a contradiction -- the two sources are not in conflict; the AXIS is simply not established by either of them.

SUPERSEDED BY CYCLE 18, kept verbatim because its commensurability standard is the right standard and cycle 18 met it, not because the question is still open. The bar it sets was cleared by src-0006's Table 2, which cycle 16 did not know contained nine same-metric rows. Its closing instruction -- 'until a commensurable cross-sub-task measurement exists, this issue should not rise above proposed' -- is therefore DISCHARGED and no longer binds a T4. One half of it survives as a finding rather than a question: the commensurability objection FAILS for the extraction-vs-classification rung of src-0007 and HOLDS for the third rung. Solving 2PR/(P+R) for the unreported IoC recall at which each model's IoC F1 would fall to its own derived TTP F1 gives crossovers of 0.1475 (GPT-4o), 0.1354 (o3-mini), 0.1180 (GPT-4o FT) and 0.0887 (GPT-4o-mini FT), every one BELOW that same model's actual TTP recall of 0.2270, 0.1759, 0.1846 and 0.1414 respectively. So if IoC recall were merely as bad as TTP recall, the gap survives for all four models; it breaks only if IoC recall is worse than TTP recall by a further factor of 1.3-1.6, i.e. an absolute recall of 0.09-0.15, which no source in this base reports for report-level extraction. The precision-only omission is a real reporting defect and is NOT an explanation of src-0007's extraction-vs-TTP gap. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE THIS (cycle 16): a single study measuring ONE commensurable metric across sub-tasks spanning the full proposed ordering, on ONE corpus with ONE model set. src-0007 comes closest and still falls short, because its yardstick changes between rows -- IoC extraction reports precision only (no recall, no F1, and the paper gives no reason for the omission, a fact cycle 15's whole-table pull confirmed is real rather than a fetch artefact), TTP identification reports precision and recall, and drafting reports a 1-5 rubric. Its apparent ordering is therefore partly an artefact of changing the measurement instrument between sub-tasks. Until a commensurable cross-sub-task measurement exists, this issue should not rise above 'proposed'.

ANSWERED BY CYCLE 18, in the affirmative -- see the between-model-versus-between-task entry above (0.272 against 0.263, equal to within 0.009). The AUC 0.912-versus-0.547 pair this question cites was re-verified exact at cycle 17 and is an instance of the pattern rather than an outlier. Kept verbatim because it is the question that turned out to matter most. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. Does the ordering, if it holds at all, hold WITHIN a stage as well as between stages? src-0006 reports F1/AUC ~0.20-0.90 across tasks and models including a spread as wide as AUC 0.912 vs 0.547 for two different models on the SAME task (Source Reliability Scoring). If between-model variance on one task is comparable to between-task variance, then task identity is not the dominant explanatory variable and the axis is mis-specified regardless of which way the between-task comparison comes out.

candidate_resolutions.summary: MOVED VERBATIM from 'task-dependent-reliability-framing' at the cycle-16 T2 split; this text was originally written by cycle 2 and its status of 'proposed' is carried over unchanged. It is reproduced here rather than rewritten, and it is the ordinal-axis half of what was previously one conflated issue. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. Across the 5 collected sources, reliability of AI-generated CTI is strongly task-dependent rather than a uniform property: narrow, mechanical extraction (IoC extraction, src-0003) reaches near-97% F1 when LLM output is constrained and human-validated, while open-ended reasoning tasks (ATT&CK technique mapping, threat-actor attribution, general threat-intel reasoning: src-0001, src-0002, src-0005) remain unreliable (accuracy ceilings around 52-72%, confidence miscalibration, and plausible-but-wrong outputs) even as model scale increases. This framing is a synthesis of currently-available evidence, not itself directly measured by any single source, and should be treated as a working hypothesis pending the open questions above. CYCLE-16 ANNOTATION, appended not substituted: the part of this text that survives the split into the parent issue is task-dependence itself, which is now supported there by five sources. What remains HERE and remains merely proposed is the ORDERING -- the claim that the extraction-vs-reasoning distinction is what explains the spread. Note also that the strongest number in this text, src-0003's 97.6% F1, is itself one side of the open contradiction ctr-0001, in which src-0007 measures an unscaffolded LLM at 0.82-0.88 precision on the same broad task; if ctr-0001 resolves in favour of the scaffolding explanation, then the top of this proposed ordering is measuring pipeline design rather than task difficulty, and the axis loses its clearest supporting datapoint. CYCLE-18 REJECTION, appended not substituted; the cycle-16 annotation and the original cycle-2 text above are preserved word for word and the provenance header stands. STATUS CHANGED FROM 'proposed' TO 'rejected'. What is rejected is the ORDINAL AXIS ONLY -- the claim that a mechanical-extraction-versus-open-ended-reasoning distinction is what explains the spread in CTI reliability. Task-dependence itself is NOT rejected; it lives, supported by five sources, in the parent issue 'task-dependent-reliability-framing'. REASON: the one commensurable within-study measurement in this knowledge base, src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows over one corpus and 15 models, puts the Attribution stage only 0.034 F1 below the Contextualization stage while making an Attribution-stage task -- TTP Extraction at 0.673 -- the best-performing task in the entire subset; and src-0007, the source whose numbers this text leans on for the reasoning end, orders its own middle and third rungs OPPOSITELY for GPT-4o and o3-mini, on a rubric normalisation the paper never states. An ordering that is locally inverted at its strongest predicted point in one study, and that reverses between two models of the same family in another, is not a property of the tasks. See this issue's open_questions for the full derivation and its three caveats.

SUPPORTED, entered cycle 18. The identical finding was produced by cycle 17, whose state edits the validator reverted; cycle 18 re-pulled src-0006's Table 2 from a second URL form and re-derived every mean, range and crossover independently before landing it. THE CLAIM: the proposed ordinal axis 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation' is NOT supported by the only commensurable cross-sub-task measurement available in this base, and the extraction-versus-reasoning binary is too coarse to explain where CTI reliability breaks down. TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES, from two unaffiliated teams on two corpora with two disjoint model sets. (1) src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows -- one corpus, one 15-model set, one metric -- gives a Contextualization stage mean of 0.636 (IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607) against an Attribution stage mean of 0.602 (TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511). The 0.034 gap is in the predicted direction but is roughly one eighth of the 0.272 mean between-model spread on a single task, and the best task in the subset is an Attribution-stage task. (2) src-0007's Table 4, the source that appears to support the ordering, reverses its own middle-to-third rung between two models: GPT-4o's attribution rubric of 1.140/5 normalises to 0.228 or 0.035 against a derived TTP F1 of 0.2502 (at or below), while o3-mini's 2.968/5 normalises to 0.594 or 0.492 against 0.2337 (above), under both defensible normalisations. THREE MATERIAL CAVEATS. (a) src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so 0.034 carries no uncertainty estimate; this candidate asserts that the ordering is NOT SUPPORTED, not that the reverse ordering holds. (b) Four of the nine rows are strictly monotone decreasing across all eight general-purpose columns in printed order, a pattern of unknown cause verified as-printed by three pulls across two URL forms; dropping all four leaves 0.641 against 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, same best task. (c) The fourth rung of the proposed ordering, open-ended GENERATION, is not represented in the commensurable subset at all, so this candidate refutes the extraction-versus-classification-versus-attribution part of the ordering and is SILENT on generation, which remains supported in the parent issue by src-0001's extraction-versus-generation confidence-interval-width split of 0.02 against 0.06.

PROPOSED, entered cycle 18 as the replacement explanatory variable this issue's inherited first open_question asked for. THE CLAIM: model identity explains as much of the variance in CTI sub-task reliability as sub-task identity does, corpus identity may explain more than either, and the extraction-versus-reasoning category is a weak third. On src-0006's nine-row commensurable F1 subset the mean between-model range within a task is 0.272 and the mean between-task range within a model is 0.263 -- equal to within 0.009 -- while the extraction-versus-reasoning stage gap on those same rows is 0.034. Separately, the same nominal sub-task, ATT&CK TTP mapping, scores F1 0.478-0.751 in src-0006 against a derived F1 of 0.157-0.250 in src-0007: a shift of roughly 0.4 on one task, larger than any between-task gap either paper reports. THREE OBJECTIONS TO ITSELF, which is why this is proposed and not supported. (i) The between-model and between-task figures are RANGES, not variance components; a range is sensitive to a single outlying model, and src-0006's LLY is an outlier on two of the nine rows (False Flag Detection 0.286, Patch Recommendation 0.442). (ii) The cross-source TTP comparison is uncontrolled -- task definition, model set, publication year and metric decomposition all differ at once -- so corpus identity is only one of at least four candidate explanations for that 0.4 shift. (iii) Both figures come from ONE study's table, and no cycle has checked whether the same equality holds in any other multi-model multi-task security evaluation; src-0014's roughly fourfold spread in prompt-sensitivity between models on identical data introduces a fourth variable, prompt strategy, that this candidate does not account for at all.

issues.title: Have AI-generated CTI failures already reached production/publication at real institutions, and how do institutions respond when caught?
open_questions: REWRITTEN cycle 12, and deliberately reframed so it stops being answerable by anecdote. The base rate of hallucinated citations across CTI PUBLISHERS is still unmeasured and no cycle should claim otherwise: we now have two named incidents (ENISA src-0004, EY Canada src-0012), and two anecdotes are not a rate. What was found instead is the nearest systematic audit in an ADJACENT population -- src-0011 (GhostCite) manually verified 2.2M citations across 56,381 papers and reports 1.01% of papers at Security venues containing at least one invalid citation. It cannot be transferred to CTI: it audits peer-reviewed conference papers, defines a ghost citation as one absent from academic databases (inapplicable to CTI footnotes, which are news/vendor URLs), and reports per-PAPER rates that are not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE THIS: (a) a link-resolution/footnote-verification sweep over N published threat reports from M agencies and vendors, which is mechanically cheap since both known incidents were found precisely this way (dead links); (b) a disclosure-policy survey of CTI publishers; or (c) an existing audit of vendor/agency reports if one can be found. Cycle 12 searched for (c) and found only academic-corpus and consulting-report audits, never a CTI-publisher audit. AMENDED CYCLE 59, DISCHARGING ctr-0022 STEP (iv), AND THE AMENDMENT IS A NARROWING, NOT AN ANSWER. That closing sentence about (c) is now SUPERSEDED IN ONE SPECIFIC AND LIMITED WAY: such a sweep EXISTS AND IS RUNNING. GPTZero states verbatim 'Over the past few months we have set up an automated pipeline to search for vibe citations by finding and scanning public reports from major consulting firms.' That is exactly the link-resolution/footnote-verification sweep option (a) asks for, applied to consulting firms rather than to CTI publishers proper. BUT IT IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF SUPPLYING THE BASE RATE THIS QUESTION ASKS FOR, AND THE REASON IS ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED: asked DIRECTLY for any total number of reports scanned, or any rate or percentage of reports found to contain hallucinated citations across the sweep, the page returned ABSENT. THE DENOMINATOR IS WITHHELD. GPTZero publishes NUMERATORS ONLY, one instalment at a time -- verbatim, 'Instead of releasing our results all at once, we are going to focus on one report at a time.' A serially-released stream of named incidents with no reported N is a source of ANECDOTES, however many of them there are, and stacking more of them will never produce a rate. CONSEQUENCE FOR FUTURE CYCLES, STATED SO THIS IS NOT REDISCOVERED: fetching GPTZero's further named investigations (a government publication and two different Deloitte reports, unfetched since cycle 13) would add INCIDENTS to this issue and is legitimate T1 work, but it CANNOT close this open question and no cycle should score it as if it could. What would still close (a) is a sweep by a party that publishes its N -- including, in principle, this loop running one itself over a named list of published threat reports, which remains mechanically cheap and undone. Cycle 13 recorded the GPTZero pipeline as 'a T1 collection lead'; no cycle in the forty-six since had recorded that the lead cannot yield a base rate as published.

PARTIALLY ANSWERED cycle 12, first half CLOSED. ENISA's AI usage was NOT disclosed to readers before publication and was admitted only when Der Spiegel asked after external researchers found the dead links (src-0004). Stronger now: ENISA's own publication pages for BOTH affected reports (src-0009, src-0010) carry revision notices dated 09 January 2026 describing the fix purely mechanically -- 'updated to edit some links' and 'updated to correct some broken links and typos' -- and as of 2026-07-29, roughly 8 months after exposure, NEITHER page carries any mention of AI or generative AI. So the non-disclosure was not merely pre-publication; it persists in the corrected record. STILL OPEN: whether ENISA changed any internal policy (a cycle-12 search found no published policy change), and whether any peer agency changed disclosure policy in response. Also still open at PDF level: the front matter / legal notice of the v1.2 PDFs was not pulled, so the 'no AI disclosure anywhere' claim is currently established only for the landing pages.

PARTIALLY ANSWERED cycle 12, and the answer for the NUMBER is no. ENISA's own primary artefacts (src-0009, src-0010) independently corroborate the STRUCTURE of the incident -- two reports, published October 1 and November 6 2025, both revised on 09 January 2026, both revisions concerning links -- exactly as src-0004 reports secondhand. But neither ENISA page gives any footnote count and neither mentions AI, so the 26-of-492 figure remains sourced to Der Spiegel via Heise and is corroborated only by outlets (cybernews, Tagesspiegel, derStandard) that themselves cite Der Spiegel, i.e. NOT independently. NOTE FOR FUTURE CYCLES: Der Spiegel's original article could not be retrieved -- spiegel.de is blocked to this agent's user agent (WebSearch returns HTTP 400 'domains are not accessible to our user agent'), so this is an infrastructure limit, not an unsearched direction; do not burn budget retrying it the same way. The remaining routes to the number are counting the footnotes in the archived v1.1/original PDF against v1.2, or locating Prof. Christian Dietrich's / Institut fuer Internet-Sicherheit's own writeup. ENISA's silence is NOT a contradiction of src-0004 and no G3 entry was opened: the notices assign no cause at all rather than a competing one.

NEW cycle 12. Institutional responses to the SAME failure mode diverged sharply -- EY Canada withdrew the offending report entirely and issued a statement invoking its 'organisation-wide commitment to the responsible use of AI' (src-0012), while ENISA retained both reports, patched the links, and described the correction without reference to AI (src-0009, src-0010). What predicts which response an institution gives: commercial reputational exposure vs public-mandate insulation, the presence of a named external investigator, the share of citations affected (16/27 = 59% for EY vs 26/492 = 5% for ENISA), or something else? Two cases cannot distinguish these; more incidents with recorded responses would.

NEW cycle 12, FIRST CLAUSE CORRECTED CYCLE 59 (ctr-0022 step (ii) location (b)). THE ORIGINAL WORDING, PRESERVED HERE SO THE CORRECTION IS AUDITABLE, READ: 'BOTH known incidents were discovered from the outside by parties clicking through footnotes (Westfaelische Hochschule researchers for ENISA, GPTZero for EY), and in neither case did the publisher's internal QA catch it.' THE 'GPTZero for EY' HALF OF THAT IS REFUTED AT SOURCE. THE CORRECTED STATEMENT, WHICH IS WHAT THIS QUESTION NOW ASSERTS: BOTH known incidents were caught EXTERNALLY rather than by the publisher's internal QA, but by MATERIALLY DIFFERENT external routes -- the ENISA case was an unprompted discovery by Westfaelische Hochschule researchers reading a report and clicking its footnotes, whereas the EY report was published as one instalment of a targeted, automated, serially-released commercial sweep by an AI-detection vendor. NOT ESTABLISHED AND NOT TO BE WRITTEN: the GPTZero page was asked DIRECTLY how this specific EY report came to its attention and returned ABSENT, so 'the pipeline found EY' is NOT established; what is established is that the report was published as an instalment of the sweep. THE QUESTION ITSELF IS UNAFFECTED AND STILL OPEN, because the shared property it turns on -- that internal QA caught neither -- survives the correction intact. src-0011 supplies a measured analogue of why in academic publishing (76.7% of surveyed reviewers do not thoroughly check references; 80.0% never suspect fake citations). Does ANY CTI publisher run automated link-resolution or citation-verification on reports before release, and is there a single documented case of this failure mode being caught internally? No source in the base documents one.

candidate_resolutions.summary: At least one major institutional CTI publisher (ENISA, the EU's cybersecurity agency) published AI-hallucinated citations in production threat-landscape reports (Oct/Nov 2025), including a technical fingerprint consistent with LLM-generated text. FINGERPRINT RENDERING CORRECTED AT CYCLE 59 (ctr-0012 step (iv)). THE ORIGINAL WORDING, PRESERVED SO THE CORRECTION IS AUDITABLE, DESCRIBED IT AS PROSE: 'misattributing the name APT29 to Microsoft's naming convention, when Microsoft actually uses Midnight Blizzard'. THE SOURCE DESCRIBES A FABRICATED HYPERLINK, verbatim: 'For example, a link to a Microsoft page about the Russian hacker group APT29 also contained this name - but Microsoft itself refers to the group as Midnight Blizzard.' That is a hallucinated CITATION TARGET -- a URL whose path string carries APT29 where a real Microsoft URL would carry Midnight Blizzard -- not a factual naming error in body text. THE CORRECTED READING IS STRONGER evidence of LLM fabrication than the original and weakens nothing: it makes the fingerprint an instance of the SAME defect class as the 26 broken footnotes (fabricated citation targets) rather than a separate prose-accuracy failure. NOTE FOR ANY CYCLE TOUCHING consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode OR attribution-confident-wrong-gap: cycle 28's finding that this defect is INVISIBLE to src-0002's CTI-TAA scoring rule (which credits any correct alias) is UNAFFECTED and if anything reinforced, since a fabricated URL is even further outside what an alias-tolerant attribution metric can see. The failure was caught by external academic researchers checking footnote links, not by internal QA, and the agency's public response ('human errors') did not fully acknowledge AI CAUSATION even after exposure -- but see candidate_resolutions[3], amended at cycle 59: ENISA DID publicly accept RESPONSIBILITY, and the phrase 'did not fully acknowledge AI attribution' must be read narrowly as being about CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION, not about acceptance of responsibility. This establishes existence of the failure mode in production but not its frequency/base rate across the CTI industry.

ADDED cycle 12. The ENISA incident is no longer carried by a single secondary source. ENISA's own publication pages for both named reports independently corroborate the incident's verifiable structure: 'ENISA Threat Landscape 2025' (published 1 Oct 2025) carries 'Revision Notice - Version 1.2. (09 January 2026): This publication has been updated to edit some links.' and the sectorial 'Public Administration' report (published 6 Nov 2025) carries 'Revision Notice - Version 1.2 (09 January 2026): This publication has been updated to correct some broken links and typos.' Two reports, October and November 2025, both corrected for links on the same January 2026 date -- matching src-0004's secondhand account on report count, dates and defect type. What ENISA's own record does NOT contain is any footnote count and any mention of AI, so the 26/492 figure and the AI attribution remain dependent on Der Spiegel via Heise.

ADDED cycle 12. The failure mode RECURS across institution types and is not an ENISA idiosyncrasy. EY Canada's 2025 report 'Points of Attack: Uncovering Cyber Threats and Fraud in Loyalty Systems' was found by GPTZero (14 May 2026) to have 16 of 27 references hallucinated, with 'more than a half-dozen footnotes led to dead webpages or did not contain the cited information'; EY Canada removed the study from its website. This is a commercial Big Four publisher of security/fraud content, published roughly six months later. ROUTE CLAIM CORRECTED AT CYCLE 59 (ctr-0022 step (ii) location (c)). THE ORIGINAL WORDING, PRESERVED SO THE CORRECTION IS AUDITABLE, READ 'discovered by the same route as ENISA (an outside party clicking through footnotes)'. THAT IS REFUTED AT SOURCE. THE DEFENSIBLE STATEMENT: both incidents were caught EXTERNALLY rather than by the publisher's internal QA, but by MATERIALLY DIFFERENT external routes -- ENISA by an unprompted discovery by researchers reading a report, EY as one instalment of a targeted, automated, serially-released commercial sweep. The sweep is described by its operator verbatim: 'Over the past few months we have set up an automated pipeline to search for vibe citations by finding and scanning public reports from major consulting firms.' and 'Instead of releasing our results all at once, we are going to focus on one report at a time.' NOT ESTABLISHED: the page was asked DIRECTLY how this specific report came to its attention and returned ABSENT, so 'the pipeline found EY' must not be written. INDEPENDENCE REASSESSED AT CYCLE 59 (ctr-0022 step (iii)), AND THIS CANDIDATE IS WEAKENED WITHOUT BEING REJECTED. The original wording ran 'Two independent institutions, one public and one commercial, is materially stronger than one for the EXISTENCE and RECURRENCE claim -- and still says nothing about frequency.' Under methodological rule (xxi), independence of SOURCE is a different question from independence of DISCOVERY, and this pair is independent in the first sense only: two unrelated publishers, two unrelated outlets, but ONE chance discovery and ONE selected instalment of a hunt designed to find exactly this failure mode, run by a vendor whose product is AI detection and who characterises the problem as 'already endemic'. THE SPLIT THAT SURVIVES. (A) The EXISTENCE claim is UNDAMAGED and arguably strengthened: a case sampled from a targeted sweep is still a real case, verified by manual footnote checking, and its provenance does not make it less real. The institutional-type spread (public agency, Big Four commercial) also stands, since that is a property of the publishers rather than of the discovery route. (B) The RECURRENCE-AS-INDEPENDENT-EVENT claim is OVERSTATED as originally worded and is hereby DOWNGRADED. Two events are two independent draws only if found independently; a hit drawn from a population selected for the purpose tells you the phenomenon exists IN THE HUNTED POPULATION, not that it recurs at large. The selection is maximally adverse because the vendor states it is releasing findings ONE AT A TIME, so the observed sequence is an artefact of a release schedule rather than of an incidence process. ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ctr-0022 STEP (iii) POSES -- does the recurrence claim now need a third incident found by an unprompted route: YES, and this cycle records that requirement explicitly. As things stand this base holds exactly ONE unprompted-route incident (ENISA). A third incident drawn from the SAME GPTZero sweep -- the government publication or either Deloitte report, all unfetched since cycle 13 -- would add existence evidence and institutional-type spread but would NOT repair the independence defect, because it is another draw from the same selected population. A T4 must not read incident COUNT as independence. STATUS IS HELD AT 'supported' rather than demoted, because limb (A) is what the candidate's headline sentence asserts and limb (A) is intact; the demotion is written into the text rather than into the status field, and a T4 scoring this issue should score limb (B) lower than cycle 12 did. Scope note: loyalty-systems fraud is security-adjacent published content, not threat intelligence in the narrow IoC/TTP/attribution sense measured elsewhere in this knowledge base.

ADDED cycle 12. On the issue's second question -- how institutions respond when caught -- the two documented cases diverge, so there is no single institutional response pattern to report. EY Canada WITHDREW the report and issued a statement referencing accuracy and 'an organisation-wide commitment to the responsible use of AI', saying it was reviewing why the study was published. ENISA RETAINED both reports, issued v1.2 corrections describing only link edits and typos, characterised the underlying errors to the press as 'human errors' while confirming AI was permitted for 'minor editorial revisions', and as of 2026-07-29 carries no AI disclosure on either publication page. The common element across both is that neither institution's internal QA detected the problem and both were corrected only after external publication of the finding. AMENDED AT CYCLE 59 (ctr-0012 step (iii)), AND THE AMENDMENT NARROWS THE DIVERGENCE THIS CANDIDATE ASSERTS. EVERY INDIVIDUAL CLAUSE ABOVE IS TRUE; THE DEFECT IS BY SELECTION, NOT BY ASSERTION. The above sets EY (withdrew, accountability statement) against ENISA ('human errors') as diverging on acceptance of responsibility. THE OMITTED MATERIAL, which appears in the SAME SENTENCE of src-0004 that supplies the 'human errors' framing, verbatim: 'Enisa, which has an annual budget of around 27 million euros, admitted the errors when asked by Der Spiegel magazine, speaking of -deficiencies- for which it takes responsibility.' -- hyphens standing for the page's double quotation marks around the single word deficiencies. ON THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS BOTH INSTITUTIONS PUBLICLY ACCEPTED RESPONSIBILITY, so a divergence over acceptance of responsibility IS NOT ESTABLISHED and must not be asserted. THE DIVERGENCE THAT IS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, and which this candidate now asserts instead, is over TWO THINGS ONLY: (1) REMEDY -- EY WITHDREW the report; ENISA RETAINED both and patched the links; and (2) CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION -- EY's statement names AI ('an organisation-wide commitment to the responsible use of AI'); ENISA attributed cause to human error and confined the AI's role to 'minor editorial revisions', and as of 2026-07-29 neither publication page carries any AI mention. That narrower divergence is independently corroborated: src-0009 and src-0010 are ENISA's own revision notices, mechanical and AI-free, against src-0012's withdrawal. IT ALSO SURVIVES THE ctr-0022 CORRECTION UNTOUCHED, because how each incident was DISCOVERED is logically independent of how each institution RESPONDED once told. The common element stated above -- neither internal QA detected the problem, both corrected only after external publication -- is likewise unaffected and remains the strongest single sentence in this candidate.

ADDED cycle 12, status PROPOSED and deliberately not promoted -- read the scope limit before citing. No base rate for hallucinated citations in CTI publications exists. The closest systematic measurement is src-0011 (GhostCite), which manually verified a flagged subset of 2.2M citations across 56,381 papers at top AI/ML and Security venues (2020-2025) and found 1.07% of papers overall, and 1.01% of papers at Security venues, containing at least one invalid or fabricated citation, with an 80.9% increase in 2025 alone and the authors calling their figure 'a conservative lower bound'. This is NOT the CTI rate and must not be quoted as one: different population (peer-reviewed conference papers, which have reviewers; CTI reports have none), different citation ecology (academic references vs news/vendor URLs), and different denominator (per-paper vs src-0004's per-footnote 26/492). What it does support is a directional claim -- that fabricated citations survive into refereed security literature at a nonzero and rising rate despite peer review -- which makes it implausible that unrefereed CTI publishing is cleaner. That inference is the proposed part, and no source tests it.

ADDED CYCLE 59, AND ITS PRIMARY PURPOSE IS TO DISCHARGE ctr-0018 STEP (iv): src-0022 HAD BEEN CITED BY NO ISSUE AND NO ASSESSMENT SINCE IT WAS COLLECTED AT CYCLE 43. Cycle 50 checked every candidate_resolutions.evidence array and every scores.evidence array in the state and found ZERO references to it, and named that as 'the real reason eight cycles of calling it the highest-value uncollected source have produced no score movement'. A source nothing cites cannot move any score. THE CLAIM: a THIRD documented institution has suffered a production-level impact from AI-generated security content, and it is the only one of the three where the institution abandoned a PROCESS rather than correcting a DOCUMENT. curl shut down its bug-bounty programme. Verbatim from the maintainer, Daniel Stenberg, 26 January 2026: 'There is no longer a curl bug-bounty program. It officially stops on January 31, 2026.' Programme scale to that date, verbatim: '87 confirmed vulnerabilities and over 100,000 USD paid as rewards to researchers.' QUANTITATIVE CORE, A BEFORE/AFTER PAIR: 'Previous years we have had a rate of somewhere north of 15% of the submissions ending up confirmed vulnerabilities.' against 'Starting 2025, the confirmed-rate plummeted to below 5%. Not even one in twenty was real.' -- roughly a three-fold fall in confirmed-valid rate. WHY THIS BELONGS TO THIS ISSUE: the issue asks whether AI-generated CTI failures have reached production at real institutions and how institutions respond when caught, and this is a real institution responding to AI-generated security reporting by CLOSING THE INTAKE PROCESS ENTIRELY -- reliability failure measured not by a benchmark but by an institution abandoning a process. It also materially widens the institutional-type spread, which previously ran public agency (ENISA) and Big Four commercial (EY) and now adds a major open-source project. FOUR LIMITS, WHICH ARE WHY THIS IS ENTERED AS 'supported' FOR A NARROW CLAIM AND NOT AS EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING BROADER. (1) THE STATED CAUSE IS THREE COMBINED TRENDS, NOT AI ALONE, and this is the thing a successor is most likely to get wrong. Verbatim: 'There are these three bad trends combined that makes us take this step: the mind-numbing AI slop, humans doing worse than ever and the apparent will to poke holes rather than to help.' ANY RENDERING OF THIS AS 'curl closed its bounty because of AI' IS AN OVER-ATTRIBUTION and must be scoped to that sentence. (2) NEITHER RATE IS DECOMPOSED BY WHETHER A REPORT WAS AI-GENERATED, so the 15%/5% pair is NOT an AI-attributable error rate and must not be used as one. The baseline window is also UNDEFINED ('previous years', no years named), so no per-year rate of change may be derived. (3) SELF-REPORTED. Personal blog post by an interested party, not peer reviewed, no external audit; Stenberg is the maintainer whose time was consumed and is describing his own decision, and all figures are his report of his own programme's records. 'somewhere north of' is his own explicit approximation. (4) N=1, and an unusually high-profile, unusually thin-staffed institution, so nothing here generalises to bounty programmes at large and nothing here measures any specific LLM. PROHIBITED FIGURE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REINTRODUCED: secondary coverage attributes a '~20% of all reports are AI-generated' figure to Stenberg. IT IS NOT IN THE POST -- ABSENT on the permalink AND on the monthly-archive rendering, a confirmed absence on two URL forms per rule (v) -- and it MUST NOT be entered into this state from a search snippet. NOTE ON THE DISCOVERY-ROUTE QUESTION THIS ISSUE NOW TRACKS: this case is not a citation-hallucination incident at all and was not 'discovered' by any external auditor -- it was DISCLOSED BY THE AFFECTED INSTITUTION ITSELF, which makes it a THIRD and distinct route and the only self-disclosed case in the base. It is therefore NOT the unprompted-route third incident that candidate_resolutions[2] says the RECURRENCE claim needs, because it is a different failure mode (inbound report quality, not published-citation fabrication).

issues.title: Do LLM-based security triage and response systems fail by accepting or acting on far too much -- an under-refusal failure that accuracy-based evaluation does not detect?
open_questions: IS OVER-ACCEPTANCE A PROPERTY OF THE MODELS OR OF THE HARNESS? This is the issue's central unknown and neither source addresses it. Neither src-0007 nor src-0015 varies the decision threshold, the stated cost of a false positive in the prompt, the availability of an explicit abstain option, or the presence of a human confirmation step. src-0003 established for a different sub-task (IoC extraction) that scaffolding around the model can dominate measured reliability; the analogous experiment for triage -- does an explicit abstain option, a stated false-positive cost, or a required evidence-fetch step move precision (Accepted) off 0.27-0.40 -- has not been run by any source in this base. Until it is, 'the models under-refuse' and 'these harnesses were built with no refusal affordance' are indistinguishable.

WHAT IS THE OPERATIONAL COST, and is it actually worse than the status quo? Neither source converts its false-positive rate into analyst hours, containment blast radius, or alert-fatigue effects, so precision (Accepted) of 0.27 cannot yet be compared against human triage on any common currency. Note a structural obstacle: src-0007's ground truth IS the human analyst's accept/reject decision, so by construction it carries no human error bar and cannot tell us whether human triage would score better on its own benchmark.

MERGED IN FROM carry-forward [15] at the cycle-16 split decision; cycle 12 excluded this from the knowledge base as a source and cycle 16 judges it belongs HERE, as an open question rather than as evidence. The mirror image of automated over-acceptance is AI-generated security claims arriving INBOUND in volume: curl ended its HackerOne bug bounty on 31 January 2026 after a flood of AI-generated 'slop' vulnerability reports, with reported figures of roughly 20% of submissions being AI slop by mid-2025 and the confirmed-vulnerability rate falling from about 15% historically to under 5%. 'AI slop arrives inbound AND automated triage cannot filter it' is a coherent single problem that this issue and carry-forward [15] describe better jointly than either does alone -- and it has a sharp practical edge, because if automated triage accepts 60-73% of what human analysts reject, it is precisely the wrong instrument for the volume problem it is most often proposed to solve. THIS IS NOT YET EVIDENCE AND MUST NOT BE CITED AS SUCH: no curl/HackerOne source exists in state/knowledge/index.json and a T2 must not invent sources (G1). A future T1 should collect it, reported at bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/curl-ending-bug-bounty-program-after-flood-of-ai-slop-reports/. Until collected, this is a question, not a claim.

Does the under-refusal generalise to the CTI sub-tasks measured elsewhere in this base? If a model were asked to extract IoCs or map ATT&CK techniques with an explicit 'insufficient evidence' option available, would it use it? src-0014 supplies this base's only abstention data -- self-consistency collapsing coverage to 24.04-60.85% -- but on vulnerability detection rather than CTI, and it measures abstention INDUCED by sampling disagreement rather than abstention OFFERED as a choice, so it does not answer this.

Is there a trade-off frontier, or is this simply a badly-set threshold? src-0007's recall (Accepted) of 0.90-1.00 alongside precision of 0.27-0.40 is consistent with a threshold set to maximise recall; nobody has published the precision the same models reach at a recall of, say, 0.7. If the frontier is favourable, this is a tuning problem and largely solved; if precision stays low across the whole frontier, it is a capability problem. No source in this base reports a precision-recall curve for triage.

candidate_resolutions.summary: CREATED cycle 16 by T2, discharging carry-forward [3] and merging carry-forward [15]; six cycles elapsed between the first proposal of this issue and the first cycle with standing to create it. Two independent sources -- different teams, different task framings, different model generations, different years -- find the same failure: the decision threshold is set so permissively that the system accepts or acts on most of what a human analyst would reject. src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026) measures automated triage on a real company's daily CTI workflow and reports an extreme asymmetry, recall (Accepted) 0.90-1.00 against precision (Accepted) 0.27-0.40 across all four models tested. src-0015 (OpenSec, Jan 2026) measures frontier incident-response agents over 40 episodes per model and finds GPT-5.2 containing in 100% of episodes at an 82.5% false-positive rate, DeepSeek 3.2 92.5% at 65%, Gemini 3 75% at 57.5%, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 62.5% at 45%, with an evidence-gated action rate of only 0.375-0.542 -- every model acts without first fetching trusted evidence about the target entity on a majority or near-majority of its containment actions. WHY THIS IS AN ISSUE AND NOT A FOOTNOTE UNDER ACCURACY: src-0015 locates the defect precisely, stating that 'All models correctly identify the ground-truth threat when they act; the calibration gap is not in detection but in restraint.' Detection accuracy is fine. These systems would be scored WELL by essentially every metric used elsewhere in this knowledge base, and the defect is invisible to all of them -- which is exactly the argument for giving it its own issue rather than filing it under an existing accuracy-shaped one. PROVENANCE ASYMMETRY, do not flatten it: src-0007 is institutionally affiliated, methodologically detailed, and had all nine of its stored Table 4 rows re-verified verbatim by cycle 15's G2 exact to four decimal places; src-0015 is by its own recorded assessment the weakest-provenance source in this base -- single-author preprint filed cs.AI, no stated venue, peer review or affiliation, n=40 synthetic RL-seed episodes per model with no confidence intervals, and only the GPT-5.2-versus-Sonnet-4.5 contrast robust, with the middle two models' ordering unresolved. The claim therefore RESTS on src-0007; src-0015 corroborates its direction on a different task and a newer model generation, which is worth a great deal for showing the failure is not one benchmark's artefact, and is worth little as independent quantification. ONE POOLING ERROR TO AVOID: src-0015's 'calibration' is an action-threshold construct (false-positive rate, evidence-gating), NOT the ECE/Brier confidence calibration of src-0001 and src-0013, and the two must never be averaged or quoted as the same measurement.

contradictions.description: ONE ISSUE ASSERTS AS SUPPORTED EXACTLY WHAT ANOTHER ISSUE HAS FORMALLY WITHDRAWN, ON THE SAME TABLE AND THE SAME NUMBERS. Opened by the cycle-33 T4 while pricing carry-forward [47](d) and [34]. This is a conflict between two SUPPORTED claims inside this state, which is precisely G3's test, and it is filed nowhere else: ctr-0008 covers only the 1.140-versus-3.612 half and is filed against a DIFFERENT issue_id, and ctr-0004 is filed against ioc-extraction-reliability. NO contradiction entry has ever been filed against task-dependent-reliability-framing. THE CLAIM IN CONFLICT, verbatim from this issue's SECOND candidate_resolution (status 'supported', evidence [src-0007, src-0013], added cycle 16 by T2): 'Two further within-study measurements strengthen the NARROW claim -- that CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property -- and both are of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task. (1) src-0007: on one expert-annotated corpus drawn from a real company's CTI workflow, the same four models reach IoC-extraction precision 0.8240-0.8846 while scoring 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o) and 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini) precision/recall on MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification, and GPT-4o scores 1.140 out of 5 on the threat-actor Attribution rubric against 3.612 out of 5 for root-cause content in the same table -- roughly a 3x spread across sub-tasks with everything else held constant.' BOTH OF ITS TWO src-0007 COMPARISONS ARE NOW KNOWN TO BE NON-COMMENSURABLE, EACH REFUTED BY A SUPPORTED CANDIDATE ELSEWHERE IN THIS GRAPH, AND ITS STATED METHODOLOGICAL WARRANT IS FALSE. CONFLICT 1 -- THE IoC-VERSUS-TTP SPREAD. ttp-attack-mapping-reliability's candidate 2 carries a cycle-31 addendum headed 'CLAIM (b) IS NOW WITHDRAWN' which withdraws THIS EXACT INFERENCE in this exact form: 'The argument was that because the identical models on the identical corpus through the identical harness reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. That inference silently assumed the two numbers were produced by comparable scoring. THEY ARE NOT.' The two rules are now BOTH known from executing code in one artefact (src-0017): the IoC side is ONE-DIRECTIONAL SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT, any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set) (ctr-0004, cycle 27), and the ATT&CK side is EXACT TECHNIQUE-ID SET INTERSECTION with no substring, parent, sub-technique or partial credit (ttp candidate 3, read cycle 31 and REPLICATED cycle 32 with ten verbatim string checks, plus the finding that TTP_Mapping.csv carries a 'sub-technique of' parent column WHICH THE LOADER DISCARDS, so a T1548.002 prediction against a T1548 ground truth is counted as a false positive AND a false negative simultaneously). THE DECISIVE POINT, AND IT IS NEW HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED: THE DIRECTION OF THE SCORING BIAS IS THE DIRECTION OF THE REPORTED FINDING. The leniently-scored task is the one that scores high and the strictly-scored task is the one that scores low. So the 3x spread this candidate presents as a sub-task difficulty fact is exactly what these two scoring rules would manufacture from equal underlying performance. The confound is no longer merely possible and unquantified; its SIGN is known and it aligns with the claim. CONFLICT 2 -- THE 1.140-VERSUS-3.612 RUBRIC CONTRAST. Per ctr-0008 (cycle 30, confirmed by two fetches of the paper's Appendix C.2 on two URL renderings and again at cycle 31 from the live sys_prompt string in eval/root_cause.py retrieved whole), the dimension named 'Attribution' IS DEFINED DIFFERENTLY IN THE TWO RUBRIC BLOCKS: in the Threat Actor block it measures SOURCE LINKING ('5: Fully attributable; all details are clearly linked to the original article'), and no anchor in that block mentions identifying a threat actor; in the Root Cause block it measures THREAT-ACTOR IDENTIFICATION ('5: Perfect attribution; accurately identifies the threat actor, their objectives, and the precise relationship to the incident's root cause'). 1.140 and 3.612 are two different constructs sharing one column name, and the labels run OPPOSITE to the way this candidate reads them. WHY THIS IS FILED AGAINST THIS ISSUE AND NOT LEFT TO ctr-0008. ctr-0008 flags this issue in passing as having 'the LARGEST SCORING EXPOSURE' but is filed against attribution-confident-wrong-gap, so per-issue queries over open contradictions do not surface it here, and it does not address conflict 1 at all. Conflict 1 is unfiled anywhere against this issue. THE FALSE WARRANT, WHICH IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE PART. The candidate's own justification for treating these as strong evidence is that they are 'of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task'. That is carry-forward [34] stated as a virtue and it is false: A WITHIN-STUDY DESIGN DOES NOT HOLD THE SCORING RULE CONSTANT, and both of this candidate's within-study comparisons are now demonstrated instances of the rule varying with the sub-task. There are now SEVEN documented non-commensurable instances in this base (src-0017/ctr-0004; src-0003's classification-over-a-regex-candidate-set; src-0005's all-or-nothing multi-select; src-0002/ctr-0006's Micro-versus-Macro-F1 with no stated ATT&CK correctness rule; src-0007's rubric against itself per ctr-0008; src-0007's IoC rule against its own ATT&CK rule; and src-0008's body text against its own Table 6 caption). EVERY TIME A CYCLE HAS ACTUALLY READ A SCORING RULE IN THIS BASE, IT HAS DIFFERED FROM WHAT THE STATE ASSUMED. That is now the base rate and it must be the prior. NEITHER SIDE IS SILENTLY PICKED, AND WHAT SURVIVES IS STATED SO THE REPAIR IS NOT OVER-READ AS A DEMOLITION. (a) src-0013's leg of this same candidate is untouched by anything here and is not in dispute. (b) The BLOCK-LEVEL rubric contrast survives conflict 2 and is broader than the sentence it would replace: GPT-4o scores 1.547 / 1.528 / 1.145 / 2.019 / 1.734 / 1.140 on Threat Actor content against 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.362 / 3.932 / 3.753 / 3.612 on Root Cause content, LOWER ON ALL SIX DIMENSIONS. But ctr-0008 records two limits on even that, and they apply here with full force: the two blocks' anchors are worded differently, so it remains a contrast between two differently-worded rubrics over two different sub-tasks, and the instrument is an LLM judge which the paper states is GPT-4o, one of the four models being scored. (c) The QUALITATIVE direction -- that measured CTI reliability is not one uniform property -- is NOT refuted by this entry and is separately carried by this issue's FIRST candidate via src-0006. THIS ENTRY DISPUTES THE WITHIN-STUDY COMPARISONS OFFERED AS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE, NOT THE ISSUE'S EXISTENCE. RESOLUTION PATH, FOR A T3 TARGETING THIS ISSUE. (i) Rewrite candidate 2 to drop the words 'varying only the sub-task' and to state the scoring-rule objection explicitly, replacing the IoC-versus-TTP sentence with the qualitative statement that the two figures are scored by different KINDS of matching whose bias runs in the direction of the observed gap, and replacing the 1.140-versus-3.612 sentence with the six-dimension block contrast plus its two limits. (ii) STATE AND ANSWER THE OBJECTION IN THE ISSUE TEXT, which is what cycle 22 asked for and no cycle has done -- an issue cannot be credited with addressing a counterargument it has not noticed. (iii) Pull src-0006's per-task scoring definitions, which no cycle has ever read: candidate 1 and route 1 of extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis BOTH rest on the assumption that its nine F1 rows share one matching rule, and given the base rate above that assumption is now the single largest untested load-bearing assumption in this project. If those rules turn out comparable, this issue's level-3 case is repairable and cycle 19's argument stands as written.

METRIC-DEFINITION CONFLICT INSIDE A SINGLE TABLE, opened by cycle 30's G2 re-verification of src-0007 (arXiv 2603.09452, CyberThreat-Eval, Microsoft Research / Microsoft / HKUST). Target chosen by staleness: the Table 4 rubric rows were a single unreplicated pull from cycle 15, and that gap is the stated reason this issue's THIRD candidate_resolution is still 'proposed'. THE NUMBERS PASS COMPLETELY AND MUST NOT BE RE-OPENED. A third independent pull of arxiv.org/html/2603.09452v1, instructed to transcribe Table 4 whole and to write CANNOT READ rather than infer, returned every one of its 34 data rows identical to the transcription stored in state/knowledge/src-0007.md, cell for cell -- including every rubric cell this issue cites: Content: Threat Actor GPT-4o 1.547 / 1.528 / 1.145 / 2.019 / 1.734 / 1.140 against o3-mini 3.964 / 3.656 / 3.165 / 4.753 / 4.731 / 2.968, and Content: Root Cause GPT-4o 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.362 / 3.932 / 3.753 / 3.612. The GPT-4o (FT) anomaly of carry-forward [19] is REPRODUCED A THIRD TIME (3.964 / 3.655 / 3.165 / 4.752 / 4.731 / 2.967, tracking o3-mini to within 0.001 on all six rubric rows) -- as-printed across three pulls at cycles 15, 21 and 30, cause still unknown, DO NOT GUESS. THE DEFECT IS IN OUR READING OF THE ROW, NOT IN THE ROW: this is methodological rule (vi), a clean source with an unclean state account of it, and it was caught by rule (iii), pulling the verbatim DEFINITION of the metric rather than only its value. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY DEFINES. Appendix C.2 prints SEPARATE criteria blocks for Threat Actor content and Root Cause content, and the dimension named 'Attribution' IS DEFINED DIFFERENTLY IN THE TWO BLOCKS. Verbatim, THREAT ACTOR block, all five anchors: 'Attribution: 1: Information is unverified or unattributed. 2: Major attribution issues; many details are not clearly linked. 3: Moderately attributable; some details lack clear source references. 4: Mostly attributable; minor gaps in linking information. 5: Fully attributable; all details are clearly linked to the original article.' Verbatim, ROOT CAUSE block, all five anchors: 'Attribution: 1: Completely incorrect attribution. 2: Significant attribution errors; misidentified threat actor. 3: Basic attribution; minor inaccuracies. 4: Mostly correct attribution. 5: Perfect attribution; clearly identifies the threat actor.' So in the Threat Actor block 'Attribution' measures SOURCE LINKING -- whether the generated text is traceable to the input article -- and NO anchor in that block mentions identifying a threat actor. In the Root Cause block 'Attribution' measures THREAT-ACTOR IDENTIFICATION and says so in three of its five anchors. Confirmed by two fetches on two URL renderings (arxiv.org/html/2603.09452v1 and arxiv.org/html/2603.09452), the second asked for both blocks whole with every numbered anchor and permitted to answer ABSENT or CANNOT READ. A one-sentence gloss from the first fetch, 'Attribution: Evaluates whether the generated context properly attributes information to the original article', is consistent with the fuller anchors. THE CLAIM IN CONFLICT, verbatim from this issue's third candidate_resolution: 'THE LOAD-BEARING PART IS THE WITHIN-TABLE CONTRAST, not the model gap: the same GPT-4o scores 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.612 on Content: Root Cause in the same table, so its 1.140 on threat-actor attribution is a deficit specific to attribution rather than a general inability to draft.' That contrast sets 1.140 against 3.612, and those two cells are NOT the same measurement. Worse, the labels run OPPOSITE to the way the state reads them: the cell the state treats as the threat-actor-attribution deficit (1.140) is the one whose rubric never mentions identifying an actor, while the cell used as the drafting CONTROL (3.612) is the one that does. NEITHER SIDE IS SILENTLY PICKED, and one side here is the paper's own appendix. WHAT SURVIVES, STATED SO THE REPAIR IS NOT OVER-READ AS A DEMOLITION. The BLOCK-LEVEL contrast is untouched and is in fact broader than the sentence it would replace: GPT-4o scores 1.547 / 1.528 / 1.145 / 2.019 / 1.734 / 1.140 on Threat Actor content against 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.362 / 3.932 / 3.753 / 3.612 on Root Cause content, i.e. LOWER ON ALL SIX DIMENSIONS, so 'a deficit specific to the threat-actor sub-task rather than a general inability to draft' remains supported -- by the whole block, not by the Attribution row. TWO LIMITS ON EVEN THAT: the two blocks' anchors are worded differently (the Root Cause anchors are incident- and malware-specific while the Threat Actor anchors reference 'the original article'), so it is a contrast between two differently-worded rubrics over two different sub-tasks, which is exactly the objection carry-forward [34] and ctr-0006 raise elsewhere; and this remains an LLM-judged construct, so it evidences WRONGNESS rather than CONFIDENCE and supplies nothing to this issue's titular 'confident' half, as cycles 26 and 28 both recorded. A SECOND FINDING FROM THE SAME PULL, NEVER RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS STATE IN TWENTY-ONE CYCLES: THE JUDGE IS GPT-4o, ONE OF THE FOUR MODELS BEING SCORED. Verbatim, Section 4.1: 'To evaluate narrative quality (threat actors and root causes), we employ the LLM-as-Judge paradigm' and 'This evaluation method provides the LLM judge with the ground-truth article, candidate output, and a scoring rubric covering relevance, factual accuracy, comprehensiveness, clarity, coherence, and attribution.' Plausible is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor; misjudgment/hallucination/spurious correlation is a SEPARATE third category. Also: the exact string 'plausible-sounding' does NOT occur in the paper, though the state presents it in scare quotes as if quoting; and no sentence in the paper interprets the correct-versus-plausible gap, so the interpretation is wholly ours. The 114 per-technique kappa values are each estimated from a 195-sentence sample, not from the 2,076-sentence corpus. src-0020 itself reports '2,028 technique occurrences' over 2,076 sentences, so a 10% sample carries on the order of 200 technique occurrences to be spread across 114 techniques -- of the order of TWO positive instances per technique on average. A per-technique Cohen's kappa estimated from that many positives is extremely imprecise, and the paper reports the mean WITH NO CONFIDENCE INTERVAL. The derived per-technique occurrence figure in this sentence IS A CYCLE-47 DERIVATION from two printed numbers and is labelled as such under rule (xii); the printed numbers are exact. LIMB 2 -- WHICH PHASE THE VALUE DESCRIBES. The paper's headline sentence reads 'Following the six-phase process, we reached a mean inter-annotator agreement of K=0.68 across 114 techniques (Landis and Koch: substantial agreement), with 65 techniques (57.0%) exceeding the K>=0.7 quality threshold' -- confirmed PRESENT as one whole sentence by the same exact-string ask, so the base's stored quotation of it is accurate. But the paragraph places the kappa computation at phase (ii), Initial Cross-Labeling, with phases (iii) relabelling, (iv) a re-check 'to verify K improvement', and (v) dispute resolution all coming AFTER it. 'FOLLOWING THE SIX-PHASE PROCESS, WE REACHED' AND 'COMPUTED AT PHASE (ii) OF SIX' CANNOT BOTH BE READ STRICTLY. This is a tension INSIDE THE SOURCE, not a state defect, and it is recorded here rather than asserted as an error: the paper does not state anywhere read so far that kappa was recomputed after phase (iv), and the 0.68 may be either the initial agreement or a final one. NOBODY MAY RESOLVE THIS TENSION BY PICKING THE READING THAT SUITS THEM. LIMB 3 -- WHAT SURVIVES, STATED NARROWLY SO THIS ENTRY IS NOT OVER-READ. Every numeral in src-0020 key_claims[1] re-verified exact, and every other stored quotation in src-0020 key_claims[0], [1] and [2] returned PRESENT under exact-string ask this cycle: the 0.22 micro-F1 sentence, the 2,076/114/2,028/211 dataset sentence (which the base stores COMPLETE, including the 'totaling 2,028 technique occurrences across 211 potential candidates' tail), the 211-technique parent-granularity sentence, and the DFIR Report generalisation caveat. src-0020 key_claims[2](a) also re-verified clean on 2026-08-01: arxiv.org/abs/2606.18166 still lists '[v1] Tue, 16 Jun 2026 17:04:15 UTC (25 KB)' as its only version and still carries NO 'Comments:' and NO 'Journal reference:' line, so the unreviewed-v1 limit stands and the version-staleness bolt-on is discharged for this source at cycle 47. DEFECT 1, ARITHMETIC, AND THIS IS THE STRONGER HALF. Precision (Accepted) is TP/(TP+FP). At precision 0.27-0.40 the quantity 0.60-0.73 is the share of the items the system ACCEPTS that the ground truth had rejected. The state converts it into the share of TRUE REJECTS that get passed through, i.e. FP/(FP+TN), and states that as fact in (b) and (d). These are different quantities and the second is NOT derivable from precision and recall alone -- it needs the class base rate, which src-0007 never reports. They are also demonstrably unequal here: with recall (Accepted) at 0.9091-1.0000 and precision about 0.30, FP is about 2.33 times TP, so the corpus must contain at least 2.33 true rejects per true accept; FP/(FP+TN) then equals 0.60-0.73 only if true rejects happen to outnumber true accepts by about 3.4 to 1, and equals 100% if the ratio is exactly 2.33 to 1. Nothing in the paper fixes that ratio. THE DEFENSIBLE RESTATEMENT is 'roughly 2 of every 3 items the system accepts are items the ground truth rejected'; the pass-through rate of true rejects is UNCOMPUTABLE from the published figures. This is the rule (xii) shape -- a derived number that no cycle audited against the log that derived it -- and the derivation is not merely unlogged but invalid.
